d.summary: This is a hand-built, analysis-by-synthesis recogniser. It renders crude 3D models of each class (planes, cars, trucks, ships, birds, frogs, cats, dogs, deer, horses) from many viewpoints, then matches the photo against them under several zooms, shifts and mirror flips. The matching uses edge-orientation layout, silhouette and material. It adds two more stored-reference comparisons, against synthetic composited scenes (colour and texture layout, and an object-plus-background-type map), and a large set of hand-weighted scene and part cues: sky, water, grass, road, wheels, legs, eyes and nose, straight edges. All of these are summed into one score per class.
d.references: Three families, all generated procedurally from hand-built 3D models with no photos involved. (1) Silhouette templates: 3D models built from ellipsoids, prisms and polygons (3 airplane shapes, 4 cars, 5 trucks, 5 ships, 4 birds, 3 frogs, 3 each of cat, dog, deer and horse in a standing pose plus a head-and-chest portrait pose). Each is rendered as a shaded grey depth-tested image at 64 px, from a grid of azimuths, elevations and in-plane tilts. That gives about 1,030 views (airplane 216, truck 120, bird 120, car 96, frog 90, cat and dog 99 each, deer and horse 66 each, ship 60). Each view stores: an 8x8 grid of 6-way edge-orientation strengths, computed from the silhouette shaded at both contrast polarities and averaged so it does not depend on object-versus-background brightness; an 8x8 interior shading pattern; an 8x8 occupancy mask; and a 16x16 shading pattern, a 16x16 occupancy mask and a 16x16 squared-occupancy weighting used to average a material score inside the silhouette. (2) Synthetic photos: 120 views per class, each composited onto 6 class-specific backdrop pairs (sky over sky, woods over road, wall over cloth, sky over sea, and so on). The backdrops are procedural noise textures in about 4 palette colours per backdrop type. The object is painted in class-typical colours, with dark windows and tyres for vehicles and fur grain or stripes or blotches for animals, then randomly zoomed, shifted, tilted, mirrored and relit, and shrunk to 32 px. That makes 720 per class, 7,200 in total, each stored as a colour, material, texture and edge-orientation layout summary. (3) Layout plans: 160 views per class times 6 backdrop pairs, 960 per class. Each is an 8x8 map over 14 roles: object body, one of 10 background types above or below a random horizon (for ships the horizon is set at the hull bottom), the shadow under vehicles, and dark parts such as windows and tyres for vehicles or bright parts for ships and planes.

stages.name: Figure-ground estimate
stages.computes: Smooths the image and converts it to a brightness plus two colour-opponent channels. For each pixel it finds the lowest possible 'largest colour step' along any path to the image border, so regions enclosed by a colour boundary score high. This is combined with how unlike the pixel is from colour patches sampled along the four borders, with a cost that rises with distance from the patch. Both terms are normalised by the image's own brightness contrast.

key_numbers.meaning: number of propagation steps for the barrier-to-border distance, enough to cross the 32 px image

key_numbers.value: 7 px patches every 5 px, 3 px deep
key_numbers.meaning: border colour palette sampled along each of the 4 edges
weight of the enclosure barrier versus colour rarity in the final object-likelihood map

stages.name: Edge and material maps
stages.computes: Measures edge strength in 6 soft orientation bins, from brightness plus the red-green and blue-green colour differences. Also builds per-class material likelihood maps: metal-like (grey, smooth, painted, not leafy or tan), fur-like (tan, coarse, not leafy), and frog-like (olive, leafy, coarse), each with class-specific brightness or darkness terms.

key_numbers.meaning: orientation bins over 180 degrees of edge direction
weight of the colour-difference edges relative to brightness edges

stages.name: Search over zoom, position and mirror
stages.computes: Resamples the edge maps, brightness, figure-ground map and material maps under 4 zoom levels times 7 offsets (centre, four diagonals, up, down) times a mirror flip, giving 56 placements. At each placement it builds an 8x8-cell edge-orientation descriptor, smoothed with neighbours and normalised by local and global edge energy, plus 8x8 and 16x16 brightness and figure-ground layouts with their means removed.

key_numbers.meaning: sampling step relative to the pixel grid: below 1 zooms into the centre, above 1 zooms out
shift sizes paired with each zoom; vertical shifts are scaled by 0.45 upward and 0.8 downward
score penalty for an off-centre placement and for the most zoomed-out placement

stages.name: Silhouette template matching
stages.computes: Correlates each placement's descriptor with every rendered template of a class. One score uses edge layout, interior shading and occupancy. A second, richer score adds 16x16 brightness and silhouette agreement and the average class-material likelihood inside the template's silhouette. For each class it keeps the best template per placement, then mixes the best placement with the mean of the top 6 placements and subtracts the class's average response over everything.

key_numbers.meaning: number of best placements averaged as supporting evidence
weight of the single best placement versus the top-6 average
how much of the class's mean response is subtracted, which penalises classes that match everything

stages.name: Scene-photo nearest neighbours
stages.computes: Summarises the whole photo as coarse 4x4-region histograms of 17 colour, material and texture properties (bright, dark, grey, green, sky blue, warm, red paint, vivid, rough, smooth, salient, horizontal and vertical line), averaged partly with their mirror image. It adds horizontal band averages, border-versus-centre averages, 4x4 edge-orientation shares and edge strength. It then compares this summary by distance with the 720 synthetic scene photos of each class and keeps the best match blended with the top 8.

key_numbers.meaning: spatial resolution of the layout summary
nearest synthetic scenes averaged per class
weight of the single nearest scene versus the top-8 average

stages.name: Object-and-background layout plans
stages.computes: Builds per-pixel soft log-likelihoods for 13 background types (sky, water, field, woods, earth, road, wall, cloth, plain backdrop, mountain, shadow, window, white enamel) from colour, brightness and smoothness, reduced where the pixel looks like foreground. It also builds a class-specific object-material likelihood that is boosted by the foreground map. The result is pooled to 8x8 and correlated against the 960 layout plans of each class, mixing the best plan with the top 12.

key_numbers.meaning: grid of 4 px cells for the layout comparison
top plans averaged per class
weight of the best plan versus the top-12 average

stages.name: Hand-written scene and part cues
stages.computes: Measures scene content in fixed regions (top band, side flanks, bottom band, centre blob): sky at the top, water at the bottom, greenery, soil, road-grey ground, a plain or studio backdrop, a two-tone top and bottom. It also measures how straight, rectilinear and horizontal the edges are, roughness and fine texture, and the extent and aspect ratio of a salient centre blob, found by its colour difference from the side strips.

key_numbers.meaning: soft extents of the ground band, top sky band and side flanks, in pixels
weighting used for the object-body measures
mean colour difference from the top-rows colour below which the surround counts as a uniform backdrop

stages.name: Part detectors
stages.computes: Wheels: pairs of dark blobs of radius 2 to 3 px with brighter surroundings, in rows 14 to 28, a fixed horizontal distance apart with a small vertical tilt allowed. Legs: pairs of thin dark vertical strokes in the lower half, 4 to 15 px apart. Eyes and nose: pairs of dark spots in the upper half, 4 to 13 px apart, with a darker ridge midway below them. Also measured: local edge coherence, giving straight lines versus curly fur, long horizontal lines (decks and hulls), diagonals (wings) and horizontal ripples low in the frame (water).

key_numbers.meaning: candidate spacings between two wheels
candidate spacings between two legs, measured in rows 16 to 30
candidate spacings between two eyes, in rows 6 to 18
how strongly one axis must dominate a coherent edge for it to count as horizontal or vertical

stages.name: Cue-based class evidence
stages.computes: Combines the cues into per-class hand-weighted sums, for example vehicle evidence as straight edges plus road plus wheels minus vegetation. Adds explicit scene hypotheses that each require several cues together (a geometric mean of the cues, then a soft maximum over alternative settings), such as a plane on a plain backdrop with diagonals, a ship with water low and sky high, a cat indoors with a face and blotches, or a horse on grass with legs. Also adds family-level scores shared by airplane and ship, car and truck, cat and dog, and deer and horse.

key_numbers.meaning: floor on each cue inside a conjunction, so one missing cue does not zero the hypothesis
weight of the best alternative setting versus the mean of all settings for a class
weight of the log scene-hypothesis score relative to the linear cue sums (0.6 each)

d.decision: The final class score is a weighted sum of the five evidence sources: 7.8 times the silhouette match (edge, shading and occupancy), plus 4.3 times the richer silhouette-and-material match, plus 0.74 times the hand-written cue score, plus 0.42 times the scene-photo nearest-neighbour score, plus 10.0 times the object-and-background layout-plan score. The class with the highest total is chosen.
d.adapts_per_image: Several things change from image to image. The figure-ground map comes from a path search to the border (the lowest colour barrier along any path) and is normalised by the image's own brightness contrast. Template matching searches 56 zoom, shift and mirror placements and keeps, per class, the best template at each placement, then the best placement plus the mean of the top 6. Every stored-reference comparison keeps a per-class best match plus a top-k average (k is 6, 8 or 12, chosen by sorting). Descriptors are normalised by edge energy and brightness variance measured on that image. The part detectors take maxima over positions and spacings. The backdrop and salient-blob cues compare pixels with colours sampled from that image's own top rows, side strips and borders. There is no iteration to convergence or branching beyond these maxima and top-k selections.

d.summary: The method compares each photo with roughly 15,000 stored views of hand-built 3D models of the ten object kinds, rendered from many angles, sizes, mirrorings and offsets. For each class it keeps a softened best match, measuring agreement on edge directions, on outline layout (against brightness, colour contrast and a map of where the photo differs from its own border colours) and on interior shading. It then adds two large sets of hand-set scene and part cues: sky, water, grass, foliage, road and soil colours by image region, straightness of lines, a dark band under the object, how large and central the foreground is, paired wheel-like rings, eye-and-nose arrangements, leg-like vertical strips and fur or skin texture. A weighted sum of these gives each class its score.
d.references: The references are about 14,900 grayscale renderings, each 48 by 48, of simple 3D models put together by hand from ellipsoids, sticks and flat panels with fixed grey shading levels under one fixed light. There are 3 airplanes, 4 cars, 3 birds, 6 cat poses plus a curled cat, 6 dog poses plus 3 dogs with face or coat markings, 3 deer bodies plus a deer head portrait, 3 horse bodies plus a horse head portrait, 2 frogs, 4 ships and 4 trucks. Each model is rendered at several turn angles (for example -38 to 88 degrees) and tilt angles (for example 3 to 77 degrees). Airplanes also get a bank of -23, 0 or +23 degrees. Each rendering is then placed at 3 or 4 scales (0.49 to 1.14), mirrored left to right, and shifted to 5 positions (centre plus about 8% offsets). Counts per class are about 4,320 airplane, 1,200 car, 720 bird, 1,890 cat, 960 deer, 2,160 dog, 540 frog, 960 horse, 960 ship and 1,200 truck. Three summaries are stored for each view. The first is edge-direction strength in 6 orientations on a 12 by 12 grid, computed with the silhouette placed on both a dark and a light backdrop. The second is the silhouette coverage on a 12 by 12 grid. The third is the interior shading on a 12 by 12 grid, measured relative to the mean inside the silhouette.

stages.name: Upsample and edge-direction map
stages.computes: The photo is enlarged to 48 by 48 and lightly blurred. At every pixel it measures how strongly a local edge runs in each of 6 orientations, on brightness and on two colour-opponent channels (red minus green, blue minus green). These strengths are averaged over a 12 by 12 grid of 4-pixel cells, compressed, centred and scaled to unit length.

key_numbers.meaning: edge orientations, spaced 30 degrees apart
how sharply each orientation channel is tuned, as a penalty on the perpendicular edge component
weight of the colour-opponent edges relative to the brightness edges
grid of 4 by 4 pixel cells on the enlarged 48 pixel image

stages.name: Foreground-from-border map
stages.computes: On the 12 by 12 cell grid, each cell's colour is compared with the colours of the border cells, giving more weight to border cells that are spatially closer, and more to closeness horizontally than vertically. Cells that look unlike any nearby border colour score high, so the map estimates where the object is.

key_numbers.meaning: colour-difference scale at which a cell counts as matching a border cell (squared luminance plus chroma difference, image values 0 to 1)
spatial falloff for horizontal and vertical cell distance when weighting border samples
weight of chroma differences relative to luminance difference

stages.name: Template matching
stages.computes: Every stored view is scored by a weighted sum of four agreements. The photo's edge-direction map is compared with the view's. The view's silhouette is compared with the photo's brightness layout, taking the strongest of brightness and the two colour-difference layouts and ignoring sign. The silhouette is also compared with the foreground-from-border map. Finally the photo's brightness layout is compared with the view's interior shading.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the edge-direction agreement
weight of the silhouette against brightness or colour contrast (strongest of the three, sign ignored)
weight of the silhouette against the foreground-from-border map
weight of the brightness layout against the stored shading

stages.name: Per-class best match
stages.computes: For each class, the method takes the best-matching stored view. It then lowers that score according to how far the class's other views fall below it, which works as a soft maximum that rewards several close matches over a single lucky one.

key_numbers.meaning: sharpness of the soft maximum over a class's views
how much the spread of the other views pulls the best score down

stages.name: Material and region colour cues (two parallel sets)
stages.computes: Each pixel gets a soft label for sky-blue, water, green leaves or grass, ochre soil, gray road, white, black, saturated paint or red, based on colour ratios normalised by brightness and, for sky and water, on smoothness. The labels are averaged over particular regions: the top rows (sky, leaves), the bottom rows (grass, water, road), the left and right edge columns (sky), and a centre region weighted toward the likely foreground (coat colour, green subject, paint, white, black).

key_numbers.value: top 8 or 9 rows / bottom 6 to 9 rows
key_numbers.meaning: bands used for sky-above, grass, water or road below, out of 32
approximate central subject window in the 32 pixel image
blue-channel brightness ramp for sky

stages.name: Layout and line cues
stages.computes: The method measures several layout and line cues. These are the share of horizontal versus vertical edges and how much edge energy forms long straight runs (man-made outlines). It looks for a coherent full-width horizontal colour change (horizon or waterline) and a dark band low in the frame (shadow or underbody). It compares texture inside the centre with texture at the border (isolation of the subject), and checks whether the top and bottom bands are uniform. It also measures how large and centred the foreground is and whether it forms a horizontal band.

key_numbers.meaning: where a dark band under the object is sought, compared with the bottom 4 rows
length over which edges must stay consistent to count as a straight line
colour spread range (0 to 1 scale) for deciding the top and bottom bands are flat

stages.name: Part detectors
stages.computes: It searches positions across the lower half (rows 14 to 28) for two ring-shaped dark-centred blobs of radius 2 to 4 pixels side by side, spaced 4 or 6 radii apart, as a wheel-pair cue. It searches the centre for two dark spots side by side with a dark spot below them, short drop for cats and long drop for dogs, as a face cue, and also for a dark nose with lighter cheeks and bridge as a muzzle cue. In the lower part it looks for pairs of thin vertical bright or dark strips spaced 6, 10 or 14 pixels apart, as a legs cue.

key_numbers.meaning: wheel radii searched
eye separation searched; nose drop equals or doubles it
spacing between leg strips
band searched for legs

stages.name: Texture cues
stages.computes: From the frequency content of the brightness image it measures fine-versus-medium and medium-versus-coarse detail, and how much of that detail lies off the horizontal and vertical axes. It also measures how consistently local edges point the same way in the centre (fur), fine grain, and blotchy dark-and-white patches (pied coat).

key_numbers.meaning: coarse, medium and fine frequency bands, in cycles per 32 pixels
cutoff for how far off-axis a frequency must be to count as non-grid texture

stages.name: Hand-set class evidence
stages.computes: Two fixed sets of signed weights combine the cues into a context score for each class, each cue measured against a neutral reference value. Examples are sky on both sides and flat borders for airplane, water below with a waterline for ship, road with a dark band and wheels for car, grass below with legs for horse and deer, green or ochre centre with grain for frog, and face pattern with white or dark coat for dog. A clipped man-made versus natural score is added to airplane, car, ship and truck and subtracted from the six animals.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the man-made versus natural shift
clip range of the man-made versus natural score

d.decision: Each class's final score is 0.87 times its best template-match score, plus 0.39 times the first context score, plus 1.27 times the second context score (materials, parts, texture and the man-made versus natural shift). The class with the highest total is chosen.
d.adapts_per_image: The method adapts to each image in several ways. For every class it searches all stored views (angles, scales, mirrorings, positions) and keeps a softened best match. The part detectors search positions, sizes and spacings and keep the strongest response (wheel pairs, eye-and-nose faces, muzzles, leg pairs). The horizon search keeps the strongest row. The edge-direction, brightness and colour layouts are normalised by their own mean and overall strength in this image, and colour cues are divided by this image's brightness. The foreground map is built from this image's own border colours and then weights where coat and paint colours are measured. Matching against the outline uses whichever of brightness or the two colour differences agrees most strongly. Nothing is iterated or sorted.

d.summary: The classifier matches the photo against a large library of hand-drawn class silhouettes. Each drawing is rendered at several sizes, aspect ratios, tilts, mirror flips, bright or dark object polarities and small shifts, and is compared on shading, edge direction, how its colour differs from its surroundings, and how well it covers a figure/ground map. The best match per drawing and per class becomes shape evidence. This is added to a hand-written scene judgement that combines colour, texture, straight lines, eye and wheel detectors, left-right symmetry and a coarse "what material is where" layout matched against stored scene sketches for each class.
d.references: 1) Hand-drawn vector sketches made of polygons, ellipses and thick strokes, 5 per class (50 in all): airplanes from above, side, front and at an angle; cars and trucks in side, front and three-quarter views with dark tyres, hubs and windows; ships with hull, sails or superstructure; birds perched or in flight; side, front and head views of cat, dog, deer and horse; frogs from the side and front. Each is drawn as a mid-grey object on an empty background and rendered 24 ways (3 sizes of about 13 to 35 px across, 2 aspect ratios of 0.82 and 1.12, 3 tilts of a few degrees, or 6 wider angles for airplanes, a mirror flip, and object brighter or darker than the background). Each rendering is then shifted to 9 positions (plus or minus 4 px). That gives 10,800 shading templates at 16x16, 10,800 four-direction edge templates at 15x15, and 5,400 filled outlines (object area minus a ring of nearby background). 2) A table of expected object-versus-surround colour for each class on 3 colour-opponent axes (for example frogs greener than their surroundings; airplanes and ships less blue than theirs). 3) 50 coarse scene sketches, 5 per class, written as "region: material" (for example airplane "sky all around, metal or white in centre, dark middle band"; ship "sky on top, water below"; deer "forest around, fawn colour in the centre"). 4) Small hand-built part templates: pairs of dark wheel blobs with car spacing (about 2.8 wheel radii) or truck spacing (about 4 radii) plus body bands; two dark eyes with a nose or mouth spot below for cat-like or dog-like faces; a haunch pattern; horizontal and vertical step-edge lines. Each is tried at about 72 positions, scales and tilts.

stages.name: Brightness and colour normalisation
stages.computes: Converts the photo to brightness as a weighted sum of red, green and blue, then rescales it to zero mean and unit spread for this image. Builds a 16x16 half-resolution brightness map and a 15x15 map of edge energy in 4 directions (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees), each direction also rescaled for this image.

key_numbers.meaning: red, green and blue weights for brightness
working grid, 2x2 image pixels per cell

stages.name: Template shading and edge matching
stages.computes: For each of the 10,800 rendered drawing variants, measures how closely the image's brightness pattern matches the template's shading (a mix of 60% fine detail with large-scale shading removed and 40% plain shading). Also measures how closely the image's edge directions match the template's outline edges. These are correlation-style scores against unit-strength templates.

key_numbers.meaning: relative weight of the shading match versus the edge-direction match
shifts tried for each rendering (+/-2 cells on the 16x16 grid)
rendered object widths (3 sizes per drawing)

stages.name: Colour inside each outline versus around it
stages.computes: On three colour-opponent axes (green versus red and blue, blue versus red and green, red versus green and blue), each mixing raw and image-normalised colour, measures mean colour inside each drawing's filled outline minus mean colour in a band around it. Then scores agreement with the class's expected object-versus-surround colour.

key_numbers.meaning: mix of raw colour difference to colour difference normalised for this image
strongest expectation: the frog object greener than its surroundings
airplane and ship expected to be less blue than their surroundings

stages.name: Figure/ground map from border background
stages.computes: Estimates the local background colour for each row from the far left and far right edge columns (smoothed over a few rows). Each pixel's foreground strength is its brightness and colour difference from the closer-matching side. Strength is capped and rescaled for this image, then correlated with every filled outline.

key_numbers.meaning: left and right border strips used as background samples (about 3 px from each edge)
cap on per-pixel foreground contrast
weight of the outline-coverage score relative to the other matches

stages.name: Best pose and best drawing per class
stages.computes: Adds shading, edge, colour and coverage scores for every variant. For each drawing it keeps the best variant over size, aspect, tilt, flip, polarity and shift. Per class it takes the best drawing and the average of the 5 drawings' bests.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the best drawing's score and of the 5-drawing average
variants searched per drawing

stages.name: Soft colour categories and texture features
stages.computes: Gives each 2x2 cell a soft membership in 13 named colours (blue, leaf green, olive, warm, tan, red, paint blue, bright, black, white, grey, muted, pink) using ramped thresholds on colour differences. Also measures long and short oriented edges, fine-grain texture (centre minus a blurred surround), and derived flat, textured and grainy flags.

key_numbers.meaning: example colour test: blue exceeds red by 0.145 on a 0-1 colour scale, softened over 0.18
size of the oriented edge and grain detectors on the full image

stages.name: Line, symmetry and part detectors
stages.computes: Searches for the strongest horizontal step edge across the image, in the lower half, and at the sides, and the strongest vertical one. Measures left-right mirror similarity around the best of 5 candidate centre columns. Searches positions, scales and tilts for paired dark wheel spots with a body above (car spacing versus truck spacing) and for two-eyes-plus-nose arrangements (cat-like versus dog-like spacing). Each detector keeps its best placement.

key_numbers.meaning: half-spacing of paired dark blobs for the tyre and running-leg detectors
eye half-spacing and nose drop for cat versus dog faces
wheel separation in wheel radii, car versus truck
caps on each part's response so one strong part cannot dominate

stages.name: Regional measurements and vote rules
stages.computes: Averages each feature over fixed regions (whole image, centre, rim, top third, bottom quarter, sides). About 50 hand-written rules ramp between a low and a high threshold, for example 'how much grass at the bottom' or 'wheel pair present'. Each rule casts weighted votes for or against every class, measured relative to a typical image. Votes are grouped into 6 families (colour, edge direction, texture and lines, faces and tyres, axles, combinations), and each family's total per class is clipped.

key_numbers.meaning: top and bottom regions as fractions of image height
maximum absolute vote each of the 6 families can give a class

stages.name: Material map and scene sketches
stages.computes: Labels each cell of a 6x6 grid with soft membership in 26 materials (sky, cloud, water, grass, wood, road, paint, metal, fur and so on), each a fuzzy AND of colour, brightness, grain and line tests. Groups them into 26 broader settings, each taking its best member, and compares the map with each class's 5 region:material scene sketches. The best sketch per class is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: coarse grid, about 5 px per cell
emphasis given to the surround, centre, middle band, bottom and top regions in a sketch
weight of the best scene-sketch agreement in the final score

d.decision: Each class's final score sums three parts. First, scene-vote evidence: 0.73 times the average for its group (vehicles: airplane, automobile, ship, truck; animals: bird, cat, deer, dog, frog, horse) plus 0.56 times its deviation from that group average. Second, shape-template evidence: 1.32 times the group average plus 1.73 times the deviation. Third, 4.2 times the best scene-sketch agreement. The highest total wins. Shape evidence weighs most for telling apart classes within a group, and scene evidence helps separate vehicles from animals.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes, heavily. Brightness, edge-direction maps, colour axes and the figure/ground map are each rescaled by this image's own mean and spread. Background colour is estimated from this image's left and right borders, and each pixel takes whichever side matches it better. For each drawing it searches 2160 variants (size, aspect, tilt, flip, polarity, 9 shifts), keeps the best, then keeps the best drawing per class. Line detectors keep the strongest line position and slope. The symmetry axis is the best of 5 columns. Wheel and face detectors keep the best of about 72 placements. Materials take the best member of each setting, and the best of 5 scene sketches is kept per class. Rule ramps and family caps clip intermediate values.

d.summary: The classifier adds up three kinds of evidence. The first matches the photo against several thousand procedurally drawn silhouettes of each class at many poses, comparing edge directions, light/dark layout and fine detail. The second compares the photo's coarse colour layout with rendered colour scenes for each class: a sky colour above a horizon, a ground colour below, and the drawn object painted in a typical body colour. The third is a hand-written set of about 54 scene and detail cues (sky, grass, water, road, texture, line direction, wheel/eye/nose detectors), combined by per-class weights, "all of these together" rules and short lists of typical scene descriptions. The class with the largest total wins.
d.references: 1) Silhouette drawings: each class has 3 to 5 hand-coded side or front views built from polygons, ellipses and rods. Examples are airplane side, top and front views, car side and front, cat/dog face, sitting and walking poses, deer/horse front and walking, frog top and side, a ship with sails or a hull, and box and articulated trucks. Each part is labelled body, darker part, black, light/window, and so on. Each class gets 5 view slots x 42 random poses (left/right mirroring, 3 sizes, small random stretch, offset up to about a quarter of the half-width, tilt up to about 8 degrees, or about 25 degrees for airplane/bird/frog, plus a large random rotation for the airplane top view). Each pose is shaded in 3 grey-level palettes, giving 6300 templates in all. For each template, three summaries are stored: a 7x7 map of edge strength in 4 directions, an 8x8 light/dark layout with an object mask, and a 16x16 high-pass detail map. 2) Rendered colour scenes: 10 classes x 6 settings (sky colour over ground colour, e.g. blue sky over sky, leaves over road, sky over water, room over wall) x 156 random poses, giving 9360 scenes. Each scene uses the same silhouette drawings, painted with a body colour drawn from a per-class list (e.g. bay/black/cream for horse, white/red/blue/silver/yellow for truck), with shading, a soft or sharp horizon at a random height, and brightness and tint jitter. Each is stored as an 8x8 colour layout. 3) Hand-written lookups: 15 named colour categories defined as colour-space boxes (blue, sky, white, pale, blue-grey, leaves, grass, earth, brown, gold, grey, dark, red, marsh, black). Fixed region masks cover the top band, bottom band, centre blob, surround, sides, lower body, top corners and middle strip. There are also wheel-pair, eye-pair and eye-plus-nose spot layouts (288, 108 and 108 placements) and 50 scene descriptions (5 per class).

stages.name: Edge direction map
stages.computes: Halves the image to 16x16, measures luminance gradient strength in 4 directions (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees), counting both contrast signs, and averages it over a 7x7 grid. The whole map is then standardised by its own mean and spread across all directions and positions.

key_numbers.meaning: working resolution for edges (2x2 pixel blocks of the 32x32 photo)
edge directions, 45 degrees apart
grid of cells over which edge strength is averaged (about 4 original pixels per cell)

stages.name: Silhouette template matching
stages.computes: Every one of the 6300 posed drawings is scored by the sum of three similarities. The first compares its edge direction map with the photo's. The second compares its 8x8 light/dark layout with the photo's standardised luminance, plus a bonus when the object area is warmer, or less green, than the background for certain classes. The third compares its high-pass detail pattern (image minus a blur, faded at the borders) with the photo's standardised 16x16 luminance.

key_numbers.meaning: posed drawings (10 classes x 5 views x 42 poses x 3 grey palettes)
the three drawing sizes for vehicles vs animals, as scale factors of a frame where the image spans -1 to 1 (larger means a bigger object)
weight of the light/dark layout match relative to the object-colour bonuses
fraction of the average over directions removed at each cell of the template edge map, so only the dominant direction counts

stages.name: Best pose per class
stages.computes: For each class and view, keeps the best-scoring pose and palette. It then takes the best view plus the average of the 5 view bests and scales the result to give the silhouette vote for that class.

key_numbers.meaning: pose x palette candidates searched per view
weight of the silhouette vote in the final score

stages.name: Rendered colour scene matching
stages.computes: Converts the 8x8 coarse colour photo into luminance and two colour-opponent axes. It scores each of the 9360 rendered scenes by negative weighted squared colour distance (centre-weighted, per-axis tolerance), keeps the best pose per setting and the best setting per class, and votes each class's best score minus a tenth of the sum across all classes.

key_numbers.meaning: tolerated spread of luminance, blue-versus-warm and green-versus-magenta differences, in 0 to 1 intensity units
centre weighting of the 8x8 cells (edges count about half as much as the middle)
weight of the colour scene vote in the final score

stages.name: Colour category maps
stages.computes: At each 16x16 location, scores membership in 15 named colours (sky blue, grass, earth, brown, grey, dark, red and so on). Each colour is a soft AND of threshold tests on colour differences and brightness. The maps are then averaged to 8x8.

key_numbers.meaning: named colour categories
typical threshold, in 0 to 1 intensity units, for a pixel to count as blue

stages.name: Texture and line measures
stages.computes: On the full image, at half resolution, measures horizontal-line, vertical-line and fine-grain (high-pass) energy, averaged to 7x7. These and the edge direction energies are summed within fixed regions to give amounts of detail, horizontal versus vertical dominance, and axis-aligned versus diagonal structure.

key_numbers.meaning: window, in original pixels, for the line and grain detectors
image bands used as 'sky' and 'base' regions

stages.name: Part detectors
stages.computes: On standardised 16x16 luminance, compares fixed spot-pair layouts and keeps the best placement of each: two wheel-like rings low in the frame with dark under-body and lighter body above, two eye spots in the upper half, and two eyes with a nose spot below.

key_numbers.meaning: wheel-pair placements (3 horizontal offsets x 4 heights x 4 spacings x 3 tilts x 2 radii)
eye-pair and eye-plus-nose placements each
heights searched for the wheel pair (lower half of the image)
heights searched for the eyes

stages.name: Scene cues
stages.computes: Forms 54 named cues from region-weighted colour fractions, mean colours, brightness differences, texture and part detector responses. Examples are open sky at top, blue floor, foliage around, grass floor, warm subject, grey road, dark chassis, shadow line, hull line, legs, eye pair, dog nose and muzzle. Each is mapped to 0 to 1 with a ramp between a low and a high threshold.

key_numbers.meaning: number of scene and detail cues
ramp for 'open sky': fraction of the top region that is sky-coloured

stages.name: Cue voting
stages.computes: Each class gets a weighted sum of cues, each measured against a typical baseline. Each class also has 3 or 4 'all together' rules: the average of 2 or 3 cues, some negated, must exceed a level, and the rule then adds or subtracts a fixed strength. These two parts are summed and soft-limited. Separately, 5 scene descriptions per class (three supporting cues minus 0.26 times two contradicting cues) contribute their best plus their average.

key_numbers.meaning: level the cue average must exceed for an 'all together' rule to fire
limit on the per-class cue vote after scaling by 0.43
weight of the scene description match
overall weight of all cue-based evidence in the final score

d.decision: The final score for each class is: silhouette vote (best plus average view match, x2.1) + colour scene vote (best rendered scene, x3.1, minus a tenth of all classes' sum) + 0.75 x (soft-limited cue vote + scene description match). The highest score wins.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes. The method searches over 126 poses and palettes for each of the 50 class views and keeps the best. It also searches 156 poses in each of 60 class settings and keeps the best, and searches 288/108/108 placements for the wheel, eye and nose detectors and keeps the best. Five scene descriptions per class are compared and the best is kept. The edge map, the luminance maps and the three coarse colour channels are each standardised by that image's own mean and spread. Ramps, rule thresholds and the soft limit then act differently depending on the image's cue values.

d.summary: The method classifies mainly by comparing the photo with a large set of hand-drawn class silhouettes rendered at many positions, sizes, tilts and stretches. For each class and view it compares edge-direction layout, local brightness pattern, a figure/ground map and the contrast between silhouette interior and rim, and averages the few best-fitting poses. It adds a scene score (sky, water, road, grass, woods, indoor and so on, weighted by how often each class occurs in each scene) and many hand-tuned cue detectors: paired wheels, eyes and a nose, legs, long straight edges, cargo panels, windshield stripes, water ripples, an empty sky around the object, fur texture and object elongation. The class with the highest combined score wins.
d.references: Procedurally drawn flat silhouettes of each class, made from polygons, ellipses and stroked limbs with a few tones (body, mid-tone part, dark shadow such as wheels and eyes, window glass). Each class has 3 view types (cat and dog have 4): for example airplane side, three-quarter and head-on views; car side, three-quarter and front; truck side cab plus box, angled and front; ship hull with cabin, sailboat, and a bow view; bird perched, wings spread and front-on; four-legged side views for deer, horse, cat and dog (antlers, mane and tail differ), standing front views; cat and dog face-on heads at several sizes; frog in three poses. Each view is rendered at 72 quasi-random poses (offset up to about 3 px, size 0.51 to 1.26 of the frame, separate width and height stretch, tilt, shear, light-on-dark or dark-on-light), plus a left-right mirror of each, so 144 per view and 4,608 drawings in all. Each drawing is drawn at double resolution and averaged down to 32 x 32. From each drawing the method stores an edge-orientation description, a local brightness-contrast pattern, a 16 x 16 silhouette mask, and an interior-minus-rim region pattern. There is also a fixed 10 class x 9 scene table of hand-set percentages giving how often each class appears in each scene type.

stages.name: Brightness and edges
stages.computes: Converts the photo to brightness and measures horizontal and vertical brightness change at each pixel, plus the edge strength.

key_numbers.meaning: red, green and blue shares of brightness

stages.name: Figure/ground map
stages.computes: Takes 12 small patches spread around the image border as background samples. Each pixel's colour (smoothed brightness plus red-green and blue-green contrasts) is compared with every sample. The closest match, and a variant penalised by vertical distance from the sample's row, are turned into a soft 0 to 1 score for how unlike the background the pixel is.

key_numbers.meaning: background colour samples at rows 2, 10, 20 and 29 near the edges, 3x3 px each
colour-distance scales for the two soft foreground scores
penalty for matching a border sample from a different height (allows sky above, ground below)

stages.name: Image description for matching
stages.computes: Splits the image into an 8 x 8 grid of 4 px cells and records how much edge runs in each of 6 directions per cell, normalised by local and overall edge strength, then removes the per-direction average. Also records a 16 x 16 map of brightness minus its 5-cell local average.

key_numbers.meaning: edge-orientation bins
how closely an edge must align with a direction to count for it
relative weight of edge layout versus brightness pattern

stages.name: Comparison with drawings
stages.computes: For every stored drawing it scores the similarity of edge layout and brightness pattern, adds similarity between the image's foreground map and the drawing's silhouette, and adds how strongly the image differs between the silhouette interior and a thin rim just outside it, in brightness and two colour contrasts, with either sign allowed.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of silhouette/foreground agreement
weight and cap of the interior-versus-rim contrast
weights of red-green and green-blue planes relative to brightness in the rim contrast

stages.name: Best poses per view and class
stages.computes: For each class and view, averages the 5 best-matching poses out of 144. Across views it takes 83% of the best view plus 17% of the second best. The class scores are then centred across classes.

key_numbers.meaning: top poses averaged per view
blend of best and second-best view
weight of the drawing match in the final score

stages.name: Scene hypotheses
stages.computes: Measures colour classes (vegetation, blue, warm, gray, pale, black) and edge calm in the top band, bottom band and side bands. It combines them into 9 scene scores: air, sea, street, field, woods, understory, indoor, garden and plain backdrop. Each class's scene score is a log of the scene evidence weighted by that class's scene percentages.

key_numbers.value: top 7 rows, bottom 6 rows, 5 px side columns
key_numbers.meaning: border bands used to describe the scene
weight of the scene score

key_numbers.value: e.g. 89% sea for ship, 67% air for airplane
key_numbers.meaning: hand-set class-in-scene percentages

stages.name: Part detectors
stages.computes: Wheels: dark round blobs with a lighter hub, found as pairs 8 to 20 px apart on roughly one level in the lower image. Faces: two dark spots side by side with a dark spot below, with left-right brightness balance (a dog version looks for a lower, longer nose). Legs: narrow upright bars in the lower half. Also long horizontal and vertical straight edges, tall vertical edges (box sides), and a strong horizontal line low in the image (hull).

key_numbers.meaning: band searched for wheel pairs
wheel spacings tried

key_numbers.value: eye spacing 2 to 6 px; rows 6 to 22
key_numbers.meaning: face search window
band searched for legs

stages.name: Object shape and appearance cues
stages.computes: From the foreground map, finds the centroid and the horizontal and vertical spread of the object to judge elongation, compactness and how much of the frame it fills. Also measures centre colours (warm, leaf green, chestnut, saturated, blue, red paint, gray, white, black), fine texture, overall contrast, a bright band over a dark band (shadow under a vehicle) and gloss.

key_numbers.meaning: central region for object colour and texture
foreground level below which a pixel is ignored for shape spread
onset of the 'elongated' cue

stages.name: Finer cues
stages.computes: Detects: rectangles framed by strong edges around a flat interior (cargo panels); paint or bright metal above a dark band (car flank); best left-right mirror symmetry about several central columns; a broad dark nose patch; fur-like disordered edges versus aligned edges; centre colour matching the surround (camouflage); a sharp centre against a smooth surround; horizontal ripples in the bottom rows; a dark horizontal stripe across the upper middle (windshield); and an object alone in a uniform, quiet surround.

key_numbers.value: symmetry axes at columns 12 to 20, 9 px each side
key_numbers.meaning: mirror symmetry search
panel sizes tested
band checked for water ripples
darkness limit for the nose patch

stages.name: Hand-tuned class evidence
stages.computes: Adds fixed weighted sums of the cues to each class: shared 'machine', 'pet' and 'wild animal' terms plus class-specific terms, for example wheels and flank for car, panels, box edges and vertical edges for truck, hull, ripples and water for ship, empty sky and elongation for airplane, compactness and focus for bird, legs and chestnut colour for horse, face, symmetry and fur for cat, nose and symmetry for dog, matching green surround for deer, and centre green, dark soil and roughness for frog.

key_numbers.meaning: strongest single cue weight for horse
airplane bonus for an object isolated in quiet sky
frog bonus for green at the centre

d.decision: Each class's score is 12.5 times its centred drawing-match score, plus 1.05 times its scene score, plus all the hand-tuned cue terms. The class with the highest total is chosen.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes, in several ways. The drawing match searches 144 poses per view (position, size, stretch, tilt, shear, mirror, light or dark polarity), keeps the 5 best, then keeps the best and second-best view per class. Each part detector searches over positions and spacings and keeps the strongest responses: wheel pairs over gap and slope, eye spacing, mirror axis, rectangle size, nose size. Background colours are sampled from that image's own border. Edge measures are normalised by that image's overall edge strength, and the brightness and colour planes for rim contrast by that image's spread. The object's centroid and spread are measured on that image. The border colour range uses that image's quartiles.

d.summary: The method builds every class score by hand from two kinds of evidence. The main kind compares the photo with 9,600 synthetic drawings: 960 rendered silhouettes per class, each at a random size, tilt, offset and mirroring. For each class it keeps the best-matching drawing and also the typical best match across subsets of the drawings. On top of that it adds a large set of hand-tuned soft rules about scene colour, layout, texture and particular parts (a wheel pair on a road, eyes and nose of a cat or dog face, a pair of legs under a torso, a waterline). It also adds scene-palette hypotheses for each class: sky, subject and ground colours stacked top to bottom. All of these are summed, and the class with the highest total wins.
d.references:
There are six families of stored references, all generated by fixed code with no learning from photos:

(1) 9,600 class drawings, 960 per class. Each is a filled silhouette built from ellipses, polygons and thick lines with grey tone levels. Each class has 4 to 10 hand-drawn poses: side, front and three-quarter views of cars and trucks, plane silhouettes, boats, faces and bodies of cats and dogs, birds, frogs, deer and horses. Each drawing gets a random size (about 10 to 23 px), aspect, tilt (up to roughly 80 degrees for some plane poses, about 9 to 15 degrees for the others), offset up to 3.8 px and possible mirroring. Each drawing is stored as three summaries: an 8x8 map of edge direction energy in 4 directions, a 16x16 light/dark layout where the figure is randomly lighter or darker than the background, and a 16x16 colour-contrast layout of figure against surround. In two out of three drawings the colour-contrast layout uses a fixed hue for the class; in the rest the hue is random.

(2) 288 wheel-pair templates: two dark rings with light hubs, light road below and body above, at 4 heights, 3 centres, 4 spacings, 3 slants and 2 sizes.

(3) 2 x 128 face templates, one set with cat proportions and one with dog proportions. Each is two dark eye spots plus a nose spot, at 4 heights, 4 centres, 4 spacings and 2 tilts.

(4) 768 randomly generated templates of two legs under a torso with a dark gap between the legs.

(5) 180 randomly placed near-horizontal light-over-dark (or dark-over-light) boundary strips, for waterlines.

(6) A table of 35 named reference colours (sky, sea, foliage, sand, fur, metal and so on), grouped into 24 four-colour material palettes. These are used in 80 scene hypotheses, 8 per class, each a top/middle/bottom triple of materials (for example sky, then freight, then water for ships).

There are also 18 hand-defined colour categories, given as ranges of channel differences and brightness (blue, sky, leaf, olive, brown, tan, rust, white, neutral, ink, green and others).

stages.name: Brightness normalisation
stages.computes: Converts the photo to brightness. Subtracts this image's mean brightness and divides by its spread, so the comparisons that follow do not depend on exposure or contrast. Also makes a half-resolution 16x16 brightness map.

key_numbers.meaning: red/green/blue weights used for brightness
grid of 2x2-pixel blocks used for the tone layout

stages.name: Edge direction map
stages.computes: Measures local brightness change in 4 directions (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees), ignoring whether the change is light to dark or dark to light. Each direction then keeps only the part above 70% of the average across all four directions, so the map shows which direction dominates at each spot. The result is smoothed, sampled into an 8x8 grid (2x2 samples every 4 px) and rescaled for each direction using this image's own mean and spread.

key_numbers.meaning: fraction of the average across directions taken away so one direction dominates
sampling step of the 8x8 edge-direction grid

stages.name: Colour-contrast layout
stages.computes: Computes two colour-opponent signals per pixel: yellow against blue (0.55R+0.45G-B) and green against red (-0.9R+G-0.1B). Rescales each by this image's mean and spread and averages into 16x16 blocks.

key_numbers.meaning: overall scale on the opponent signals

stages.name: Drawing comparison
stages.computes: Scores the photo against each of the 9,600 class drawings. The score is the sum of three agreements: edge-direction map, light/dark layout and colour-contrast layout, weighted about 0.58, 0.37 and 0.15. For each class it keeps the best drawing score and the mean of the best scores within 8 subsets of 120 drawings.

key_numbers.meaning: drawings per class
weight on the best drawing match per class
weight on the average of the 8 subset bests

stages.name: Colour category maps
stages.computes: Gives every 2x2 block a soft membership in each of 18 named colour categories. Each category is a soft AND of ramps on channel differences (for example blue minus red) and on brightness. The memberships are then averaged over 8 image regions: whole frame, top, bottom, a centre blob, border rim, sides, very top and very bottom.

key_numbers.meaning: named colour categories
region cutoffs in a frame running from -1 to 1: top/bottom beyond 0.43, rim beyond 0.68 horizontally or 0.71 vertically

stages.name: Texture, line and brightness-layout measures
stages.computes: Measures several region-averaged properties: amount of fine edges, capped at 0.95 per spot so a few strong edges do not dominate; vertical and horizontal edge amounts; long straight lines (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) from elongated 9x9 detectors, capped at 1.65; brightness per region and in three horizontal bands (under, belt, roof); left-right brightness asymmetry about 3 candidate mirror axes. It also measures fine and medium bar and blob texture (oriented bars and spots at two scales) and how often bar texture breaks or changes between neighbouring spots.

key_numbers.meaning: cap on edge strength at each pixel for texture
cap on long-line strength
heights of the under/belt/roof brightness bands, frame from -1 (top) to 1 (bottom)
candidate vertical mirror axes in 16-column units

stages.name: Part detectors with placement search
stages.computes: Tries every stored placement and keeps the best response for each detector. The detectors are: a wheel pair with road contact (288 placements); a cat face and a dog face as eye-eye-nose triplets of dark spots in lighter surrounds (128 placements each, where a placement scores as its weakest of the three parts); two legs under a torso (768); a horizontal waterline (180). Separately, it measures colour differences between top and bottom, between centre and rim, and how much the colour varies around the border.

key_numbers.meaning: wheel-pair placements searched
face placements searched per species
leg-pair placements searched
waterline placements, each in 2 polarities

stages.name: Reference colour palette fit
stages.computes: Averages the image into 8x8 blocks of 4x4 pixels. For each block it computes a weighted absolute colour distance to each of 35 reference colours, using brightness, red-green and yellow-blue. For each of 24 four-colour materials it keeps the closest member colour, then averages that closeness over the top, middle, bottom and rim regions.

key_numbers.meaning: reference colours
weights on brightness, red-green and yellow-blue differences in the colour distance
four-colour material palettes

stages.name: Soft scene rules
stages.computes: Turns 41 hand-written measures into clipped 0-to-1 ramps between a low and a high threshold. Examples: blue around the border, sky above, water below, green background, grey road, paired cat eyes, wheels with road contact, a rough background. Each ramp casts hand-set votes for or against every class, scaled by 0.26. Another 23 cue ramps cast no direct votes and are used only in the scene combinations.

key_numbers.meaning: overall weight on direct rule votes
example ramp: the blue-border fraction that takes 'extensive blue background' from 0 to fully on

stages.name: Per-class scene combinations
stages.computes: Each class has 6 hand-written scene descriptions, each the average of 3 or 4 rule ramps (for a ship: blue water below, vertical layering and a level waterline). Each class gets its best description plus the mean of its 6.

key_numbers.meaning: alternative scene descriptions per class
weight on the best description
weight on the mean of the 6

stages.name: Per-class palette hypotheses
stages.computes: Each class has 8 hypotheses of materials from top to bottom (for example sky, freight, water for a ship). A hypothesis scores 0.3 times the top fit, 0.43 times the middle fit and 0.27 times the bottom fit. Each class gets its best hypothesis plus the mean of its 8.

key_numbers.meaning: palette hypotheses per class
weight on the best palette hypothesis
weight on the mean of the 8

stages.name: Texture votes
stages.computes: Seven ramps on texture contrasts, such as fine bars against medium bars in the centre, fine spots, broken bar texture, and fine texture at the bottom against the top. Each votes for or against classes; frog and cat are favoured by fine broken texture, vehicles and ships by medium bars.

key_numbers.meaning: overall weight on texture votes

d.decision: Each class score is the sum of five parts: drawing-match evidence (best plus subset average), direct rule votes, best and mean scene description, best and mean palette hypothesis, and texture votes. The class with the highest total is the prediction. There is no rejection option.
d.adapts_per_image: Brightness, the colour-opponent signals and the edge-direction map are each rescaled by their own mean and spread in this image. For each class the drawing comparison keeps the best of 960 drawings and the best within each of 8 subsets. The part detectors search over stored placements and keep the best: wheel pairs (288), cat and dog faces (128 each, a placement scoring as its weakest part), legs (768) and waterlines (360 counting both polarities). The palette fit keeps the closest of 4 colours in each material at each block. The scene stages keep the best of 6 descriptions and the best of 8 palette hypotheses per class. Edge and line strengths are capped at each pixel. There is no iteration or branching beyond these max selections.

clusters.approach: Hand-built synthetic silhouette or render template matching (edge orientation, light/dark layout, figure-ground, best pose per class) summed with hand-weighted scene colour, texture and part-detector cues (wheels, eyes and nose, legs, sky, water, grass). The highest additive class score wins. Some members add stored synthetic scene references (A, C, D, F).

pairs.shared: Rendered 3D primitive models from many viewpoints, 6-orientation edge templates at both polarities, occupancy and shading, a border-based figure-ground map, a soft best per class, hand-weighted region colour cues and wheel, leg and face detectors, and a weighted sum.
pairs.differs: A searches 56 image placements and adds a synthetic-photo nearest-neighbour stage, an object-background layout-plan stage and conjunctive scene hypotheses. B pre-shifts its templates and has no stored scene references.

pairs.shared: Synthetic silhouette templates matched on edges, shading and figure-ground coverage with best-per-class pooling, plus hand-set scene and part cues and stored per-class scene references (A's layout plans, C's region:material sketches).
pairs.differs: C uses 2D vector drawings, 4-direction edges and an inside-versus-surround colour expectation, and its votes are clipped by family with group-average and deviation weighting. A uses 3D renders, a placement search, material likelihoods and nearest neighbours over synthetic photos.

pairs.shared: Silhouette matching plus rendered colour scenes: objects painted in class colours over procedural sky/ground backdrop pairs and compared by coarse layout. Both also have hand-weighted cues, conjunctive scene rules and a weighted sum.
pairs.differs: D uses 2D drawings with 4-direction edges and a high-pass detail map, and adds per-class scene descriptions. A uses 3D renders with a zoom and shift search, a material score and a separate 14-role layout-plan stage.

pairs.shared: An 8x8 grid of 6-direction edge cells normalised by local and global energy, a figure-ground map from border colour patches, silhouette agreement, top-k pose averaging, hand-tuned scene and part cues, and a summed score.
pairs.differs: E uses 2D drawings, an interior-minus-rim contrast and a class-in-scene percentage table. A uses 3D renders and has synthetic-photo nearest neighbours and layout plans.

pairs.shared: Synthetic silhouette matching with best and mean pooling, hand-written scene and part cues, stored per-class scene hypotheses over top, middle and bottom regions, and summed evidence.
pairs.differs: F uses 2D drawings with 4-direction edges and a colour-contrast layout, part templates searched over placements, palette hypotheses and texture votes. A uses 3D renders, nearest neighbours over synthetic photos and 14-role layout plans.

pairs.shared: Template matching on edges, shading and a figure-ground map derived from border colours, a best match per class, region colour cues, wheel and face detectors and texture cues, combined in hand-set sums.
pairs.differs: B uses 3D renders with 6 edge orientations and a soft max. C uses 2D drawings with 4 edge directions, inside-versus-surround colour, scene-sketch matching and group-deviation weighting.

pairs.shared: A template library matched on edge directions and light/dark layout with the best per class, plus region colour cues, wheel and eye-nose detectors and hand-weighted per-class cue sums.
pairs.differs: D adds a rendered colour-scene matching stage and scene descriptions and uses 2D drawings with 4 directions. B uses 3D renders, 6 orientations, a border foreground map and a soft max.

pairs.shared: 6-orientation edge templates, a figure-ground map from border colour similarity compared with silhouettes, interior shading or contrast, soft or top-k pooling per class, and very similar hand-tuned cue sets (wheels, face, legs, straight lines, dark band, sky and water).
pairs.differs: B uses 3D renders, while E uses 2D drawings, an interior-versus-rim contrast and a class-in-scene table.

pairs.shared: Silhouette matching on edges and light/dark layout with the best per class, plus hand-set colour, texture and part cues combined additively.
pairs.differs: F has placement-searched part templates, scene descriptions and palette hypotheses, and uses 2D drawings with 4 directions. B uses 3D renders, 6 orientations and a border foreground map.

pairs.shared: 2D hand-drawn silhouettes with 4-direction edges and 16x16 shading or detail, a best per view plus the average of 5 views per class, soft-AND colour categories, ramped cue votes measured against a typical baseline, 5 scene descriptions per class and wheel and eye detectors.
pairs.differs: D adds rendered colour-scene matching. C adds an inside-versus-surround colour expectation, a figure-ground coverage term, clipped vote families and a 26-material map.

pairs.shared: 2D drawn silhouettes over many poses and polarities matched on edges, brightness and figure-ground coverage, interior-versus-surround contrast, best and top pooling, and hand-written cue votes with part detectors.
pairs.differs: C has region:material scene sketches, group-deviation weighting and 4 directions. E has 6 directions and a class-in-scene percentage table.

pairs.shared: 2D drawings with 4-direction edges and a 16x16 light/dark layout, colour-contrast matching, best plus averaged pooling, soft-AND colour categories, ramped rule votes, face and wheel detectors searched over placements, symmetry, and per-class region-material scene hypotheses.
pairs.differs: F uses palette hypotheses from reference colours, subset-best pooling and texture votes. C uses a figure-ground map, clipped vote families and group-deviation weighting.

pairs.shared: 2D drawn silhouettes at many poses matched on edges and brightness layout, best per view pooled across views, region colour cues, wheel, eye and nose detectors and hand-weighted per-class cues, summed.
pairs.differs: D adds rendered colour scenes and scene descriptions and uses 4 directions. E uses 6 directions, a figure-ground map, a rim contrast and a scene percentage table.

pairs.shared: Nearly the same pipeline: 2D drawings with 4-direction edge maps sharpened by subtracting part of the mean across directions, a 16x16 light/dark layout, best plus average pooling, soft-AND named colour categories over fixed regions, a wheel-pair template with 288 placements and eye-nose templates, ramped cue votes, per-class scene descriptions (best plus mean), and colour scene or palette hypotheses over top and bottom regions.
pairs.differs: D matches rendered colour scenes, while F fits reference palettes by top, middle and bottom region. F adds leg and waterline templates and texture votes.

pairs.shared: 2D drawn silhouettes with random poses and polarity matched on edges and brightness layout, top or subset pooling, part detectors (wheels, faces, legs, lines, symmetry), and hand-tuned per-class cue sums.
pairs.differs: E uses 6 directions, a figure-ground map, a rim contrast and a scene percentage table. F uses 4 directions, a colour-contrast layout, palette hypotheses and scene descriptions.

steps.step: Convert photo to brightness (and colour-opponent channels) and normalise by this image's own statistics
steps.note: Generic preprocessing. The programs also feed red-green and blue-green channels into edges. The networks use brightness only for edges and keep colour for separate stages.

steps.step: Oriented edge-energy map pooled on a coarse grid (6 orientations, brightness plus colour-opponent edges)
steps.note: All the networks use 4 directions at 45 degrees on brightness only (N1 15x15, N2 7x7, N3 8x8). Every program uses 6 bins at 30 degrees, and P1 and P2 add colour-difference edges. Same idea, coarser and narrower computation.

steps.step: Figure/ground map from dissimilarity to colours sampled at the image border
steps.note: N1 takes background colour per row from the left and right border columns only, a fixed stand-in for P3's 12 border patches with a row penalty and P2's distance-weighted border cells. N1 does not compute P1's minimum-barrier path search. N2 and N3 build no foreground map.

steps.step: Library of procedurally drawn class silhouettes rendered over many poses (size, tilt, stretch, shift, mirror, polarity)
steps.note: The networks use flat 2D vector drawings, as P3 does. P1 and P2 render 3D models from azimuth and elevation grids, so the network libraries match P3 in kind but not P1 or P2.

steps.step: Template score: edge-orientation layout agreement
steps.note: A correlation of the photo's edge map with each template's edge map, though with 4 directions rather than 6.

steps.step: Template score: brightness or shading layout agreement (local-contrast or interior shading)
steps.note: N1 mixes high-passed and plain shading, which resembles P3's brightness minus local average. N2 uses an 8x8 light/dark layout plus a 16x16 high-pass map. N3 uses a 16x16 light/dark layout.

steps.step: Template score: silhouette mask agreement with the foreground map
steps.note: Only N1 correlates its filled outlines with a figure/ground map, at weight 0.22 against P3's 0.21.

steps.step: Template score: colour/material contrast between silhouette interior and its surround
steps.note: P3 measures interior-minus-rim contrast with either sign allowed. P1 averages a class material likelihood inside the silhouette. P2 takes the strongest of the brightness and colour layouts against the silhouette, sign ignored. The networks instead score agreement with a fixed, signed class-expected object-vs-surround colour: N1's colour table, N2's warmer/less-green bonus, N3's fixed class hue in 2 of 3 drawings.

steps.step: Per-class pooling of template scores (best plus top-k, soft max, or best and second view)
steps.note: N1 takes the best variant per drawing, then 7x the best drawing plus 2.5x the 5-drawing mean. N2 takes the best pose per view, then the best view plus the mean of the 5 view bests. N3 takes the best of 960 plus the mean of 8 random-subset bests. Each is a best-plus-average pool but not P1's top-6 placements, P2's spread-penalised soft max or P3's top-5 poses with an 83/17 view blend.

steps.step: Subtract a class's mean response or centre template scores across classes
steps.note: N1 splits shape evidence into a vehicle/animal group average plus the deviation from it, a partial centring. N2 subtracts a tenth of the class sum only for the colour-scene vote, not for silhouettes.

steps.step: Nearest-neighbour match against synthetic colour scenes (object painted in class colours composited on class-specific backdrop pairs)
steps.note: N2's 10 classes x 6 sky-over-ground settings x 156 poses, with class body-colour lists and a soft horizon, closely mirror P1 reference family 2. N2 matches on an 8x8 colour layout only, without P1's texture and edge histograms, and keeps the best match rather than the best blended with the top 8.

steps.step: Object-plus-background layout plans: per-cell material/background likelihood map correlated with stored per-class layouts
steps.note: N1's 6x6 map over 26 materials, compared with 5 hand-written region:material sketches per class, is a fixed stand-in for P1's 960 generated 14-role plans per class. N3's top/middle/bottom palette hypotheses (8 per class) are a cruder stand-in. N2's 5 cue-based scene descriptions per class are only loosely similar.

steps.step: Soft per-pixel colour/material category labels (sky, water, grass, road, earth, white, black, paint)
steps.note: These are soft ANDs of thresholds on channel differences and brightness: N1 13 colours plus 26 materials, N2 15, N3 18 plus 35 reference colours.

steps.step: Region-band scene cues (sky in top band, water/grass/road in bottom band, side flanks, centre subject colour)
steps.note: All average category maps over fixed regions. The bands are similar in kind but differ in exact extent.

steps.step: Scene hypotheses combining several cues per class (conjunctions or a class-by-scene table)
steps.note: P1 uses a floored geometric mean with a soft max over settings. P3 uses a 9-scene log table of class percentages. The networks use averages of cue ramps with thresholds (N2 'all together' rules, N3 6 descriptions per class) or a clipped 'combinations' vote family (N1), a different combination rule.

steps.step: Straight-line and horizontal-vs-vertical edge dominance cues
steps.note: Long oriented-line detectors at 7x7, 5x5 or 9x9 in the networks, against coherence or run-length measures in the programs.

steps.step: Horizon/waterline or hull-line detection (strongest horizontal colour or brightness step)
steps.note: N1 searches for the strongest horizontal step edge, N2 has hull-line and shadow-line cues, N3 matches 180 waterline strip templates.

steps.step: Wheel-pair detector searched over positions and spacings in the lower image
steps.note: N2 and N3 use identical 288-placement wheel layouts. N1 separates car from truck spacing in wheel radii, which P2 does with radii multiples.

steps.step: Two-eyes-plus-nose face detector with cat vs dog nose drop
steps.note: All search eye spacing and nose drop. N3 scores a placement by its weakest part, a min rule the programs do not use.

steps.step: Leg-pair detector (paired thin vertical strokes in the lower half)
steps.note: N1 has a paired dark-blob running-leg detector at a single 9.0 px half-spacing. N2 lists a 'legs' cue but describes no leg detector. N3 matches 768 leg-under-torso templates.

steps.step: Texture/fur cues (fine grain, disordered vs coherent edges, blotches)
steps.note: The networks use high-pass grain and bar/spot filters. P2 uses frequency bands. The quantity measured is the same.

steps.step: Left-right mirror symmetry about candidate central axes
steps.note: N1 tries 5 candidate columns, N3 tries 3 axes (6.5 to 8.5 of 16), P3 tries columns 12 to 20.

steps.step: Foreground blob extent: size, centroid, aspect ratio, elongation, compactness
steps.note: No network measures object spread or elongation from a foreground map.

steps.step: Dark band or shadow under the object (vehicle underbody)
steps.note: N2 has dark-chassis and shadow-line cues. N3 uses fixed under/belt/roof brightness bands. N1 has only a 'dark middle band' in its sketches and body bands in its wheel templates.

steps.step: Rectangular cargo-panel, windshield-stripe and car-flank detectors
steps.note: Only P3 has these. The networks' 'belt' and 'roof' bands are not panel detectors.

steps.step: Hand-weighted per-class cue sums, including man-made vs natural or family-level terms
steps.note: Signed votes against a typical baseline. The networks add ramps between thresholds and clipping or soft limits.

steps.step: Final weighted sum of evidence sources, then argmax
steps.note: The same architecture: template evidence plus scene and cue evidence, each with a hand-set weight.

network_only.step: Fixed per-class expected object-vs-surround colour table on 3 opponent axes, scored against the measured inside-minus-band colour (signed, class-specific)
Votes grouped into 6 families, each family's per-class total clipped to a fixed maximum
Final scores decomposed into a vehicle/animal group average plus the within-group deviation, with separate weights
26 materials regrouped into 26 broader settings, each taking its best member
Each template pose shaded in 3 grey-level palettes and searched as a separate candidate
Per-class cue vote soft-limited (scaled by 0.43, limited at 1.35)
Per-class pooling via the mean of best scores within 8 fixed subsets of 120 drawings
Face placement scored as the weakest of its three parts (min rule)
Fit to 35 reference colours grouped into 24 four-colour material palettes, closest member per block
Texture votes on broken or changing bar texture between neighbouring spots, and fine vs medium bars and spots
Colour-contrast template layout using a fixed class hue in two thirds of the drawings

numbers.meaning: Weight of silhouette vs foreground-map agreement in the template score
Red/green/blue weights for brightness
numbers.network_values: N1: 0.3 / 0.53 / 0.17 (N3 0.299/0.587/0.114 is the standard luma formula, generic)

numbers.meaning: Edge-orientation descriptor grid of 8x8 cells, 4 px each
numbers.program_values: P1: 8x8 cells; P3: 8x8 grid of 4 px cells
numbers.network_values: N3: 8x8 grid, 4 px sampling step

numbers.meaning: Background/setting pairs per class used for synthetic colour scenes
numbers.network_values: N2: 6 settings per class (sky colour over ground colour)

numbers.meaning: Eye half-spacing for face detector
numbers.program_values: P2: 2 to 6 px half-spacing; P3: eye spacing 2 to 6 px
numbers.network_values: N1: 3.7 (cat) / 4.2 (dog) px

numbers.network_values: N1: 2.84 (car) / 4.05 (truck) radii

numbers.program_values: P3: offset up to about 3 px
numbers.network_values: N1: +/-4 px; N3: up to 3.8 px

numbers.network_values: N3: 6.5/7.5/8.5 of 16 (13 to 17 px); N1: best of 5 central columns

numbers.meaning: Best vs average blend in per-class template pooling
numbers.program_values: P1: 0.73 / 0.27 (best placement vs top-6 placements); P3: 0.83 / 0.17 (best vs second view)
numbers.network_values: N1: 7 / 2.5 (about 0.74 / 0.26, best drawing vs 5-drawing mean); N3: 3.7 / 2.0

numbers.meaning: Count of 5 in pooling

numbers.network_values: N1: average of 5 drawings' bests; N2: average of 5 view bests
