cover.verdict: The three networks have the same overall design as the programs: a pose-searched library of hand-drawn silhouettes matched on edge layout and brightness layout and pooled best-plus-average per class, plus hand-weighted scene colour bands, line, wheel, face, leg, texture and symmetry cues, all summed and argmaxed. N2 even reproduces P1's synthetic-colour-scene family almost exactly. But they match the programs at the level of ingredients, not the exact computation. They use 4 brightness-only edge directions where the programs use 6 bins with colour edges. N2 and N3 drop the border-based figure/ground map and the silhouette-vs-foreground term entirely, and the sign-free interior-vs-rim contrast is replaced by fixed class-expected colour signatures. They leave out foreground extent and elongation, P1's 3D-rendered views and minimum-barrier enclosure, P2's spread-penalised soft max, and P3's panel, windshield and flank detectors. Stage 6 gives N1 the closest overall match (especially to P3: 2D drawings, polarity, figure/ground coverage at 0.22 vs 0.21), N2 is closest to P1, and N3 is the furthest of the three.

d.summary: The image is converted to a log-like lightness plus red, blue and yellow colour-opponent maps, contrast-normalised over the whole image. The method then matches against a large bank of synthetic, hand-drawn renderings of every sign: outer shape and colour layout, the inner symbol, the speed-limit digits, the warning-triangle pictograms, edge orientation along the outline, and the diagonal "end of" stripe. It searches over many sign sizes, offsets and aspect ratios and keeps the best-matching placement. A weighted sum of these best-match scores, plus a few per-class offsets, gives the class.
d.references: All references are drawn procedurally from geometry. None is taken from photos. (1) Symbol stencils for all 43 classes, about 4 drawing variants each. They cover digit strings drawn from hand-placed stroke paths ("20" to "120", 4 font variants differing in height, width, gap and stroke weight), cars, trucks, people, arrows, bars, a STOP lettering, lamps, bumps, a snowflake, a deer and so on. Each sits in a circle, triangle, diamond or octagon area. The "end" signs have a diagonal slash over them. (2) Central pictogram templates: 48 per class (4 variants x 4 radii 9.3 to 14.5 px x 3 aspect ratios, with small tilts). That makes 2064 band-passed, zero-mean, unit-norm patterns, with polarity flipped for light-on-dark signs. (3) Colour and silhouette layouts for 14 sign families (red ring, no passing, truck no passing, warning triangle, yield, priority diamond, stop octagon, no vehicles, no trucks, no entry, end 80, end of limits, end of no passing, blue disc). Each is placed at 72 poses on a 16x16 grid, 1008 patterns in all. (4) Digit-string glyph templates: 8 speed limits x 4 variants, compared in a tight box around the number. (5) Whole-sign renderings per class: 43 x 4 variants on a 24x24 pose-normalised grid. (6) Per-pose expected red, blue and yellow region maps for each class. (7) Expected edge-orientation maps (12 directions) for 8 outline families. (8) Warning-pictogram templates for 15 triangle classes, 8 variants each including mirrored and shifted ones. Each also has 3 sub-part templates (centre, lower left, lower right) at 5 small shifts each. (9) Inscription digit templates: 8 limits x 32 variants (stretch, height, slight horizontal offset). (10) Diagonal-stripe probes at 3 angles near 45 degrees. (11) A hand-placed colour pattern for traffic lights (red top, yellow middle, green bottom) and a red-truck colour pattern.

stages.name: Tone and colour conversion
stages.computes: Each RGB value goes through a piecewise approximation of log(value + 0.023), which lifts dark images. The three log channels then become a lightness channel (0.3R + 0.5G + 0.2B) and three colour-opponent channels: redness (R minus G and B), blueness (B minus R and G) and yellowness (R and G minus B).

key_numbers.meaning: offset inside the log curve: how strongly dark pixel values are expanded (pixel value units 0 to 1)
brightness breakpoints of the piecewise log approximation
R/G/B weights forming lightness

stages.name: Per-image lightness standardisation and detail maps
stages.computes: Lightness is set to zero mean and unit spread over the whole image. From it come a band-pass map (each pixel minus its Gaussian-blurred neighbourhood) and a lightly smoothed lightness map. Both are re-standardised over the image and clipped.

key_numbers.meaning: Gaussian blur width of the surround subtracted to get local contrast (9x9 px window)
small blur mixed (20%) into the smoothed lightness map
clip level, in image-standard-deviation units, on both detail maps

stages.name: Colour surface map
stages.computes: The redness, blueness and yellowness channels are clipped, joined by the smoothed lightness, and averaged down to a 16x16 grid. This grid is used by every colour-layout comparison.

key_numbers.meaning: clip level on each colour-opponent value
averaging cell giving the 16x16 colour grid

stages.name: Sign-family silhouette and colour match
stages.computes: The 16x16 colour grid is correlated with templates of 14 sign families, each showing where it should be light, red, blue or yellow. Each family is tried at 72 placements, and its best placement is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: sign radii tried (4 sizes) in the 32 px image
aspect ratios tried
horizontal and vertical offsets of the sign centre tried (3 each)

stages.name: Central pictogram match
stages.computes: An 'ink' map (mostly band-pass detail plus some lightness) is read from the central 20x20 px window at 25 offsets (up to 2 px each way). It is correlated with the 48 drawn symbol templates per class, and the best score over templates and offsets is kept per class.

key_numbers.meaning: side of the central window read
offset search range (5x5 positions)
sign radii used when drawing the templates

stages.name: Speed-limit number reading in candidate boxes
stages.computes: The standardised lightness is resampled into 16x16 chips from 288 candidate boxes around the centre, each chip re-standardised. Each chip is correlated with the drawn digit strings of the 8 speed limits. A penalty applies when the box's width to height ratio departs from that number's own ratio, and a smaller one for distance from the centre. The best box and variant is kept per limit.

key_numbers.value: 5.8 to 13.4 px tall, 7.9 to 17.5 px wide
key_numbers.meaning: heights and widths of the candidate number boxes
allowed width/height ratio of a box
box centre offsets tried (4x4)
log aspect mismatch tolerated before the penalty

stages.name: Pose-registered whole-sign evidence
stages.computes: 90 sign poses are tried (5 radii, 2 aspects, 3x3 centre offsets). For each pose the lightness is resampled into a sign-centred chip and re-standardised. That chip is correlated with each class's whole-sign drawings (4 variants, keep best) and with the class's expected red, blue and yellow region layout. The outline is also checked against the expected edge directions of its family.

key_numbers.meaning: sign radii tried
sign centre offsets tried
chip resolution, spanning 1.04 sign radii either side of the centre
edge orientations compared along the outline

stages.name: Pose-registered warning pictogram, digit and stripe checks
stages.computes: At the same 90 poses, the lower-middle interior of the triangle is resampled (18x18) and matched with the 15 warning pictograms. Two kinds of match are used: a whole match, and a parts match where centre, lower-left and lower-right pieces may each shift slightly and are then averaged. A separate 18x18 chip of the sign interior is matched against 32 digit variants per speed limit. A diagonal dark-stripe probe at 3 angles needs both ends of the slash to be darker than the flanks, and takes the weaker end.

key_numbers.meaning: downward shift of the warning chip centre from the sign centre
horizontal and vertical shifts allowed for each pictogram part
stripe angles tested for 'end of' signs
stretch along the stripe where each end is checked

stages.name: Pictogram colour cues and pose choice
stages.computes: At each pose, hue patterns are checked: red at the top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom for traffic lights, and a red truck on the left for 'no passing for trucks'. All per-pose evidence for a class is summed with fixed weights, and the best pose is kept per class.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the whole-sign drawing match within the pose sum
weight of the registered digit reading for speed classes
weight of the stripe evidence and of the traffic-light colour pattern
vertical positions of the three lamps

stages.name: Blank-centre measure
stages.computes: Gaussian-weighted total absolute detail near the image centre. Strong detail counts heavily against 'no vehicles' (an empty disc) and mildly against 'yield'.

key_numbers.meaning: horizontal and vertical width of the central weighting
penalty per unit of centre detail for 'no vehicles'

d.decision:
Each class gets a weighted sum of its evidence, and the highest total wins:
- 0.35 x the best silhouette and colour match of its sign family.
- 0.3 x its best central pictogram match (0.12 for speed limits, 0.17 for blue mandatory signs).
- 2.8 x its best pose-registered combined score.
- For the 8 speed limits only: 6 x the best digit-string match in the candidate boxes, with a -2 offset.
- The blank-centre penalty.
- Fixed per-class offsets: 'no vehicles' +1.05, 'yield' +0.5, 'end' signs +0.4, 'stop' -0.35.
d.adapts_per_image:
Lightness and the detail maps are standardised by the mean and spread measured on each image, and every resampled chip is re-standardised the same way. The method searches over sign size, aspect ratio and centre offset, keeping the best placement:
- 72 placements for family shape.
- 25 offsets for the central symbol.
- 288 boxes for the number.
- 90 poses for the joint whole-sign match, shared across all cues for a class.

Within those searches it also keeps the best drawing variant, the best part shift and the best stripe angle. There is no branching or iteration beyond taking these maxima.

d.summary: The sign is located separately for each of eight sign shapes (red ring, red-bordered up triangle, blue disc, white end-of disc with diagonal stripe, yellow diamond, inverted yield triangle, octagon, red disc with white bar). For each shape it searches a fixed set of positions, sizes, aspect ratios and slants for the best colour and brightness outline match, and for the round and triangular shapes it then refines the fit locally. The inside of the located sign is resampled to a standard frame and compared against many drawn and deformed pictograms of each class in that shape family. Speed limit numbers are also read digit by digit with stored digit drawings. The class score adds how well the shape fits to how well the content matches, with a few special colour checks, and the highest score wins.
d.references: 1) Shape outline templates: for each of 8 sign shapes (circle, upright triangle, inverted triangle, diamond, octagon, plus circle variants for blue, end-of and no-entry signs), soft masks for outside surround, rim band, inner core, and shape-specific parts (a diagonal stripe band for end-of signs, a horizontal central band for no-entry and octagon). Each mask is given at 1125 candidate placements (5 x centres, 5 y centres, 5 sizes, 3 aspect ratios, 3 slants) on a 16x16 coarse grid. 2) Outline probe points: 56 points around a circle, or 3 x 17 points along the sides of an upright or inverted triangle, each sampled at 4 offsets across the rim (just inside the core, on the rim, just outside, further outside). 3) Pictogram drawings: hand-drawn vector pictures of every class's inner symbol (speed numbers 20 to 120 in up to 4 font styles, car pair, truck, truck plus car, bend arrows, pedestrian and child stick figures, bicycle, deer, snowflake, traffic light circles, road works man, the direction arrows and roundabout, the end-of diagonal stripe pattern with faint old symbol, the word STOP, the white no-entry bar). Each is rendered at high resolution, lightly blurred, and resampled inside the sign frame under a grid of horizontal and vertical scales, shears and small shifts, then mean-centred and unit-normalised: about 12,500 for the red ring family (29 drawings x 432 deformations), about 6,800 for warnings (21 drawings x 324), about 2,400 for blue arrows, about 970 for end-of signs, 243 each for stop and no-entry. Smoothed and edge-difference versions of the warning and end-of templates, and per-zone local contrast energies for warnings, are also stored. 4) Digit drawings: 8 digits (0,1,2,3,5,6,7,8) at 3 stroke weights x 3 widths x 3 heights x 3 shears x 3 horizontal shifts x 2 vertical shifts, 3,888 in all, on an 11 wide by 15 tall cell.

stages.name: Colour and brightness maps
stages.computes: Takes the logarithm of each colour channel and forms soft redness, blueness and yellowness maps from opponent differences, plus a brightness map stretched between the image's own 8th and 92nd brightness percentiles. A second, red-weighted brightness map (for reading dark ink on white) and greenness and redness maps for the traffic light check are also made.

key_numbers.meaning: offset added before the logarithm so near-black pixels do not blow up (pixel value units, 0 to 1)
per-image brightness stretch range
what redness is measured against, in log colour

stages.name: Coarse sign shape search
stages.computes: On a 16x16 downsampled version of the maps, scores each of 1125 candidate placements for each of the 8 sign shapes by how red (or blue, or yellow) the rim or body is versus the surround and how bright the core is versus the rim, minus a penalty for being off centre, off the typical size, stretched or slanted. Keeps the best placement and its score for each shape.

key_numbers.meaning: candidate sign centre and half-height in pixels of the 32x32 image
red rim width as fraction of sign radius for round and triangular signs
allowed horizontal stretch and shear of the outline
preferred centre (pixels) and preferred half-height (pixels) for the penalty

stages.name: Fine outline fitting
stages.computes: For the red ring, warning triangle and yield triangle shapes, refines centre, width, height, slant and a vertical tilt by coordinate-wise hill climbing at three step sizes, scoring how much the rim samples are red and dark relative to the inner core and the outer surround along the outline probe points.

key_numbers.meaning: search step for position and size in pixels (shear and tilt use 0.072 times this)
points around the circle or along the triangle sides

stages.name: Rim versus interior check
stages.computes: After resampling the sign to a 26x26 standard frame, compares redness in the rim band with the interior and brightness of the interior with the rim, and adds this to the shape score, so a red rim around a pale field is favoured. For the yield shape the spread of brightness inside also scores how blank the interior is.

key_numbers.meaning: distances from the edge (fraction of radius) defining rim and core for round signs; 0.13 and 0.18 for triangles
interior brightness spread, a blank yield interior scores higher

stages.name: Pictogram matching
stages.computes: Resamples the sign interior inside a shape-specific margin, clips and normalises its brightness by the image's own percentiles and mean, inverts so dark ink is positive (for red ring, warning and end-of signs), and correlates it with every stored deformed drawing; each class keeps its best matching deformation, minus a small penalty for large deformations. For warnings and end-of signs it also correlates smoothed and edge-direction versions and, for warnings, compares local contrast energy in 9 zones with the drawings. The no-vehicles class instead scores high when the interior is nearly flat.

key_numbers.meaning: standard frame size for the sign interior
fraction of sign radius excluded as rim for round and triangular interiors
per-image interior brightness clipping range
weight of the red-weighted ink map versus the plain brightness map for round and warning signs

stages.name: Speed number reading by fixed slots
stages.computes: For speed limit candidates, places 2 or 3 digit windows across the sign centre at 4 overall scales (and, for 3 digits, two spacing layouts), normalises each window, and matches it against stored digit drawings: first digit among 2,3,5,6,7,8 with second digit 0, or first digit 1, middle 0 or 2, last 0. Keeps the best layout per number.

key_numbers.meaning: horizontal positions of two digits as fraction of sign radius
overall size of the digit layout relative to the sign
half-height of the digit window, fraction of sign radius

stages.name: Speed number reading by segmentation
stages.computes: Estimates the local paper white per column, turns darkness below it into an ink map, projects ink onto columns and rows to find the text's extent, then cuts between digits at the emptiest column near the expected split position (half way for 2 digits, 27 percent and 64 percent for 3). Each segment is matched to the digit drawings, and a clean blank gap at the cut adds credit.

key_numbers.meaning: resampled grid over the sign interior used for segmentation
expected cut positions as fraction of text width for 2 and 3 digit numbers
ink strength used to normalise the ink map, per image

stages.name: Special colour cues
stages.computes: For the ring family, redness on the left of the interior versus the right raises both no passing classes (red car on the left) and lowers 120. For warnings, a green spot low in the middle together with a red spot near the top raises traffic lights. For the yellow diamond, it checks four straight sides with brightness and yellowness falling from inside to outside, using the middle two of the four side scores.

key_numbers.meaning: left and right interior regions compared for red, as fraction of radius
vertical positions of the green and red light test spots inside the triangle
inside and outside sample distances along the diamond sides, fraction of size

stages.name: Score combination
stages.computes: Each class's score is its shape family's outline score plus 0.86 times its content score. For speed limits the content score blends template matching (0.45), fixed slot reading (0.31) and segmentation reading (0.24). Stop, no entry and priority road use a shape score plus a fixed or edge-based content score.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of content match relative to shape fit
weights of pictogram, slot reading and segmented reading for speed numbers

stages.name: Second look for close calls
stages.computes: If the top two class scores are within 0.18, the image is slightly blurred and the whole pipeline is run again, and the two score sets are averaged 0.64 to 0.36.

key_numbers.meaning: score margin below which an image counts as ambiguous
weights of the original and blurred passes

d.decision: The class with the highest combined score (shape fit plus weighted content match, averaged with a blurred second pass when the top two were close) is chosen.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes, a lot. Brightness is stretched between the image's own percentiles. The best sign placement is searched per shape over 1125 positions, sizes, aspect ratios and slants, then refined by hill climbing for round and triangular shapes. Each class keeps its best matching template deformation, and each speed number keeps its best digit layout and scale. Segmentation finds the text extent and digit cut points from each image's ink profile, normalised by per-image paper and ink levels. A second, blurred pass runs only when the first pass's top two scores are within 0.18.

d.summary: The method assumes the sign is roughly centred and tries 36 guesses of where it is (4 sizes times a 3 by 3 grid of centre positions). For each guess it adds up many matching scores for every class: does the frame colour and shape fit the class's sign family, does the inside look like hand-drawn pictures of that class's symbol (both full-sign and inner-symbol drawings, each under several distortions), and do simple colour and layout checks pass. It then keeps the best-scoring guess for each class and picks the class with the top total.
d.references: All of it is drawn by hand in the build code from geometry, and nothing comes from training photos. (1) Vector drawings of each class's pictogram, drawn on a 128x128 canvas where 1 unit is the sign radius, in 4 drawing styles: speed numbers built from hand-placed curve strokes in two digit widths and two stroke weights, cars, a lorry, walking people, children, a bicycle, a deer, a snowflake, traffic-light dots, arrows, the STOP letters, the exclamation mark, bends, bumps, the roadworks figure and diagonal end-of stripes. Dark symbols are stored with negative polarity and white symbols (blue signs, stop, no entry) with positive polarity. (2) Frame outlines for 8 sign families (red ring, red warning triangle, blue disc, grey end-of disc, inverted yield triangle, yellow priority diamond, stop octagon, red disc with white bar), each with outer, inner, band and support regions, drawn at all 36 sign positions and sizes. (3) Built from these: about 19,656 inner-symbol templates (39 classes x 4 sizes x 9 shifts x 14 distortions), 384 typeset templates for the speed numbers (8 numbers x 4 heights x 3 stretches x 4 slant and spacing styles), 63 distortions per class of the symbol drawn in a straightened sign frame, 8 distortions per class of whole-sign drawings (frame plus symbol), 168 left-to-right ink profiles of the speed numbers, 9 diamond outlines, and many fixed colour-region masks (ring arcs, triangle sides, diagonal stripe ends, a central bar, traffic-light spots, the left car area).

stages.name: Tone and colour opponents
stages.computes: Each red, green and blue value goes through a log-like brightness curve built from straight pieces. Four colour signals are then formed: brightness, red against the rest, blue against the rest and yellow against blue. Each signal is rescaled by its own mean and spread over the whole image, capped, and the unscaled colour signals are added back in. The result is averaged down to 16x16.

key_numbers.meaning: offset inside the log curve, so very dark pixel values are lifted (value scale 0 to 1)
red, green and blue weights for the brightness signal
cap on each colour signal, in image standard deviations
weight of the unscaled colour difference added back to the rescaled one

stages.name: Candidate sign positions
stages.computes: Sets up 36 hypotheses for where the sign is: 4 sign radii times a 3 by 3 grid of centre offsets around the middle of the image. Almost every later score is computed separately for each hypothesis.

key_numbers.meaning: sign radius in pixels on the 32x32 image
horizontal and vertical centre offsets, in pixels

stages.name: Frame family evidence
stages.computes: For each of the 8 sign families and each position, the coarse colour image is compared with a drawing of that family's frame: a brightness pattern plus the expected coloured band (red ring or triangle, blue disc, yellow diamond, grey annulus, octagon, white bar). A second comparison contrasts the frame colour with the inner field under 5 small stretches and tilts and keeps the best one. The strongest position for each family is also added to every position, and the totals are passed to every class in that family.

key_numbers.meaning: inner edge of the frame band, as a fraction of the sign radius
tilt and stretch range tried for the frame
weight of the combined frame score in each class total

stages.name: Ink map
stages.computes: A grey ink image (mostly red and green, put through the log curve) is rescaled by its own mean and spread over the image and capped. A band-pass copy is also made: each pixel minus 0.77 times a blur of its neighbourhood.

key_numbers.meaning: red, green and blue weights for the ink grey
cap in image standard deviations
blur width of the surround subtracted in the band-pass copy

stages.name: Inner symbol matching
stages.computes: The central 26x26 band-passed ink patch is rescaled to its own mean and spread. It is compared with each class's pictogram drawing, masked to that family's inner field, at every position and under 14 distortions (scale, shear, small rotation, drawing style, vertical shift). The best distortion is kept for each class and position. This covers 39 classes, all except yield, priority, no vehicles and no entry.

key_numbers.meaning: side of the central window that is read
range of horizontal scale distortions
largest symbol rotation tried
radius of the symbol mask for red ring, blue and end-of signs, as a fraction of the sign radius

stages.name: Speed number reading
stages.computes: The 8 speed-limit numbers are drawn as typeset text in 48 sizes and styles. Each is slid over the central 23x23 band-passed ink patch across a 9x9 range of shifts, and the best shift and style are kept for each number. Each number's score is its reading minus the average reading of all 8, and it applies to every position. A second test compares the left-to-right ink profile inside the straightened sign face with the profiles of the drawn numbers.

key_numbers.meaning: heights of the drawn numbers
width stretches tried for the number
shift search for the typeset number
weight of the number reading relative to the mean

stages.name: Straightened symbol and whole-sign matching
stages.computes: For each position, the ink is resampled onto a 19x19 grid that straightens the sign face (folded into a triangle for warning signs, an ellipse for round signs), rescaled to its own mean and spread, and compared with each class's pictogram under 63 shifts and distortions, keeping the best. A separate 17x17 resampling maps the disc or triangle onto a square, and the whole sign (frame plus symbol, in rendered grey levels) is compared against 8 distortions for every class.

key_numbers.meaning: grid size of the straightened face for symbol and whole-sign matching
symbol match level counted as neutral (score is 2.6 times the match minus 0.38)
how a whole-sign match turns into class evidence

stages.name: Colour and layout checks
stages.computes: Fixed region tests at each position. (1) Inner brightness, redness and blueness inside 0.66 of the radius: bright faces favour red-ring, warning and end-of signs, blue favours blue signs. (2) A red car on the left favours the no-passing signs. (3) Red is checked in 8 arcs of the ring, and missing arcs count against red-ring signs and for end-of signs. (4) Red against the inner field on all 3 triangle sides, averaged, for warning signs. (5) A light diagonal stripe at both ends of the diagonal, taking the weaker end, for end-of signs. (6) Red over yellow spots for traffic lights, a red top edge for yield, and a light central bar between red flanks for no entry. (7) The yellow channel resampled into a diamond and matched against diamond outlines for priority road.

key_numbers.meaning: radii of the ring band and the inner band in the arc test, as fractions of the sign radius
arc contrast below which a ring arc counts as missing
distance along the diagonal where the stripe ends are checked, as a fraction of the radius
diamond outline sizes tried for priority road, as fractions of the radius

stages.name: Blank face rule
stages.computes: Measures the average edge strength of the ink inside 0.61 of the radius at each position. Low texture strongly favours the signs with plain faces (yield, no vehicles, priority, no entry), each with its own fixed bonus.

key_numbers.meaning: radius of the region checked for texture, as a fraction of the sign radius
penalty per unit of texture for yield and no vehicles

stages.name: Combine and choose
stages.computes: For each class and position, all the evidence above is added up. The best position is kept for each class, and the class with the highest total wins.

d.decision: Each class gets a total score at every one of the 36 sign position and size guesses. That total is the sum of its frame, symbol, number, whole-sign and colour-rule evidence. The class keeps its best guess, and the class whose best total is highest is the answer.
d.adapts_per_image: Several things change with the image. Colour signals and ink maps are rescaled by each image's own mean and spread, and each extracted patch is rescaled again to its own mean and spread. Each class's score is the best over 36 sign positions and sizes. Within each test, the best of several distortions or drawing styles is kept, and the speed number keeps its best position within ±4 px. The frame score adds the family's best position to every position. Speed number scores are measured against the average of all 8 number readings. Missing ring arcs and the weaker diagonal stripe end are found with thresholds and minimums. Otherwise there is no looping, iterating until convergence, or branching on intermediate results.

d.summary: The method works out the colour and brightness of the image relative to that image's own lighting, then searches positions, sizes and slants to fit each of eight sign outline shapes: red-ringed circle, upright triangle, inverted triangle, blue disc, red octagon, yellow diamond, red disc, and pale disc with a dark diagonal stripe. Each class is scored as how well its outline fits, plus how closely the content inside the fitted outline matches stored drawings of that class's symbol. Brightness patterns and edge directions are both compared, and a second ink-centred reading is used for the circle and triangle signs. A few plain signs are scored by hand-written tests instead, such as an empty interior or red corners, and the class with the highest score wins.

stages.name: Lighting-normalised colour maps
stages.computes: Takes the log of each colour value and builds a luminance map stretched between that image's 10th and 90th percentile brightness. It also builds red, blue and yellow opponent maps, each shifted by its own 25th percentile to cancel part of the colour cast.

key_numbers.meaning: dark and bright anchor levels for stretching brightness, measured per image
per-image colour-cast offset taken off each opponent map (68% of it removed)
offset added before the log, which limits noise amplification in very dark pixels

stages.name: Coarse shape search
stages.computes: On an 18x18 downsampled view, scores each of the 8 sign shapes at 224 placements by comparing colour and brightness in a rim band, the interior and a ring outside the rim. For example: red rim brighter outside and pale inside for circles and triangles, blue disc, yellow centre with white border for the diamond, pale disc with a dark diagonal for 'end of'. Placements far off centre or strongly non-square are slightly penalised, and the best one is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: candidate horizontal and vertical radii of the sign in the 32 px image (width and height may differ by up to 4.8 px)
candidate sign centres around the image centre
thickness of the border ring as a fraction of sign size (0.003 to 0.13 for triangles)

stages.name: Ring and edge completeness check
stages.computes: For circle and triangle shapes, splits the rim into 6 angular sectors (circle) or 3 sides (triangle) and checks in each that the rim is darker or redder than the band just inside it. The score blends the average and the weakest sector, so the border has to hold up all the way round.

key_numbers.meaning: parts of the border checked separately
how strongly one weak part of the border pulls the score down

stages.name: Fine shape refinement
stages.computes: Around the best coarse placement, resamples a 29x29 window in the sign's own frame and tries 405 adjustments: shifts, rescales and shears. It keeps the best, with small penalties for large adjustments, and the shape score blends the coarse and fine fits.

key_numbers.meaning: fine centre adjustment
fine size adjustment per axis
slant adjustment for signs seen at an angle
weights of the coarse and fine fit in the shape score

stages.name: Alternative placement
stages.computes: For the red-ringed circle and the upright triangle, it also keeps a second-best placement that is clearly away from the first, then refines that one in the same way. This gives a fallback when the best fit was fooled, for example by a covered border.

key_numbers.meaning: minimum separation in centre and size (pixels) for the alternative placement
score handicap given to the alternative placement

stages.name: Interior symbol matching
stages.computes: Resamples the inside of each fitted shape onto a 25x25 sign-centred grid and builds a symbol image from it. For red circles and triangles this is darkness, with the red border suppressed; for blue discs it is brightness minus blueness; for 'end of' signs it is darkness. Inside a family-specific interior mask, it correlates the normalised symbol image with every stored drawing variant of each class in that family and keeps the best per class. For circles and triangles it blends in a match of edge directions.

key_numbers.meaning: interior sampling resolution
interior region compared, as a fraction of sign radius, for red circle, blue disc and 'end of' signs
weights of brightness-pattern match and edge-direction match

stages.name: Ink-centred re-framing and second match
stages.computes: Inside the fitted sign, it separates dark ink from pale background using thresholds set by that sign's own 24th and 92nd percentile levels. It measures the ink's centre of mass and spread, re-frames tightly on the ink and correlates the result with a second bank of drawings that are framed by their own ink extent. This match is combined with the first one.

key_numbers.meaning: background and ink levels within this sign

key_numbers.value: cut at 34% from background to ink
key_numbers.meaning: soft threshold separating ink from background
how far the ink frame may move, as a fraction of sign radius
weights of the first match, the ink-framed match and the better of the two

stages.name: Special tests for plain signs
stages.computes: No vehicles: red circle with a low-variance interior and little ink contrast. Yield: inverted-triangle fit plus a uniform interior. Priority road: diamond fit plus a uniform centre. Stop and no entry: shape fit plus a match to STOP letters or the bar, plus redness in all four corner quadrants above and below the middle. No entry also rewards a uniform bright bar and penalises texture. Traffic lights: a bonus when the top of the symbol is redder or yellower than the bottom.

key_numbers.meaning: penalty for an uneven interior when scoring 'no vehicles'
penalty for an uneven interior when scoring 'yield'
region of the no-entry bar, as a fraction of sign radius
quadrant regions that must be red for stop and no entry

d.decision: Each class score is the fitted shape's score plus 0.85 times the best symbol match for that class. The 'end of' signs weight them 0.66 and 1.23, and stop and no entry use their own mix. Where a class can be read from several placements (the primary and the alternative), its highest score is kept. The class with the overall highest score is predicted. In effect the sign's shape and colour pick the family, and the symbol inside picks the member.
d.adapts_per_image:
- Brightness and colour are normalised by percentiles measured on each image.
- For each sign shape, the method searches 224 coarse placements and then 405 fine adjustments, keeping the best.
- For two of the shapes it also keeps a second, clearly distinct placement.
- Interior templates are compared at many scales, shifts and slants, keeping the best per class.
- The ink-centred pass places and sizes its second reading from the ink's centre of mass and spread, measured on that image.
- Ink and background thresholds come from each sign's own percentile levels.
- The final answer takes the maximum over placements and classes.

d.summary: This is a hand-built recogniser that works by explicit shape and symbol matching, not by learned features. It first works out which kind of sign outline is present (red-rimmed circle, red triangle, inverted triangle, yellow diamond, blue disc, grey "end" disc with a diagonal, octagon, circle with a bar) and where it sits, by scoring the colour of a rim band, the inner field and the area just outside. It then refines that placement, samples the sign face in the sign's own frame and compares it with many drawn and blurred pictograms of each class, plus a digit reader for the speed limits. Shape evidence, whole-sign colour layout and symbol evidence are added up, and the best class wins.
d.references: All reference material is drawn procedurally at 192x192 from geometric primitives (polygons, ellipses, thick strokes, Bezier curves), smoothed, and resampled; nothing is taken from photos. (1) Outline detectors: for each of 8 outline families, 81 placements (3x3 centre offsets of plus or minus 1.6 px, half widths and heights of 10, 12.5 or 15 px). Each is a weighted mask of rim band, inner field and exterior ring over red, blue or yellow colour and brightness, at 16x16. (2) Point sets: 80 sample points each in the rim band, inner field and exterior for each family. (3) Interior pictograms: hand-drawn symbols for every class with symbols (speed numerals in 3 font styles, cars, trucks, arrows, people, bicycles, deer in 7 poses, snowflake, traffic light, STOP letters, bars, diagonal stripes). Each is rendered at 2 or 3 blur levels, 3x3 scales (0.84, 1, 1.17) and 9 or 15 shifts, which gives thousands of normalised templates, plus edge-difference versions for the red circle, red triangle and end families. (4) Digit reader: 8 speed strings (20 to 120) x 3 styles x 4 widths x 2 heights x 5 x 3 shifts x 2 slants = 720 per number, 5760 in all, each with its digit split position. (5) Part models for warning triangles: each pictogram at 5 shifts x 4 stretches, with 5 sub-regions (whole, upper, lower, left-lower, right-lower), each sub-region allowed 5 small displacements. (6) Whole-sign colour layouts: per class and style, a full sign (rim colour, face colour, dark symbol, traffic light colours) at 1 or 2 rim widths and 8 jitters (shift plus or minus 0.045, scale 0.96 or 1.04), in green-like brightness, red and blue channels. (7) Small red-region templates for the red car or truck in the no-passing signs and the red lamp of the traffic light.

stages.name: Exposure and colour normalisation
stages.computes: Brightness is stretched per image twice, once between low and high ranks of the whole image and once between ranks of the central part of the image, and the two are blended 40/60. Red, blue and yellow strength maps are computed as relative channel differences divided by overall brightness, clipped. Yellow is reduced where red is present.

key_numbers.meaning: about the 6th and 92nd brightness percentiles of the whole image, used as black and white points
region used for a second, sign-centred stretch (15th darkest to 20th brightest pixel)
blend of the global stretch and the centre-region stretch
fraction of red strength subtracted from yellow so that red rims do not count as yellow

stages.name: Coarse outline and placement search
stages.computes: At half resolution, each of 8 outline families is scored at 81 placements by contrasting the family's colour in a rim band with the inner field and the exterior, plus brightness in the inner field against the rim. The best placement per family is kept, with a small penalty for being off centre.

key_numbers.meaning: candidate sign half width and half height, separately in x and y
candidate centre offsets from the image centre
inner edge of the rim band as a fraction of sign radius for circles, triangles and the diamond
penalty per pixel of offset from the image centre

stages.name: Keep competing outline hypotheses
stages.computes: Every family whose best coarse score is within a margin of the top family is kept for detailed analysis. Classes of the other families are scored -20 and ruled out.

key_numbers.meaning: score margin below the best family within which other families stay alive

stages.name: Placement refinement
stages.computes: Hill-climb style local search: the coarse placement is perturbed in size and position (45 options) and then in finer position and shear (27 options). Each option is scored by mean colour and brightness at the stored rim, field and exterior points, and the best is kept each time.

key_numbers.meaning: size step in each axis on the first pass
centre shift steps on the coarse and fine passes
horizontal shear tried, to allow for viewing angle

stages.name: Outline completeness check
stages.computes: For circles, triangles and the diamond, each rim point is compared with the point at 68 percent of the radius toward the centre (colour should drop and brightness rise moving inward). A low percentile of that contrast is taken, so the whole perimeter must agree, not just a few patches. For the diamond, the yellow inside and the dark-blue trim around it give extra evidence. For octagon and bar circle, a penalty applies if red is stronger at the left and right sides than above and below the centre.

key_numbers.meaning: inward scale where the inner field is checked against the rim
weakest quarter of the perimeter decides the score
diamond interior and trim zones, as a fraction of diamond radius

stages.name: Whole-sign layout comparison
stages.computes: Brightness, red and blue are sampled over the full face in the fitted frame and compared with rendered full-sign colour layouts of each class (rim, face, symbol). The best match per class is kept. Red and blue count only if they vary enough on this image.

key_numbers.meaning: sampled face extent as a fraction of sign radius
relative weight of the brightness pattern and the colour pattern

stages.name: Interior symbol matching
stages.computes: The face interior is resampled on a grid in the fitted frame and contrast-stretched between low and high percentiles, inverted so dark ink is positive (for blue, octagon and bar signs, bright ink is positive). It is then correlated with every stored pictogram and the best match per class is kept. Red circles, triangles and end signs also correlate local brightness differences (edges).

key_numbers.meaning: black and white points of the face interior for this image
interior sample grid, cut to about 0.70 (circle, also limited to 0.53 vertically), 0.695 (triangle) or 0.87 to 0.9 of the sign radius
weight of intensity match against edge match

stages.name: Speed limit digit reading
stages.computes: For red circles, the central number area is matched against the 720 digit renderings of each speed. For the best rendering per speed, agreement is measured separately in the leading digit region and the trailing region. For 100 and 120, the leading '1' is checked to be darker than the paper beside it. The result is blended 65/35 with the general pictogram score.

key_numbers.meaning: window read for digits, as a fraction of sign radius
weights of the whole-string match, first-digit match and last-digit match
weight of the digit reader against the generic symbol match for speeds

stages.name: Family-specific special checks
stages.computes: Red circle: 'no vehicles' scores high when the face has low contrast relative to its own brightness and no digit or stroke is recognised, and red-patch templates help no-passing signs. Warning triangle: the blur of the red border's inner edge is estimated and pictograms rendered at a very different blur are penalised. Red, yellow and green spots at three heights support traffic lights. Upper, lower, left and right halves are matched separately, and a deformable parts match lets sub-regions shift. End signs: only the two crescents away from the diagonal are matched, and low crescent contrast favours 'end of all limits'. Yield and priority: a uniform field is rewarded.

key_numbers.meaning: positions inside the triangle border used to measure edge sharpness
expected red, amber and green lamp positions, in sign half-heights
half-width of the diagonal band excluded on end signs, in sign radius units
red-variation floor below which red-region evidence is ignored

stages.name: Score combination
stages.computes: Each class in a surviving family gets 0.83 x outline score + weight x (symbol score - 0.43) + 0.96 x (whole-layout score - 0.39), with small family offsets.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of outline and placement evidence
weight of interior symbol evidence (0.57 for red circle, triangle and end families)
weight of whole-sign layout evidence
bonus for end-of-restriction signs, which lack colour evidence

d.decision: The class with the highest combined score wins, across all 43 classes. Classes in outline families ruled out early stay at -20. Within a family, each class's score comes from its best-matching rendering (best style, blur, scale and shift).
d.adapts_per_image: Heavily adaptive. Brightness and contrast are normalised by percentiles measured on each image, both over the whole image and over the face interior. The method searches 81 placements per outline family and keeps the best, then refines it with two rounds of local search over size, position and shear. It keeps only the outline families that come close to the best score. Each class keeps its best matching template from many renderings. The digit reader picks the best rendering and then re-scores digit regions on it. Colour evidence is weighted by how much colour varies on this image. Triangle symbols are penalised by a mismatch between template blur and the blur measured on this image. The perimeter check uses a percentile over rim points.

d.summary: The method matches the photo against thousands of reference images drawn from idealised drawings of all 43 signs. It looks at the sign in several ways: the colour outline of the sign family, the whole sign in colour, the central symbol in brightness, the layout of edges, and a version of the sign face unwarped to a standard disk or triangle, where numerals and pictogram parts are read. For every class it adds up the match evidence at each of five assumed sign sizes, with position, stretch, slant and drawing style each set to whichever fits best, and the class whose best sign size scores highest is the answer.
d.references: All references come from one procedural renderer that draws every one of the 43 signs from geometric primitives. It draws the shape (circle, triangle, inverted triangle, diamond, octagon) in coded colours (white, black, red, blue, yellow, grey). The content is drawn in the same way: numerals in up to 4 font variants, car and truck silhouettes, arrows, the STOP word, the warning pictograms (person, children, cyclist, deer, snowflake, traffic lights and so on) and the diagonal stripes on the "end of" signs. These drawings are resampled at 5 sign sizes and several horizontal or vertical stretches and slants, then blurred, centred and normalised, giving about 5,100 references: (a) 200 outline-family references, covering 8 families (red-ringed disk, grey "end of" disk, upright warning triangle, yield, diamond, octagon, solid red disk, blue disk) x 5 sizes x 5 stretches/slants, colour, with the inner face weighted down; (b) 1075 whole-sign colour references (43 x 5 x 5); (c) 1260 central-symbol brightness references (42 classes, none for 'no vehicles', x 5 sizes x 6 poses), mixing the plain pattern with its fine detail; (d) 1075 edge-layout references (43 x 5 x 5), built from 8 directional edge maps of the drawings; (e) references on the unwarped face: 216 whole-face drawings for 27 disk-type classes and 120 for 15 triangle classes (8 font or stretch variants each); 288 numeral references for the 8 speed limits (36 poses each), weighted towards the informative digit (the first digit of two-digit limits, the middle digit of 100/120); 300 pictogram-part references for the 15 triangle classes, each built from 4 local blobs (top, bottom, lower left, lower right of the pictogram); and 576 close-up digit-region references, taken from small 9x9 patches covering either the distinguishing digit or the whole number.

stages.name: Log colour and opponent channels
stages.computes: Each red, green and blue value is passed through a piecewise-linear approximation of a logarithm, then mixed into three opponent channels: brightness, red versus green/blue, and yellow versus blue.

key_numbers.meaning: offset in the log of (value + 0.025), which limits how far very dark pixels are stretched (on the 0 to 1 colour scale)
input levels where the piecewise log curve bends
red, green, blue weights of the brightness channel
weights of the red-versus-blue colour channel

stages.name: Lighting normalisation and downsizing
stages.computes: Each opponent channel is standardised by its own mean and spread over this image. Brightness is kept only in this relative form. The two colour channels mix the relative and absolute values, so real colour still counts. The result is halved to 16x16 by averaging.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of relative and absolute red-versus-blue colour
weights of relative and absolute yellow-versus-blue colour

stages.name: Outline-family matching
stages.computes: On the 16x16 colour image, eight sign-family outline references (shape plus border colour, with the face weighted down) are slid over a 5x5 grid of positions. For each family and sign size, the best position and best stretch or slant are kept.

key_numbers.meaning: sign radius in 16x16 pixels (about 7 to 14 pixels in the full image), 5 sizes
positions searched, a shift of up to 2 half-resolution pixels each way
how much the inner face is weighted down, so the rim and outline dominate

stages.name: Family to class transfer
stages.computes: Each class receives its family's outline score at each size. Fixed extra credit goes to 'no vehicles', 'priority road' and 'yield', the classes with no inner content beyond their shape.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the family score in each class's evidence
constant extra credit for no vehicles, priority road and yield

stages.name: Whole-sign colour matching
stages.computes: Colour references of every one of the 43 signs are slid over the 16x16 colour image. The best position and stretch or slant are kept per class and size.

key_numbers.meaning: reference size in half-resolution pixels
pose variants per class

stages.name: Central symbol matching
stages.computes: The relative brightness of the central 24x24 pixels is cut out and standardised again. Brightness references of each class's inner symbol, masked to the inside of its shape and emphasising fine detail, are slid over a 5x5 grid of positions, and the best pose is kept per class and size.

key_numbers.meaning: central window taken from the 32x32 image
sign radius in full-image pixels, 5 sizes
mix of plain pattern and fine detail in each reference

stages.name: Edge-layout matching
stages.computes: In the central window, brightness changes are measured in 4 directions and 2 polarities, and each of the 8 edge maps is standardised. These are compared with edge maps of the rendered signs, keeping the best position and stretch per class and size.

key_numbers.meaning: edge directions times polarities (horizontal, vertical, two diagonals, each light-to-dark and dark-to-light)
blur, in pixels, applied to the drawings before their edges are taken

stages.name: Unwarping the sign face
stages.computes: The image's absolute brightness (not lighting-normalised) is resampled onto 16x16 canvases. One set maps a disk of 0.7 times the assumed radius to a square; another maps the inside of an upright triangle. Each geometry is tried at 5 sizes x 2 horizontal stretches x 5 centre offsets, giving 50 canvases, and each canvas is then contrast-standardised.

key_numbers.meaning: fraction of the sign radius covered by the disk canvas, which leaves out the rim
horizontal stretches tried
centre offsets tried (four diagonals and the centre)

stages.name: Reading the face
stages.computes: On each canvas, the method compares whole-face drawings (27 disk-type classes, 15 triangle classes), numeral drawings for the 8 speed limits, the four local parts of each triangle pictogram, and close-up patches of the distinguishing digit and of the whole number. The close-up digit scores are then expressed relative to the average over the 8 speed limits. Each class keeps its best style per canvas, then its best stretch and offset per size.

key_numbers.meaning: weight on the first and second digit of two-digit limits (the second is always 0)
weight on the three digit regions of 100 and 120, centred on the middle digit
fixed deductions from numeral and pictogram-part evidence, so only strong matches add to the class score

stages.name: Blankness tests
stages.computes: On the absolute-brightness disk canvases, the average strength of brightness change is measured over the central 12x12 region and over a smaller upper-centre box. Low variation adds evidence for 'no vehicles' (empty white face) and for 'yield' (empty centre), using the flattest offset at each size.

key_numbers.meaning: region tested for 'no vehicles' blankness (16x16 canvas)
region tested for 'yield' blankness
penalty per unit of average edge strength for no vehicles and for yield

stages.name: Combining per size
stages.computes: For each class and each of the 5 sign sizes, the evidence from outline family, whole sign, central symbol, edge layout and face reading is added. The class score is the best total over the 5 sizes.

key_numbers.meaning: sign-size hypotheses (radius about 7 to 14 pixels)

d.decision: The class with the highest score wins. A class's score is its best sign size, where each size's value is the sum of outline-family, whole-sign colour, central-symbol, edge-layout and face-reading evidence (whole face, numerals, digit close-ups, pictogram parts, blankness) at that size, plus fixed extra credit for no vehicles, priority road and yield.
d.adapts_per_image: The method adapts to each image in several ways. Lighting normalisation: each opponent channel is standardised by this image's mean and spread; the central window, each edge map and each unwarped canvas are standardised separately. Search: every comparison keeps the best result over position (5x5 grid, or 5 centre offsets for the unwarped canvases), stretch and slant, and font or drawing variant, separately for each class and size. Size: the sum across all evidence sources is formed per size, and the best of the 5 sizes is kept per class. Numeral close-ups are scored relative to the average over the speed-limit classes on this image. There is no iteration and no branching beyond these best-of selections.

clusters.approach: Fit the outline first, then read the inside: search placements for each of the 8 sign outline families by rim, interior and exterior colour contrast, refine the best placement locally (hill climb or adjustment grid), resample the interior into the sign's own frame, and correlate it with procedurally drawn, deformed pictograms of that family's classes plus a speed digit reader. Class score is shape fit plus weighted content match.

Sum evidence per pose hypothesis: enumerate a fixed set of sign size and position hypotheses, add up family outline and colour match, whole-sign rendering match, central pictogram correlation, digit reading and colour or blankness rules for every class at each hypothesis, all against procedurally drawn templates. Keep each class's best hypothesis and take the argmax. There is no separate locate-then-refine step.

pairs.shared: Log opponent colour, procedurally drawn templates for all classes, sign family colour and shape match on a 16x16 grid, pictogram correlation, speed digit reading, blankness for no vehicles, traffic light colour cues, weighted sum then argmax
pairs.differs: A scores whole-sign and pictogram evidence jointly over fixed pose grids and sums them per class. B fits each outline first with coarse search and hill-climb refinement, then reads the interior in that frame, uses digit-by-digit slot and segmentation reading, and runs a blurred second pass on close calls

pairs.shared: Piecewise log opponent channels, 16x16 colour grid, family frame templates, band-pass ink correlated with drawn inner symbols at offsets, speed number strings, whole-sign renderings per pose, stripe, traffic light and red car checks, blank-centre rule, per-pose evidence summed, best pose per class, argmax
pairs.differs: Differences are in tuning only: C has 36 hypotheses with a straightened face grid and ring arc checks. A has 90 poses with an edge-orientation map and parts-based warning matching

pairs.shared: Log opponent colour, drawn pictogram banks, sign shape and colour evidence, interior pictogram correlation, edge information, special blank and traffic light tests, additive score
pairs.differs: D fits each of 8 outlines with coarse search, sector completeness and fine refinement, plus an alternative placement, then reads the interior in that frame and adds an ink-recentred second match. A sums evidence over a fixed pose grid with no fitting step

pairs.shared: Drawn templates, family outline colour matching, whole-sign colour layout match, pictogram correlation, warning parts matching, digit reading, traffic light spots, blankness, weighted sum
pairs.differs: E locates and refines the outline per family, checks perimeter completeness, prunes families, then samples the interior in the fitted frame. A uses joint pose-grid scoring

steps.step: Log colour transform and red/blue/yellow opponent maps
steps.note: All six take a log with a small offset (0.019 to 0.027) and build opponent maps. P3 uses channel differences divided by brightness rather than a log, but the step is the same in kind.

steps.step: Per-image brightness/colour normalisation
steps.note: The programs stretch between per-image percentiles (8/92, 10/90, about 6/92 plus a centre stretch). The networks z-score by the image mean and spread. Same purpose, different statistic. No network has P3's centre-region stretch or P2's 25th-percentile cast removal.

steps.step: Coarse sign-family outline search over a fixed placement grid (rim colour vs interior vs surround), best placement kept
steps.note: N1 correlates 14 family templates at 72 placements. N2 compares 8 family frames at 36 positions. N3 slides 8 outline references over 5x5 positions at 5 sizes. All work on a 16x16 colour grid, as the programs do on 16x16 or 18x18. Unlike the programs, N3 keeps the best per size instead of one overall best.

steps.step: Fine refinement of the fitted outline around the coarse best (hill climbing or a local adjustment grid over centre, size, shear)
steps.note: No network refines anything iteratively. N1 replaces it with an independent fixed grid of 90 poses. N2 tries only 5 stretches and tilts for the frame. N3 has stretch and slant variants in the coarse search but nothing anchored on the coarse best.

steps.step: Rim vs interior contrast check (red or dark rim around a pale field)
steps.note: These are built into family colour templates (N1, N3 with the face weighted down) and into N2's inner brightness and colour region test. None makes a separate rim-sample vs inward-sample comparison along the fitted outline.

steps.step: Border completeness by sector (weakest part of rim must hold up)
steps.note: N2 checks 8 ring arcs against a threshold and averages 3 triangle sides. That matches P2's sectors in idea, but N2 counts missing arcs where P2 blends the mean with the minimum and P3 takes a low percentile. N1's 12-direction edge-orientation check along the outline might play this role but has no weakest-part logic.

steps.step: Keep or prune competing family hypotheses (P3 margin pruning to -20; P2 second distinct placement)
steps.note: The networks never prune and never search for a second distinct placement. Instead every class takes its own max over all poses, which keeps every hypothesis implicitly.

steps.step: Resample sign interior into the fitted sign frame
steps.note: The programs resample in the fitted frame (26x26, 25x25, 30x30). The networks resample at a fixed set of poses that are not fitted: N1 at 90 poses (24x24), N2 with a 19x19 straightened face at 36 positions, N3 on 50 unwarped canvases. Some network symbol matches (N1 central 20x20, N2 26x26, N3 24x24) use a fixed central window with no frame at all.

steps.step: Correlate interior with a bank of deformed synthetic pictograms, keep best deformation per class
steps.note: All build banks of normalised, mean-centred procedural drawings under scale, shear and shift, and take the max per class. The networks use banks of similar size.

steps.step: Edge or gradient version of the pictogram match
steps.note: The programs blend edge-direction or edge-difference correlation (0.67/0.33, 0.74/0.26). N3 matches 8 directional edge maps of the whole sign. N1 and N2 use band-pass (DoG) ink maps instead of edge directions.

steps.step: Ink-centred re-framing (centre of mass and spread of ink) with a second ink-framed bank
steps.note: No network measures where the ink sits in order to re-frame. N1's search over candidate number boxes is a fixed-grid stand-in for digit framing only.

steps.step: Speed-limit reading with digit or whole-string templates at fixed layouts and scales
steps.note: N1 searches 288 boxes and 32 variants per limit. N2 slides typeset strings ±4 px over a central patch. N3 uses numeral and close-up digit-region references weighted towards the informative digit, which is close to P3's lead and trail digit weighting. All of them read in fixed windows or poses rather than the fitted frame.

steps.step: Digit segmentation by ink projection and cut at the emptiest column
steps.note: N2 compares the left-to-right ink profile with stored profiles but makes no adaptive cut.

steps.step: Blank-interior test for plain signs (no vehicles, yield, priority)
steps.note: All use interior texture, spread or detail as a penalty or bonus. The networks add fixed class offsets.

steps.step: Colour cues: red car on left for no passing, lamp colours at fixed heights for traffic lights
steps.note: N1 and N2 have explicit region tests. N3 has only whole-sign colour references that contain these colours.

steps.step: Diamond side or trim check for priority road
steps.note: N2 matches yellow resampled into a diamond against 3 outline sizes. N1 and N3 rely on family or whole-sign templates. None checks per-side gradients.

steps.step: Stop or no-entry corner redness and bar region test
steps.note: N2 checks for a light bar between red flanks. N1 and N3 rely on colour layout templates. None tests corner quadrants.

steps.step: End-of diagonal stripe evidence
steps.note: N1 probes the stripe at 3 angles and takes the weaker end. N2 checks both stripe ends and takes the weaker. N3 has the stripe only inside its templates. P3's crescent-only matching that excludes the diagonal is in no network.

steps.step: Whole-sign colour layout comparison per class
steps.note: All three networks match rendered full signs (frame plus symbol) per class.

steps.step: Deformable parts match for warning pictograms
steps.note: N1 shifts 3 parts. N3 has 4 blob parts. P3 uses 5 sub-regions with small displacements.

steps.step: Measure border blur and penalise templates at mismatched blur
steps.note: No network estimates blur from the image.

steps.step: Weighted sum of shape and content evidence, argmax over classes
steps.note: The programs fix one placement per family and then add content. The networks sum the evidence per pose or size and take the best pose per class, so each class can pick its own pose.

steps.step: Blurred second pass when the top two scores are within a margin
steps.note: No network branches on intermediate results.

network_only.step: Per-class joint pose selection: all evidence is summed per pose (or size) and each class takes its own best pose. The programs instead commit to one fitted placement per shape family.
Band-pass (pixel minus Gaussian surround) detail maps used as the ink signal, re-standardised and clipped.
The family's best frame score is added to every position hypothesis.
Speed-number scores are expressed relative to the average reading over all 8 limits.
Fixed per-class constant offsets (for example no vehicles +1.05 or +1.65, yield +0.5 or +1.35, stop -0.35). P3 has only small family offsets and +0.15 for end signs.
Family silhouette templates split into 14 families (separate no-passing, truck no-passing, end 80 and similar layouts) instead of 8 outline shapes.
