cover.verdict: The networks use the same broad recipe as the programs: log opponent colour maps, a coarse 8-family outline search on a 16x16 grid, correlation against large banks of deformed procedural pictograms with the best kept per class, digit-string templates for speed limits, blank-face, stripe and lamp cues, and a weighted sum followed by argmax. Several hand-tuned constants match in role and nearly in value (log offset about 0.02 to 0.027, symbol mask radii 0.745/0.82/0.9 vs 0.755/0.85/0.91, interior 0.7, rim edge 0.775 vs 0.765). They are not the same computation, though. Every adaptive step in the programs becomes a fixed grid plus max: hill-climb or local outline refinement, one committed placement per family, ink-centred re-framing, projection-based digit segmentation, P3's family pruning, the blur-mismatch penalty, sector-weakest rim scoring and P1's blurred second pass are all replaced by fixed pose grids or missing, and each class picks its own pose instead of sharing one fitted sign frame.

d.summary: This is a hand-built rule system, not a learned matcher. It samples the galaxy's light and colour on a polar grid around the image centre (9 radii by 24 directions), subtracts the sky and caps each sample relative to the central brightness. From this grid it derives about forty interpretable measurements: elongation, isophote shapes, spiral winding and pitch, lopsidedness, colour, concentration, one-sided tails, and off-centre secondary peaks or nuclei. Hand-tuned linear rules with thresholds then turn these into scores, first splitting smooth from structured galaxies, then picking a sub-class within each family, alongside separate scores for edge-on, merging and disturbed.
d.references: none. There are no stored templates or prototypes. The fixed sampling patterns are all generated analytically: 216 elongated Gaussian sampling spots on 9 rings by 24 directions for each of brightness and colour, a sky annulus, Gaussian smoothing kernels, and cosine and sine angular patterns. Every class rule uses hand-picked coefficients.

stages.name: Polar photometry around the centre
stages.computes: Averages the image 2 by 2, then measures brightness (a weighted mix of the three bands) and a colour difference (first band minus third band) in small elongated Gaussian spots. The spots sit on 9 rings at 24 directions around the image centre, and they widen radially and tangentially with radius. Sky level is measured in a broad annulus near the frame edge.

key_numbers.meaning: ring radii in original 128-pixel image pixels, roughly logarithmic spacing
directions per ring (15 degree steps)
sky annulus radius and width, original pixels
band weights forming the brightness channel

stages.name: Sky subtraction and central-brightness capping
stages.computes: Takes the central brightness as the mean of the two innermost rings minus sky. Subtracts sky from every spot and clips it to the range from zero up to a radius-dependent multiple of the central brightness, so bright stars or neighbours cannot dominate. The colour channel is carried alongside the brightness and clipped the same way.

key_numbers.meaning: cap on each spot as a multiple of central brightness, r = ring radius in pixels
extra allowance above the cap, image intensity units

stages.name: Ring profiles, angular harmonics and asymmetry
stages.computes: For each ring it computes the mean brightness, the colour, and the strength of 1- to 5-fold angular patterns. It also measures point-to-opposite-point brightness differences (rotational asymmetry). From these it derives ellipticity at inner, middle, outer and large scales, as 2-fold strength relative to the local radial brightness slope. It also derives odd-fold (3 and 5) structure, and the twist of the 2-fold pattern angle between rings 2 to 4 rings apart.

key_numbers.meaning: characteristic radii (pixels) of the radial weightings for inner, mid, outer and large elongation
phase samples used to estimate each pattern's strength independent of orientation

stages.name: Isophote shapes along 12 diameters
stages.computes: At 4 brightness levels set as fractions of the central brightness, it finds the radius along each of 12 diameters where the brightness falls to that level. Only light present on both sides of the centre counts. For each level it keeps the longest diameter (the major axis length) and the largest log length difference between a diameter and the one perpendicular to it (the axis ratio). It also measures how irregularly these profiles change between levels (warp), and the concentration from the outer and inner major-axis radii.

key_numbers.meaning: isophote levels as fractions of central brightness
diameters searched for the major axis (15 degree steps)

stages.name: Colour measures
stages.computes: Computes core, disk and outer red-versus-blue log ratios as weighted ring averages. The disk and outer colours are mostly taken from light that appears on both sides of the centre, so one-sided contaminants are ignored.

key_numbers.meaning: core colour region

key_numbers.value: radius weightings peaking about 14 px (inner cut 6) and 22 px (inner cut 9 to 10)
key_numbers.meaning: disk and outer colour regions

stages.name: Spiral winding and pitch
stages.computes: Predicts each ring's 2-fold and 3-fold pattern from the next inner ring three ways: unrotated, or rotated as a logarithmic spiral with 36 degree or 18 degree pitch in either sense. It keeps the better sense for each pitch and measures the leftover mismatch. Winding is how much better the best spiral fits than no rotation. Pitch says whether the tighter or the more open spiral fits better.

key_numbers.meaning: trial spiral pitch angles
expected fraction of the 2-fold or 3-fold pattern strength that carries over from one ring to the next
clip on the winding measure

stages.name: Tails, rebrightening and connected light
stages.computes: Detects outward rebrightening along a direction (an outer ring brighter than 0.87 times the inner one), and separately counts the cases with no match on the opposite side, which signal tidal features. It finds narrow radial ridges that stand out from their sides, have no counterpart opposite, and continue across adjacent rings (streams). Following each direction outward, it keeps only light that grows by at most 27 percent per ring, so it stays connected to the centre. It then measures that connected light's lopsidedness and its 1-sided dipole.

key_numbers.meaning: outer-to-inner ring brightness ratio above which a direction counts as rebrightening
allowed outward growth factor and offset for light to count as connected to the centre
flank positions (45 and 75 degrees) used to judge ridge prominence

stages.name: Secondary peaks and second nuclei
stages.computes: At quarter resolution it smooths the brightness at two scales and marks points brighter than all 8 neighbours at 2 or 3 cells (local maxima prominence). It keeps the strongest such peak in each distance annulus from the centre. A finer version on the half-resolution image keeps peaks that curve downward in every direction and drops star-like point sources. It requires a dip between the peak and the centre, plus diffuse light bridging them halfway (a second nucleus inside a common envelope). The strongest candidate per annulus is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: annuli from the centre for companion peak search (original pixels)
annuli for the second-nucleus search
smoothing widths on the half-resolution grid (about 2, 3.7, 6 original pixels) for the nucleus search
down-weighting of more distant annuli for second nuclei

stages.name: Family scores
stages.computes: Forms hand-weighted, clipped combinations. Edge-on: large axis ratio at the faint isophotes, 2-fold strength and a long major axis. Structured (spiral rather than smooth): blue disk, core-to-disk colour gradient, extent, odd-fold structure, twist, winding, warp, rebrightening and bar evidence. Bar: inner elongation beyond the outer elongation, plus elongation localized to one radius band. Loose: blue colour, low concentration, a weak centre and a pitch favouring 36 degrees. Bulge: red core, central contrast and concentration. Merger: companion peaks, second nuclei, asymmetry and red disk. Disturbed: tails, asymmetry and connected dipole, minus second nuclei.

key_numbers.meaning: axis-ratio pivot for edge-on evidence
faint-isophote major-axis pivot for disk size
asymmetry pivot for merger and disturbed evidence

d.decision: The highest of 10 scores wins. Disturbed, merger and both edge-on scores are used directly. The edge-on pair is split by bulge evidence: a positive bulge score penalises the no-bulge class, and a negative one penalises the with-bulge class. The three smooth classes are penalised by any positive structured score, and the three spiral classes by any negative one. Within the smooth family, a combined flattening measure picks round (below 0.24), in-between (0.24 to log 2.05) or cigar (above log 2.05). The chosen sub-class scores 0 and the others score negative. The smooth classes are also penalised when the edge-on score exceeds about minus 0.1. Within the spiral family the choice works the same way: barred if the bar score is highest, otherwise tight or loose by the sign of the loose score.
d.adapts_per_image: There is no search over scales or positions of the galaxy, and no iteration: everything is centred on the image centre at fixed radii. It still adapts per image in several ways. Sky level and central brightness are measured on each image, and almost every measure is normalised by them, including the brightness caps and the isophote levels. The major axis comes from the best of 12 diameters at each level. The spiral sense comes from the better of two rotation directions at each pitch. Companion peaks and second nuclei come from a maximum within each distance annulus. Connected light is traced outward ray by ray, depending on the previous ring. The final rules branch on intermediate results through clipped and max/min combinations: smooth versus structured gating, and the within-family winner.

d.summary: This is a hand-built set of rules, with no learned parts. It finds the galaxy's nucleus, then traces its outline at 11 brightness levels and fits an ellipse to each. It then unrolls the disk into rings and measures shape, flattening, colour gradient, winding spiral patterns, bar-like inner elongation, lopsidedness and nearby companion galaxies. A fixed ordered series of yes or no tests on scores built from these measurements gives the class: merger, then edge-on (with or without bulge), then disturbed, then smooth (round, in-between, cigar), then barred spiral, then loose versus tight spiral.
d.references: None. Nothing is stored that depicts a galaxy class. The only fixed patterns are made up as needed: ideal logarithmic spiral phase patterns at fixed pitch angles (6 pitches from 10 to 50 degrees, for 2, 3 and 4 arms, both handednesses, in 3 radial windows), and ellipse shapes fitted to each image. All thresholds and weights are hand-set constants. (build.py only writes the classifier source to disk, and that copy keeps its explanatory comments.)

stages.name: Sky removal and noise level
stages.computes: For each colour band, it takes the median brightness of the outer frame and subtracts it. It mixes the bands into one grey image and makes three blurred copies of it at different scales. Noise is a robust spread of grey-image brightness in the outer frame, with a small floor.

key_numbers.meaning: pixels farther than this from the frame centre count as sky
how much each of the three bands counts in the grey image
blur widths of the fine, medium and broad copies

stages.name: Locate nucleus
stages.computes: It takes the brightest point of the medium-blurred image, but brightness counts for less the farther it is from the frame centre. Three rounds of a local weighted centroid then refine this to a fraction of a pixel. Pixels below 13% of the central value are left out. The brightness at the result is the reference 'peak'.

key_numbers.meaning: preference for the frame centre: drops by a factor e at about 7.7 px from centre
widths of the three refinement windows
fraction of the central brightness below which pixels are ignored when refining

stages.name: Trace outlines at several brightness levels
stages.computes: From the nucleus it casts 128 rays out to 85 px. On each ray it finds the first point where brightness falls below each of 11 levels, measured as fractions of the peak, and does not rise back. Each outline is smoothed by a median over 5 neighbouring rays. An ellipse is fitted to each outline (axis ratio, angle, size), keeping how far the outline departs from the ellipse and how far it is from point-symmetric. The 'outer' outline is the level nearest 8.5% of peak.

key_numbers.meaning: brightness levels at which outlines are traced; never lower than 2.4 times the noise
how finely outward distance is sampled
level that sets the galaxy's outer size, flattening and orientation

stages.name: Unroll the disk into rings
stages.computes: It samples the image on 52 ellipses scaled to the outer outline. Their sizes run from 0.07 to 1.5 times its long axis, with the flattening kept no thinner than 0.16, at 128 angles each. Brightness on each ring becomes contrast against the ring's median. It breaks the variation around each ring into 1, 2, 3 and more fold patterns. Rings are weighted by how far above noise they are. The blue band gets the same treatment.

key_numbers.meaning: ring sizes as a fraction of the outer outline's long axis, spaced evenly in log size
thinnest flattening allowed when unrolling, so edge-on disks are not stretched without limit

stages.name: Spiral and winding measures
stages.computes: It checks how well the 2, 3 and 4 fold patterns rotate steadily with log radius, as ideal logarithmic spirals would. The tight score is the best match at 19 degrees or less, the open score at 26 degrees or more. A second winding score follows how the 2 to 10 fold patterns turn from one ring to a ring 2, 4 or 6 steps out. That score is calibrated against four empty sky patches in the same image. It also estimates the local arm direction and pitch from brightness gradients in the unrolled disk.

key_numbers.meaning: range of spiral pitch angles tried
pitch dividing 'tight' from 'open' winding
off-galaxy places used to measure how much winding noise alone produces

stages.name: Colour, profile and structure
stages.computes: Core colour (red band minus blue band over their sum) comes from rings at 0.07 to 0.22 of the outer size, disk colour from 0.52 to 0.92, and the gradient is their difference. It also measures: how lumpy the rings are beyond what noise explains (3 to 10 fold patterns); lopsidedness (1 fold pattern and point asymmetry of the outlines); whether outline centres drift outward; brightness 'shoulders' in the radial profile; and how large the bright body is compared with the faint wings.

key_numbers.meaning: ring zones, as fractions of the outer size, for core and disk colour
used as the size of the bright body, compared with the outer size

stages.name: Bar detection
stages.computes: Inner outlines (levels 2 to 5) are compared with the outer disk, allowing for tilt, to see whether they are more elongated. The elongated part must reach 10 to 78% of the outer size and keep a steady angle. It also looks for a 2 fold pattern that is straight in the inner rings and then changes beyond its end.

key_numbers.meaning: allowed bar length as a fraction of the outer long axis
inner outlines must be flatter than this axis ratio to count

stages.name: Companion search
stages.computes: It finds local brightness peaks more than 4 px from the nucleus and less than 62 px from the frame centre, and keeps up to 18 ranked by brightness and closeness. For each, it measures: the dip in brightness along the line to the nucleus; its own size and wings; brightness relative to the nucleus; a plausible galaxy-like colour; colour likeness to the nucleus; distance relative to both galaxies' sizes; light bridging the dip compared with the opposite side of the main galaxy; and whether it still stands out after the mirror-image patch on the far side is subtracted. The best candidate's combined score is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: closest distance to the nucleus and farthest distance from the frame centre for candidates
brightness relative to the nucleus at which a companion counts as comparable
candidates fainter than this, or with less dip between them and the nucleus, are dropped
most candidates checked

stages.name: Edge-on tests
stages.computes: Thinness comes from the flattest outer outlines and how pointed the outline is along its long axis. It also measures whether the vertical thickness swells at the centre, compared with positions 13 to 61% of the way out along the long axis. A thin bright line of light along the long axis, against light just off it, also counts. For edge-on cases, bulge evidence combines a thicker centre, a central brightness spike, a red core and a core redder than the disk line.

key_numbers.meaning: outer axis ratio at which the thinness score crosses zero
positions along the long axis, as a fraction of the outer size, used for the thickness profile
core colour around which the bulge score is centred

d.decision: The class comes from a fixed order of threshold tests on hand-weighted sums of the scores. First, merger (1) if the companion score plus disorder is high, or if the galaxy is very irregular with a red, luminous core and a weaker companion. Then edge-on if thinness is positive and irregularity is not too high: 9 if the bulge score is above 0, otherwise 8. Then disturbed (0) if the irregularity score (lopsided, drifting, blue, not winding) is positive and also above 0.85, or disk evidence is low, or lopsidedness clearly beats the spiral signal, or the galaxy is very blue. Then smooth if disk evidence (spiral, structure, colour gradient, bar, size) is below 0: round (2) if axis ratio is above 0.79, cigar (4) if a combined axis ratio is below 0.43, otherwise in-between (3). Then barred spiral (5) if the bar score minus a penalty for open arms is above 0.33 and the bar keeps a steady angle. Otherwise, a loose-versus-tight score (open minus tight winding, measured pitch, arm contrast, small bright body) picks 7 if above 0, else 6.
d.adapts_per_image: A great deal adapts to each image. Sky level and noise are measured on each image's outer frame. Every brightness level is a fraction of that image's own peak. The nucleus is searched for and refined by repeated centroiding. Outline radii are found along each ray. The ring grid is scaled and turned to the fitted outer ellipse. Spiral matching keeps the best pitch, handedness and radial window. Winding is calibrated against that image's own empty sky patches. The companion search ranks and keeps up to 18 local peaks and the best of them. Edge-on bar strength is the best over 9 nearby angles. The final class comes from a branching series of tests on these image-specific measurements.

d.summary: A hand-built feature extractor that measures the central galaxy's brightness profile and shape from the image: axis ratio and size from light moments and isophotes, bars and spiral arms from angular harmonics, ring profiles and log-spiral matching, off-centre bright cores, colour gradients, and how well ellipses fit. It also finds the best-matching rendered model galaxy from several template families. Hand-weighted formulas turn these into ten class scores, built from soft thresholds and with shape gates (roundness bands, flatness), and the highest score wins. Nothing is learned from data.
d.references: Yes. Rendered synthetic galaxy images on a 24 x 24 grid with 3 original-pixel spacing (about 72 px across, centred), filtered and normalised to zero mean and unit spread so they can be compared by correlation. There are 9 families, each rendered over axis ratios, position angles and scale lengths. (1) Plain exponential disk plus a core, 108 images. (2) Disk with a bar, at 10 bar angles and 2 bar lengths, 720. (3) Tight two-armed log spirals, pitch 12 or 21 deg, both handednesses, 10 phases, 1440. (4) Loose spirals, pitch 30 or 45 deg, 1440. (5) Smooth Sersic-like ellipses, axis ratio 0.33 to 1, 16 angles, 5 sizes, 2 profile shapes, 810. (6) Thin edge-on disks, axis ratio 0.12 to 0.29, 240. (7) Edge-on disks with a central bulge, 480. (8) Single nucleus, 104. (9) Two nuclei 6 to 33 px apart at 16 angles with 2 brightness ratios, 640. There are other fixed masks (Gaussian apertures, rings, sectors, a log-polar sampling grid, and 51 ellipse models of 6 axis ratios times 10 angles, sampled at 12 sizes and 16 points), but these are measurement apertures, not depictions of classes.

stages.name: Downsample, smooth and convert to brightness
stages.computes: Averages 2x2 blocks (to 64x64) and blurs slightly. Combines the three colour bands into one brightness image with fixed weights. A clipped version keeps only light between a faint level and a bright cap.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of the three colour bands in the brightness image
assumed sky level: light below it is ignored in the clipped image (pixel intensity, 0 to 1 scale)
cap above which light is not counted further (same scale)

stages.name: Elongation and size from light moments
stages.computes: Takes second moments of the clipped light (spread along x, y and the diagonals) within Gaussian windows of several sizes, and turns them into an axis ratio at each scale. Growth of flux from the small to the large window measures how big the galaxy is. The axis ratios of smaller or larger windows are blended according to that size.

key_numbers.meaning: Gaussian window radii in original pixels
flux-growth ranges (13 px window vs 5 px) that switch to larger-scale axis ratios

stages.name: Isophote shape and extent
stages.computes: Samples brightness on a log-polar grid around the centre. At several brightness levels it marks which samples are above the level, then measures how elongated that region is and how large. It repeats this on a sky-subtracted image (local sky taken from an annulus) at three levels. These give the final axis ratio q, an area, and a length (area divided by q) that flags long thin disks.

key_numbers.meaning: log-polar sampling grid around the image centre
brightness levels for the isophotes on the raw image
brightness levels above the local sky for the sky-subtracted isophotes
annulus used to estimate the local sky

stages.name: Ring harmonics: bar, arms, winding, asymmetry
stages.computes: On 8 rings it measures mean light and the strength of 1, 2, 3 and 4-fold angular patterns relative to the mean. A strong 2-fold pattern inside that fades outside means a bar. A 2-fold pattern that grows outward means arms. A 2-fold phase that rotates between neighbouring rings means winding. 3-fold and 4-fold patterns mean structure and boxiness. Differences between opposite sectors at 4 radii measure lopsidedness (inner) and clumpiness (outer).

key_numbers.meaning: ring radii (8 rings)
radii for inner lopsidedness / outer clumpiness
bar-contrast range mapped to 0..1 bar evidence

stages.name: Spiral and ring searches in polar coordinates
stages.computes: Each ring is normalised to zero mean and unit spread, then compared with logarithmic spiral patterns: 2 or 3 arms, pitch 0 to 55 deg, both handednesses, 8 phases, over sliding radial windows. The best response for each pitch is kept, giving tight versus open spiral power. It also finds places where brightness rises going outward, preferring a rise at the same radius on both opposite sides (symmetric arms or rings), and bumps above the radial trend (ridges).

key_numbers.meaning: pitch angles counted as tight vs open
radial window length for spiral matching
brightness rise or bump needed before a ridge counts

stages.name: Ellipse-fit residuals
stages.computes: Samples brightness at 16 points around ellipses of 51 shape and orientation models and 12 sizes. For each model it measures how much brightness varies around the ellipse: total, the part shared by opposite points (even, spiral or bar-like) and the part that differs between them (odd, asymmetric). Within inner, middle, outer and whole-body radial weightings it keeps the best-fitting model, overall and within the thin, intermediate, round and flat groups. The leftover residuals, scaled by central flux, measure arms and disorder, and how much worse round or intermediate models fit (signs of a bar or a flat disk).

key_numbers.meaning: axis ratios of the ellipse models
ellipse semi-major axes
centres of the inner, middle, outer and body radial weightings

stages.name: Off-centre cores (merger evidence)
stages.computes: On a 32x32 coarse image it finds spots that curve downward in every direction (compact bright peaks) at two blur sizes. It compares peak strength away from the centre (annuli 6 to 36 px) with the central peak. Separately it compares the brightest sample at 12 to 28 px from the centre with the central brightness, after subtracting sky.

key_numbers.meaning: peak-detector blur widths in coarse pixels (4 original px each)
peak strength above which an off-centre peak counts as conspicuous
central, inner and remote zones for peak counts

stages.name: Colour and concentration
stages.computes: Measures sky-subtracted aperture flux and red-minus-blue colour at several sizes. This gives overall warmth (red means bulge-like, blue means star-forming), the centre-to-outskirt colour gradient, rings bluer than the centre colour predicts (blue arms), and light concentration (small aperture flux vs larger ones).

key_numbers.meaning: aperture radii
ring radii for the arm colour excess
colour-gradient range mapped to 0..1 disk evidence

stages.name: Template matching
stages.computes: Filters a 24x24 sample of the central light, normalises it, and correlates it with every stored rendering. It keeps the best correlation per family. Comparing families gives evidence such as bar over spiral, tight over loose, any spiral over a plain disk, smooth fit quality, edge-on over smooth, bulging over thin edge-on, and double over single nucleus.

key_numbers.meaning: grid spacing of the 24x24 central sample
smooth-model correlation range mapped to regular-ness

stages.name: Class scoring
stages.computes: Each class score is a hand-weighted sum of soft-ramped evidence. Smooth classes 2, 3 and 4 are each penalised outside a band of axis ratio. Spirals 5, 6 and 7 share a disk score and are split by bar and loose evidence. Edge-on 8 and 9 share a flatness score and are split by bulge evidence. Mergers use off-centre peaks and the double-nucleus match. Disturbed uses chaos, lopsidedness and irregularity minus the merger evidence.

key_numbers.meaning: axis ratio favoured for round smooth (class 2)
axis-ratio band favoured for in-between smooth (class 3)
axis-ratio band favoured for cigar-shaped (class 4)
axis ratio above which the edge-on score is cut sharply

d.decision: The class with the highest of the ten hand-weighted scores wins. The scores were revised in several rounds, and only the last version of each is used. Small final adjustments follow: ridge evidence moves score from the smooth classes to the spiral classes, and the off-centre-peak ratio raises the merger score when it agrees with merger or lopsided evidence.
d.adapts_per_image:
Yes, in several ways:
- **Best match kept:** it keeps the best of many options per image: best template per family, best ellipse model per radial weighting and shape group, best spiral pitch, phase and radial window, the strongest ridge or rise over angles and radii, the brightest off-centre sample, and the strongest ring harmonic over radii.
- **Size sets the scale:** the measured flux growth decides which window scales' axis ratios are used.
- **Measured normalisation:** quantities are divided by fluxes measured on that image (ring means, aperture fluxes, central peak), and local sky is subtracted from an annulus on the same image.
- **Per-image normalising:** each ring is normalised separately before spiral matching, and the template comparisons normalise the image patch.
- **No iteration:** nothing repeats until it converges. The computation is a single pass, and its shape gates are soft.

d.summary: The method takes a sky-subtracted brightness profile along 48 rays from the image centre, scales it by the central peak brightness, and cuts it off wherever light rises again after a dip, so that neighbouring objects are dropped. From this cleaned central galaxy it measures isophote shapes at several brightness levels (ellipticity, axis ratio, lopsidedness, higher-order distortions, twist of orientation between levels), colours in nested apertures, logarithmic-spiral arm patterns, small-scale knots and gaps, asymmetry, secondary peaks and pairs of separate nuclei. Hand-set formulas then combine these into one score per class, with shared smooth/spiral/edge-on base terms and class-specific tie-breakers.
d.references: No stored drawings or prototypes of the classes. The only fixed patterns are measurement probes generated analytically: 29 x 48 polar sampling spots (Gaussian, growing with radius) on rays from the centre; 8 border sky sectors; Gaussian and ring apertures for colour photometry; 14 ellipse families (circular, plus axis ratios 0.73, 0.48 and 0.3 at 6, 8 and 10 orientations) sampled on 12 rings, for two-armed-pattern analysis; ideal logarithmic-spiral phase patterns at 3 pitch angles x 8 radial windows x 2 windings x 8 phases (384), plus 64 non-winding counterparts; second-derivative line/blob detectors at 8 orientations and 2 scales; centre-versus-surround and point-source tests on a 21 x 21 grid of candidate nucleus positions; and 36 half-plane splits per separation scale for pairing nuclei.

stages.name: Downsample, brightness, sky level
stages.computes: Averages 2x2 pixel blocks and forms a single brightness image weighting the red, green and blue channels. The sky level for each colour is the mean of the darkest of 8 angular sectors near the frame border, and it is subtracted.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of red (z), green (r), blue (g) channels in the brightness image
radius (original pixels from centre) beyond which border sky sectors are measured; 8 sectors of 45 degrees

stages.name: Polar profile and peak scaling
stages.computes: Samples brightness on 48 rays at 29 radii out to about 61 px with small elongated spots that widen with radius. The central peak is the maximum within 3.5 px of the centre, and every sample is divided by it (plus a small floor).

key_numbers.meaning: radial sampling range in original pixels (about 32 arcsec)
radius within which the central peak brightness is taken
floor added to peak brightness before dividing (image intensity units)

stages.name: Isolate the central galaxy along each ray
stages.computes: Takes the running minimum of brightness from the centre outward on each ray. Wherever light rises well above that minimum (more than 1.65 times it plus 0.018 of peak), it is clipped, which removes detached neighbours. The rise above the running minimum is kept separately as evidence of companions or arm crests.

key_numbers.meaning: cap on brightness after a dip, as a fraction of central peak
valley depth (fraction of peak) below which a later rise counts as separated by empty sky and is penalised

stages.name: Isophote shape at several levels
stages.computes: For 7 brightness levels it finds the radius where each ray drops below the level, smooths over neighbouring angles and averages each ray with its opposite to get a diameter profile. On the log of these it takes the mean size, the 2-, 4- and 6-fold angular components (ellipticity, boxiness), the 1-, 3- and 5-fold components of the radius (lopsidedness, odd distortions), and the longest and shortest diameter.

key_numbers.meaning: 7 isophote levels relative to the central peak
relative softness of each level cut

stages.name: Faint outer contours
stages.computes: Repeats the contour measurement on the profile without peak scaling, at 3 fixed surface-brightness levels after a similar companion clip. It takes the angular components 0 to 5 of the log radius, which show faint tails, outer elongation and outer lopsidedness.

key_numbers.meaning: absolute brightness levels above sky (image intensity units 0 to 1)
companion cut on the unscaled profile

stages.name: Point asymmetry and colours
stages.computes: Measures how much brighter each point is than the point opposite it through the centre, averaged in 4 annuli. Also measures sky-subtracted light per colour in a central spot and in 4 rings, giving red-minus-blue colours, colour gradient, green excess and blue outer halo.

key_numbers.meaning: annuli for the asymmetry measure
scales of the central and ring colour apertures

stages.name: Two-armed spiral search
stages.computes: Over 14 assumed tilts and orientations of a disc, it measures the two-fold angular pattern of brightness on 12 rings and compares it with ideal logarithmic spirals of 3 pitch angles in 8 radial windows, both winding directions, all phases. It keeps the best match, the advantage over a non-winding elongated pattern, and the difference between winding senses.

key_numbers.meaning: spiral pitch angles tested
radius range of the 12 rings (log-spaced)
disc axis ratios assumed besides face-on
weight of the non-winding pattern subtracted from spiral evidence

stages.name: Knots and inter-arm gaps
stages.computes: On a 4x4-block image, curvature detectors at 8 orientations and 2 scales find compact bright knots (dimmer in every direction around them) and dark gaps along the circumferential direction. These are averaged in 3 rings around the centre and compared with local brightness.

key_numbers.meaning: two detector scales in original pixels
radii of the rings where knots and gaps are counted
gap strength needed relative to local brightness

stages.name: Companions and double nuclei
stages.computes: Along each ray it finds the strongest rise after a dip (companion crest) in 3 radius ranges, plus arm crests above 0.025 of peak. On a 21 x 21 grid of positions spaced 4 px apart it scores compact local peaks, playing down point-like stars and peaks without a surrounding halo. Over half-plane splits at 6 angles and 3 offsets it keeps the fainter of the two best peaks on either side, then the best split, giving the strength of a second nucleus. It also finds the strongest extended secondary peak at 3 distance ranges.

key_numbers.meaning: spacing and extent of candidate nucleus positions
minimum separation scales for nucleus pairs
distance ranges searched for secondary peaks
radius ranges searched for companion crests on rays

stages.name: Hand-set class scores
stages.computes: Combines the features with soft threshold ramps into scores. A 'structured' score (lopsidedness, odd distortions, irregularity, twist, arms, blue colour, colour gradient, size, spiral winding, knots, gaps, blue halo) raises the spiral classes and lowers the smooth ones. Flatness and length give edge-on. Within each group: round vs in-between vs cigar by elongation and length; bulge vs no bulge by outer-minus-inner elongation, ridge and colour; barred by inner elongation, inner vs outer ellipticity and orientation change; loose vs tight by blueness, odd modes, open pitch and faintness; merging by nucleus pair, secondary peaks, asymmetry and bending; disturbed by faint tails, bending, faintness, compactness and off-centre peak.

key_numbers.meaning: elongation (log axis measure) splitting round from in-between smooth galaxies
elongation at which the cigar score peaks
major-axis length range that raises the edge-on score
flatness range over which the spiral score is reduced in favour of edge-on

d.decision: The class with the highest of the ten hand-built scores is chosen. Each score is a shared group term (smooth, spiral or edge-on, or standalone for merger and disturbed) plus a capped class-specific term: roundness for the smooth classes, bar or looseness for the spirals, bulge for the edge-ons. No learned or nearest-reference comparison is used.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes. The sky level comes from the darkest border sector of the image. All profiles are divided by the image's own central peak brightness. A running minimum along each ray decides where to cut off neighbouring light. Isophote radii are found per image at levels relative to its peak. The spiral search keeps the best match over 14 disc tilts and orientations, 8 radial windows, phases and windings. Curvature detectors take the best of 8 orientations. The nucleus-pair search takes maxima and minima over 441 positions and 36 half-plane splits per scale. Companion searches take the maximum over rays and radii.

d.summary: The method is a hand-built rule cascade over measured galaxy morphology, with nothing learned. It finds the central galaxy, traces its brightness contours and fits ellipses to them, then unrolls the disk into a face-on view and measures arm-like angular patterns, bar elongation, colour and shape. Weighted evidence scores for merger, edge-on, disturbed, spiral, barred and loose arms are each checked against a cutoff in a fixed order, and the first one that passes decides the class.
d.references: There are no stored images or prototypes. The only reference bank is generated by a formula: ideal logarithmic spiral patterns at 9 winding rates (0.75 to 11.3), in both handednesses, for 1, 2, 3 and 4 arms. That makes 72 patterns, and the measured angular structure of the face-on disk is compared against each of them. Every other comparison uses hand-set thresholds.

stages.name: Clean and measure the sky
stages.computes: Each colour band is lightly blurred. The sky level per band is the median of pixels far from the frame centre, and it is subtracted. Brightness is taken as a weighted mix of the three bands. A second, more blurred brightness image is also made. Sky noise is estimated from the spread of the same far-out pixels.

key_numbers.meaning: blur widths of the detail image and the broad image
pixels farther than this from the frame centre count as sky
how much the red(z), green(r) and blue(g) bands count toward brightness

stages.name: Locate the galaxy centre
stages.computes: It takes the brightest point of the broad image, favouring points near the frame centre. It then refines the position 4 times using the light centroid of nearby pixels brighter than a fraction of that peak, moving at most 1 px per step.

key_numbers.meaning: no centre preference within 3 px of the frame centre, then a soft falloff of about 9 px
fraction of peak brightness a pixel needs to count in the refinement
radius of the refinement window

stages.name: Trace brightness contours and fit ellipses
stages.computes: Along 128 rays from the centre, it finds where brightness first falls below each of 6 levels set relative to the core brightness. For each level it averages each ray with its opposite and fits an ellipse (size, axis ratio, orientation) in two passes that ignore overshooting rays. It then shifts the centre to the middle of the inner contours, by at most 3 px, and traces again.

key_numbers.meaning: contour levels as fractions of the core brightness, each at least 2.8 times the sky noise
maximum ray length, sampled every 0.5 px
a ray longer than 1.26 times the fitted ellipse is cut back to it (keeps stars from stretching contours)

stages.name: Disk geometry and face-on unrolling
stages.computes: The disk tilt and orientation come from the 33%, 21% and 13% contours together, and the disk size mostly from the outer two. The image is resampled on a grid that undoes the tilt, with rings at logarithmically spaced radii and 128 angles, giving a face-on map of radius versus angle.

key_numbers.meaning: how much the 3rd, 4th and 5th contours count toward disk tilt and orientation
allowed range of the disk radius (0.65 times the 13% contour size plus 0.35 times the 8% contour size)
radial span of the unrolled map, in disk radii (64 rings)

stages.name: Angular structure of the face-on disk
stages.computes: On each ring, bright outliers such as stars are capped and the ring is scaled by its mean. It then measures how strongly the light repeats 1 to 10 times around the ring, minus the expected noise level. From this come lopsidedness, odd-fold asymmetry, fine clumpy structure in the inner and outer disk, and how much the two-fold pattern rotates with radius. Tidal tails are found as light that exceeds the diametrically opposite side over a run of neighbouring angles at large radii.

key_numbers.meaning: outer zone used for lopsidedness and clumpy detail
inner zone
radii searched for tidal tail excess
cap for bright outliers on each ring, relative to the ring's typical spread

stages.name: Spiral arm detection
stages.computes: The ring patterns are compared with the generated left- and right-handed logarithmic spirals in two overlapping radial bands. Spiral strength is the best one-handed match, and tightness is the match-weighted average winding rate. Two other estimates come from the face-on map: the angle of bright ridges, found from the local curvature of brightness at two smoothing scales, and the direction of brightness changes, which gives arm pitch in degrees and how consistently the arms turn one way.

key_numbers.meaning: centres of the two radial bands used for spiral matching
range of spiral winding rates tested (9 values)
ridge angle range that counts as steep, open arms

stages.name: Bar detection
stages.computes: It looks for a consistent two-fold pattern in the inner disk at three radii, keeping the strongest. A pattern that continues to the disk edge, or that runs along the minor axis of a tilted disk, counts against a bar. Separately, it fits contours to the red band at fixed fractions of the red core brightness, undoes the disk tilt, and measures any leftover elongation (a stretched inner core).

key_numbers.meaning: radii tested for an inner two-fold pattern
red-band contour levels as fractions of the red core brightness
red contour size over which bar evidence is phased in

stages.name: Colour, concentration and contour shape
stages.computes: It measures the red-minus-blue colour (relative to green) of the core and of the outer disk, and the difference between them. It also measures several shape properties: how concentrated the light is (area of the 50% contour against the 13% contour), how fast the light fades at large radii, whether the contours have pointed or boxy ends, how lopsided the contours are, whether contours at neighbouring levels bulge or change colour the same way, and how faint outer contours lean to one side.

key_numbers.meaning: inside this is the core used for core colour
pair whose area ratio measures concentration
faint contour levels on the broad image used for one-sided extensions

stages.name: Edge-on thickness and bulge
stages.computes: It cuts across the disk at several points along its long axis and compares the thickness near the centre with the thickness further out. It also checks whether the centre is brighter than the brightness further along the long axis, extended inward, would predict. Both signal a central bulge.

key_numbers.meaning: positions along the long axis where thickness is measured
points along the long axis used to extend the disk brightness inward
range of central brightness over that inward estimate over which a bulge is phased in

stages.name: Companion search
stages.computes: It finds local brightness peaks away from the main core and ranks them by brightness, discounted by distance, keeping the top 18. Each is scored on several things: brightness relative to the main core, whether it is extended rather than star-like, distance compared with galaxy size, the dip in brightness along the line joining it to the core, colour similarity to the core, and extra faint light on that side compared with the opposite side. Peaks that lie along a thin disk, or are separate objects in clear sky, are penalised. The best score is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: a peak must be at least 3.2 px from the core and within 62 px of the frame centre
minimum brightness of a candidate peak
rings around each peak used to test whether it is extended
score above which the image is called a merger

d.decision: The class is decided by a fixed sequence of yes/no tests, and the first test that passes wins. (1) A companion score above 0.86 gives merging (1). (2) An edge-on score above 0.47, with disk axis ratio below 0.51 and visible axis ratio below 0.55, gives edge-on. A bulge score (warm core, pointed contours, central thickening, central excess) above 0.55 then gives 9, otherwise 8. (3) A disturbed score above 0.54 (lopsidedness, asymmetry, tails, blue core with no bulge, one-sided faint light, displaced centre) gives disturbed (0). (4) A spiral score below 0.41 gives smooth, split by visible axis ratio: above 0.814 is round (2), below 0.50 is cigar (4), anything between is in-between (3). (5) Otherwise a bar score above 0.44 gives barred spiral (5). (6) Otherwise a loose-arm score above 0.47 (open pitch, strong two-fold outer arms, lopsidedness, clumpy detail) gives loose spiral (7), else tight spiral (6).
d.adapts_per_image: A lot adapts to each image. The galaxy centre is found by a search followed by iterative refinement, then shifted to the middle of the contours. Sky level and noise are measured on each image. Contour levels are fractions of that image's own core brightness. The ellipse fits run twice, cutting back rays that overshoot. The face-on map is scaled to the measured disk size and tilt, so every radius-based zone is relative to that galaxy. The bar test keeps the strongest of three radii and the spiral strength keeps the best winding rate. The companion search ranks the local peaks found in that image and keeps the best-scoring one. The final class comes from a branching sequence of tests.

d.summary: A hand-built decision cascade over measured galaxy morphology. It finds the galaxy centre, traces its contours at several brightness levels and fits ellipses to them, unrolls the light along ellipses matched to the outer disk, and measures many hand-defined quantities: spiral winding, bar elongation, lopsidedness, tails, companion nuclei, edge-on thinness, colour gradients and profile shape. Fixed tests then pick the class in order: merger, then edge-on (with or without bulge), then disturbed, then disk (barred, or tight or loose unbarred spiral), and finally smooth galaxies split by roundness.
d.references: none. No stored templates, prototypes or lookup tables. Every threshold and weight is a hand-written constant. build.py only writes out the classifier source text, and that text matches solution.py apart from its comments.

stages.name: Clean-up and sky removal
stages.computes: Each colour channel is lightly blurred. A sky level is taken as the median of a border frame and subtracted. The channels are combined into one brightness map (0.30 of the first channel, 0.42 of the second, 0.28 of the third). A more heavily blurred copy is made too, and the noise level is estimated from the spread of the border pixels.

key_numbers.meaning: blur width (Gaussian sigma) in pixels, mimicking seeing
blur width in pixels for the broad map used to find nuclei
pixels from the image centre beyond which pixels (in x or y) count as border sky
weights of the three colour channels in the brightness map

stages.name: Find the galaxy centre
stages.computes: Takes the brightest point, weighted towards the image centre. It then refines that position six times, each time to the centroid of light within about 3 px whose brightness is well above the core level.

key_numbers.meaning: width in pixels of the preference for points near the image centre
window width in pixels for refining the centroid
fraction of peak brightness subtracted before centroiding

stages.name: Trace contours along rays and fit ellipses
stages.computes: Samples brightness along 128 directions out to 80 px. At 8 brightness levels it finds where each ray first drops below the level for good, then median-smooths those radii over neighbouring directions. From each contour it gets ellipse size, axis ratio and orientation, the asymmetry between opposite sides, and how far the contour departs from the fitted ellipse.

key_numbers.meaning: the 8 contour levels as fractions of central brightness
minimum contour level, in multiples of sky noise
maximum ray length in pixels, sampled every 0.5 px
cap on fitted ellipticity, so axis ratio is never below about 0.06

stages.name: Unroll the disk along ellipses
stages.computes: Uses the outer contours (levels 5 to 7) to set a reference ellipse. It samples the brightness map and the two outer colour channels on ellipses of that shape at 52 sizes spaced evenly in log radius, each with 128 angles. Each ring is divided by its median brightness, clipped, and broken into angular harmonics 1 to 8 (one-fold, two-fold and so on). Ring medians give radial brightness and colour profiles.

key_numbers.meaning: range of ring sizes as fractions of the outer contour's semi-major axis
allowed semi-major axis in pixels
clip on ring-relative contrast, limiting foreground stars

stages.name: Spiral and arc measures
stages.computes: Correlates angular harmonics 1 to 4 with logarithmic spirals at 9 winding rates in both senses, over three radial bands. This gives loose-arm strength (5 slowest rates), tight-arm strength, and overall wave strength. Separately it measures the local slant of brightness ridges in the unrolled chart over 3 radial zones and 8 angular sectors, giving arc strength, agreement of handedness, and the share of ridges that are open.

key_numbers.meaning: winding rates tested (rotation per unit log radius per fold); 2.75 or less counts as loose
radial window for the arc test, in units of outer semi-major axis
arc slant (pitch) range counted as open arms

stages.name: Companion nucleus search (merger test)
stages.computes: Finds local brightness peaks in the broad map within 62 px. For each peak at least 4.5 px from the centre it requires a brightness dip on the line back to the centre, enough brightness and a resolved half-width. It scores each candidate by separation relative to both cores' sizes, light bridging the gap, brightness similarity, saddle depth and core redness, and keeps the best score. A high enough score, or a moderate one combined with lopsidedness, odd harmonics, off-centre position or tails, gives merging galaxies.

key_numbers.meaning: minimum distance in pixels of a second peak from the centre
minimum companion brightness as a fraction of central brightness
minimum companion half-width in pixels (rules out point-like stars)
companion score that gives a merger on its own (0.30 or 0.20 with extra evidence)

stages.name: Edge-on disk test
stages.computes: Takes cuts across the major axis at many positions along it and measures half-brightness thickness, comparing thickness near the centre with thickness out on the disk. It measures two-sided length against width at a faint level, how far the faint contours reach, their flatness, light standing above the midplane near the centre, and the inner-to-outer axis-ratio change. If the galaxy is thin or long enough and not too lopsided, it is edge-on. A bulge score from central thickening, central excess, core redness, central light concentration and inner roundness then decides with or without bulge.

key_numbers.meaning: maximum thickness-to-length ratio for a thin disk
minimum two-sided extent in pixels for the disk rules
maximum mid-contour axis ratio for an edge-on call
bulge score above which the class is edge-on with bulge

stages.name: Disturbance test
stages.computes: Adds up evidence of irregularity: side-to-side contour asymmetry, odd-fold harmonics, the centre's offset from the frame centre, one-sided reach of faint light at three levels, faint plumes in a more heavily smoothed map, contour bending, and a blue core. Ordinary two-armed structure counts against it. Above a threshold, with supporting conditions and no strong coherent spiral, the galaxy is disturbed. A second route catches faint bent plumes or outer contours twisted against inner ones.

key_numbers.meaning: disturbance score threshold
brightness levels (fractions of central brightness) for measuring one-sided reach
blur width in pixels for the faint-plume map, scaled to galaxy size
outer-versus-inner contour twist that, with asymmetry, triggers disturbed

stages.name: Disk versus smooth decision
stages.computes: Builds a disk score from arm strength, a core redder than the outskirts, size, contour irregularity, bar evidence, blue outskirts, and a radial brightness profile shaped like an exponential rather than a steep cusp. Very regular elliptical contours count against it, as do small, bright, regular galaxies. A score above threshold, or a strong bar in a resolved irregular galaxy, sends the image to the spiral branch.

key_numbers.meaning: disk score threshold
semi-major axis in pixels over which a galaxy counts as increasingly resolved
geometric-mean radius in pixels over which size votes for a disk

stages.name: Bar test
stages.computes: Looks for a two-fold elongation in the inner rings of the outer colour channel that keeps a fixed orientation and stops or changes outside the inner part. It combines this with a change between inner and outer contour ellipses and a straight, two-sided ridge brighter than its flanks. It also checks redder light along the bar, and that a round bulge stretched by projection is not posing as a bar. The bar must beat the spiral wave and one-fold signals, and the disk must not be too inclined.

key_numbers.meaning: bar quality threshold, rising as arm openness grows
minimum outer axis ratio (not too inclined)
inner radial windows searched for the bar, in units of outer semi-major axis

stages.name: Tight versus loose arms
stages.computes: Builds an openness score from loose against tight winding strength, open arc share, odd-fold structure, fine structure, blue outskirts, a two-fold phase that holds its angle with radius, and outer blue two- and three-fold contrast. A concentrated core counts against it.

key_numbers.meaning: openness threshold above which arms are loose

stages.name: Smooth galaxy roundness
stages.computes: Blends the inner, middle and outer contour axis ratios, with a correction for seeing blur of about 1.65 px applied to the middle contour, and thresholds the result.

key_numbers.meaning: blended axis ratio above which the galaxy is round smooth
blended axis ratio above which it is in-between; below it, cigar-shaped
seeing blur in pixels removed from the contour size in the roundness correction

d.decision: An ordered cascade of hand-set threshold tests, where the first match wins. Merging galaxies (1) if a companion nucleus scores high enough. Next, edge-on: with bulge (9) if the bulge score is above 1.7, otherwise without bulge (8). Then disturbed (0) if the irregularity score or the plume/twist rules fire. If the disk score passes: barred spiral (5) if the bar tests pass, otherwise loose (7) or tight (6) unbarred spiral by the openness score. Anything left is a smooth galaxy: round (2), in-between (3) or cigar-shaped (4) by axis-ratio thresholds. Classes are chosen by these rules, not by comparing per-class scores.
d.adapts_per_image: Extensive. The centre is found by an iterative centroid search. Contour levels are set relative to that image's central brightness and sky noise. The reference ellipse (size, shape, orientation) used to unroll the disk, the positions of the cross-axis cuts, and the plume-map blur width all come from that image's measured contours. Ring contrasts are divided by each ring's median. The companion search loops over every local peak in the image and keeps the best one. Several measures keep the best over several radial windows or brightness levels. The final class comes from branching on these measured quantities.

clusters.approach: Nucleus finding, ray-traced multi-level contours with ellipse fits, unrolling the disk on fitted ellipses, log-spiral harmonic matching, bar, edge-on thickness and scored companion search, then an ordered first-match threshold cascade (merger, edge-on, disturbed, then smooth vs spiral subclasses)

Polar sampling about the image centre with sky subtraction and central-peak scaling or clipping, isophote radii along rays or diameters, angular harmonics, spiral twist, asymmetry and secondary-peak features, combined into hand-weighted per-class scores with family group terms and an argmax decision
Hand-built morphology features plus correlation against banks of rendered synthetic galaxy templates, combined into ten hand-weighted soft-ramped class scores with an argmax decision

pairs.shared: Hand-built morphology features: isophote shape, angular harmonics, log-spiral winding, colour gradient, bar, lopsidedness, secondary peaks; family-level split of smooth vs structured
pairs.differs: A samples a fixed polar grid at the frame centre with no nucleus refinement, ellipse fitting or disk unrolling, and decides by gated argmax over scores; B fits ellipses, unrolls the disk, scores ranked companion candidates and uses an ordered threshold cascade

pairs.differs: C adds a major template-matching stage against rendered synthetic galaxies plus light-moment and ellipse-fit residual measures; A has no references and uses explicit family gating

pairs.differs: D isolates the galaxy via running-minimum clipping, adds a tilted-disk log-spiral template search and knot/gap curvature detectors; A uses ring-to-ring rotated prediction for winding and explicit sub-class gating

pairs.differs: E finds and refines the nucleus, fits ellipses to ray contours, unrolls a face-on disk, scores companion candidates and decides with an ordered threshold cascade; A uses a fixed centre polar grid and argmax

pairs.differs: F tests disk first and falls through to smooth (equivalent complement of B's smooth test); differing thresholds and extra plume/twist route

pairs.differs: duplicate guard
