steps.step: Sky level subtracted using pixels in the outer frame/border of the image
steps.note: N1 uses a 55+/-6 px annulus and N3 the darkest of 8 border sectors, both measured on each image. N2 assumes a fixed sky of 0.105 and only subtracts a local sky from a 23 to 32 px annulus for some measures.

steps.step: Sky noise estimated from the spread of border pixels, used to floor contour levels
steps.note: None of the networks measures noise. Their levels are tied to the central brightness only, or are absolute.

steps.step: Weighted mix of the three bands into one brightness image
steps.note: All use fixed band weights of a similar size.

steps.step: Blurred copies of the brightness image at several scales
steps.note: N1 and N3 smooth implicitly through Gaussian sampling spots that widen with radius. N2 blurs, and also uses peak detectors at two blur sizes.

steps.step: Locate the nucleus: centre-weighted brightest point, then iterative centroid refinement
steps.note: All networks fix the centre at the image centre with no search or refinement. N3 only reads the peak brightness within 3.5 px.

steps.step: Trace contours along rays: first radius where brightness falls below each of several levels set as fractions of peak
steps.note: N3 uses 48 rays, 7 peak-relative levels, angular smoothing and opposite-ray averaging, matching the programs' procedure. N1 uses only 12 fixed diameters at 4 levels. N2 instead thresholds a log-polar grid and measures the region above each level.

steps.step: Ellipse fit to each contour (axis ratio, orientation, size)
steps.note: N1 takes the longest diameter against its perpendicular, N2 uses region and moment elongation plus a best-of-51 fixed ellipse model, and N3 uses the 2-fold Fourier component of log radius. None performs an actual fit.

steps.step: Contour departure from the ellipse and contour point asymmetry (odd-fold distortions)
steps.note: N3 takes the 1-, 3-, 5- and 4-, 6-fold components of contour radius. N1 has warp between levels and point-pair asymmetry. N2 has even and odd residuals around fixed ellipses.

steps.step: Re-centre on contour centres, or measure contour-centre drift
steps.note: The networks never move the centre.

steps.step: Unroll the disk on ellipses matched to the fitted outer contour (tilt and size), with log-spaced rings
steps.note: N1 and N2 use fixed circular rings at fixed pixel radii. N3 tries 14 fixed tilt and orientation combinations and keeps the best. No network scales the rings to the measured galaxy size.

steps.step: Angular harmonics on each ring, normalised by the ring's median or mean
steps.note: N1 computes 1 to 5 fold, N2 1 to 4 fold relative to the ring mean, and N3 2 fold on 12 rings.

steps.step: Cap or clip bright outliers (stars) on the rings
steps.note: N1 caps at a radius-dependent multiple of the central brightness, N2 at an absolute 0.62, and N3 clips light that rises after a running-minimum valley. P2 and P3 cap relative to each ring's own spread or median.

steps.step: Correlate ring harmonics with ideal log-spiral phase patterns over pitch, handedness and radial window, keeping the best
steps.note: N2 matches 2 and 3 arms at pitches 0 to 55 deg, both senses, over sliding windows. N3 matches only the 2-fold pattern at 3 pitches. N1 instead predicts each ring from the next ring rotated at only 18 or 36 deg.

steps.step: Split spiral strength into tight and open winding by pitch
steps.note: N1 has only a binary comparison between 18 and 36 deg.

steps.step: Phase twist of the 2-fold (and higher) pattern between rings at different radii
steps.note: N3 measures the orientation twist between isophote levels, not between ring phases.

steps.step: Winding score calibrated against empty sky patches in the same image
Local arm pitch or ridge slant from brightness gradients or curvature in the unrolled map
steps.note: N2's outward rises and bumps are ridge detectors but give no slant. N3's curvature detectors find knots and gaps, not pitch.

steps.step: Core and disk colour, and the colour gradient
steps.note: The networks use fixed pixel apertures, while the programs use zones relative to the measured disk size.

steps.step: Clumpy fine structure: higher-fold ring power beyond noise
steps.note: N1 uses odd-fold 3 and 5 strength, N2 opposite-sector differences, and N3 knot and gap detectors. None subtracts the noise level.

steps.step: Lopsidedness from the 1-fold pattern and point asymmetry
Concentration: bright-body size or flux against the outer size
steps.note: N1 uses the ratio of inner to outer isophote radius. N2 uses aperture flux ratios, and N3 nested apertures.

steps.step: Radial profile shape (shoulders, fade rate, exponential versus cusp)
steps.note: N2's bumps above the radial trend resemble P1's shoulders.

steps.step: Bar: inner contours more elongated than the outer disk, corrected for tilt, with a steady angle and a bounded length
steps.note: No network corrects for tilt. All compare inner and outer elongation at fixed radii.

steps.step: Bar: 2-fold pattern fixed in the inner rings that stops or changes beyond
steps.note: N2 looks for a strong inner 2-fold pattern that fades outside. N1 looks for elongation localised to one radius band. N3 uses the orientation change between isophotes.

steps.step: Red-band bar contours, or redder light along the bar
Companion search: local peaks within distance limits, ranked, with a dip to the nucleus, a size or extension test, a brightness ratio and bridging light
steps.note: N1 keeps the best peak per fixed annulus and checks the dip and bridging. N2 compares only off-centre peak strength, with no dip test, plus double-nucleus templates. N3 uses rise-after-dip crests along rays and a fixed 21x21 grid with half-plane pairing.

steps.step: Companion colour similarity to the nucleus
Companion side compared with the mirror-image opposite side
Tidal tails: light exceeding the opposite side at large radii
steps.note: N1 detects rebrightening with no opposite match, plus streams. N3 uses components of the faint absolute-level contours.

steps.step: One-sided reach of faint light at faint levels
steps.note: N1 uses the dipole of its connected light. N3 uses absolute levels, where P3 uses fractions of the central brightness.

steps.step: Edge-on thinness from the flattest outer contours and their length or pointedness
steps.note: These rest on the networks' approximate contour measures. N2 also uses thin edge-on templates.

steps.step: Edge-on bulge from vertical thickness cuts along the major axis, centre against outer disk
steps.note: N2 matches bulged against thin edge-on templates. N3 uses the change from inner to outer elongation. N1 uses only red core, contrast and concentration.

steps.step: Central brightness excess over the disk extrapolated inward (central spike)
steps.note: N1 has a central contrast term.

steps.step: Thin bright midplane line, or light above the midplane
steps.note: N3 lists a 'ridge' term in its bulge score.

steps.step: Disk-versus-smooth evidence score (spiral, structure, colour gradient, bar, size)
steps.note: These are hand-weighted sums of similar inputs.

steps.step: Smooth roundness split by axis-ratio thresholds (round, in-between, cigar)
steps.note: N2 uses soft q-bands inside an argmax.

steps.step: Seeing correction to contour size before roundness
Loose-versus-tight score (open minus tight winding, pitch, contrast, concentration, blueness)
Disturbed score (lopsidedness, tails, blue core, asymmetry)
Fixed-order first-match decision cascade (merger, edge-on, disturbed, smooth or spiral, bar, loose or tight)
steps.note: All networks take the argmax of 10 scores. N1 imitates the gating with penalties, and N3 with shared group terms. Precedence is soft, not ordered.

network_only.step: Correlation template matching against about 6000 rendered synthetic galaxies in 9 class-like families (disk, bar, tight and loose spirals, Sersic, edge-on thin and bulged, single and double nucleus)
Second moments of clipped light in Gaussian windows, with flux growth used to choose which scale's axis ratio to use
Fixed absolute sky floor (0.105) and bright cap (0.62) on the clipped image
Best-fitting model chosen among 51 fixed ellipse models, by shape group and radial weighting, with residuals as arm and disorder evidence
Connected-light tracing outward along each direction with a growth limit of 1.27 per ring
Radius-dependent brightness cap of min(1.5, 0.85 + 4/r) times the central brightness
Running-minimum valley clip along each ray to cut off detached neighbours
Curvature line and blob detectors (8 orientations, 2 scales) for knots and inter-arm gaps
Nucleus pairing over half-plane splits on a 21x21 candidate grid
Green-excess colour and blue outer halo terms
2x2 downsampling before measurement (N2 and N3 also do this)

numbers.meaning: Axis-ratio boundary between round and in-between smooth galaxies
numbers.network_values: N1 0.24 in log units (q about 0.79), N3 0.25 (q about 0.78), N2 upper in-between bound 0.79 (round favoured above 0.855)

numbers.meaning: Axis-ratio boundary between in-between and cigar smooth galaxies
numbers.network_values: N1 log 2.05 (q about 0.49), N2 in-between lower bound 0.48

numbers.meaning: Radius beyond which pixels count as border sky
numbers.program_values: P1 56 px, P2 50 px, P3 52 px
numbers.network_values: N1 55 +/- 6 px annulus, N3 53 px

numbers.meaning: Band weights for the brightness image
Top isophote level as a fraction of the central brightness
Pitch dividing tight from open spirals
numbers.program_values: P1 19 / 25-26 deg, P1 range 10 to 50 deg
numbers.network_values: N1 18 vs 36 deg, N2 14 and 23 vs 36 and 55 deg, N3 15/30/48 deg

numbers.meaning: Axis-ratio cut for an edge-on call
numbers.program_values: P2 disk q below 0.51 and visible q below 0.55
numbers.network_values: N2 edge-on score cut sharply above q 0.44

numbers.meaning: 0.085: P1 outer contour level against N3 faint contour level
numbers.network_values: N3 0.085 absolute intensity above sky

numbers.meaning: 1.05: P2 detail blur against N1 and N2 smoothing widths
numbers.program_values: P2 1.05 px blur on the full-resolution image
numbers.network_values: N1 and N2 1.05 on half- or quarter-resolution grids

numbers.meaning: 0.075: P2 ring span start against N2 sky-subtracted isophote level
numbers.program_values: P2 0.075 disk radii (P3 0.075 of outer semi-major axis)
numbers.network_values: N2 0.075 brightness above local sky

numbers.meaning: 0.45: P2 refinement fraction against N1 asymmetry pivot
numbers.network_values: N1 0.45 asymmetry pivot

numbers.meaning: Core colour region
numbers.program_values: P1 0.07 to 0.22 of outer size, P2 0.15 to 0.32 disk radii
numbers.network_values: N1 rings at 2, 3.5, 5.5 px, N2 and N3 2.5 px aperture

cover.verdict: The networks compute the same kind of thing as the programs: hand-built morphology features (contour elongation, ring harmonics, log-spiral matching, 2-fold twist, colour gradient, lopsidedness, companion peaks, edge-on flatness) fed into hand-weighted scores, and several thresholds line up, notably the round/in-between cut at an axis ratio of about 0.79. Strictly, though, they do not compute the same steps. Every per-image search in the programs (nucleus relocation, ellipse fitting, tilt-corrected unrolling scaled to the galaxy, noise-calibrated levels, the ordered first-match cascade) becomes fixed-centre, fixed-radius sampling with an argmax over scores, and N2 adds a large bank of rendered class templates that no program uses. The networks leave out noise estimation, re-centring, sky-patch winding calibration, arm pitch from gradients, deprojected and red-band bar tests, companion colour and mirror tests, vertical thickness profiles and seeing correction.

d.summary: The method looks for evidence of a person in several separate ways. It searches the image at several sizes for faces, using a skin colour map and a brightness map. It matches edge directions against stored outlines of whole human figures in a few poses, and it looks for a head above shoulders and clothing. It also adds scene context clues such as where skin, clothing colours, grass, sky, snow and fine detail sit in the frame. The best match from each detector is turned into a score, and the scores are combined with fixed weights and diminishing returns. The total is compared with a fixed reference level.
d.references:
Hand-drawn, not learned:
(1) Face templates. 5 face shapes (a small oval, a larger oval, a tall oval tilted 12 degrees left, the same tilted 12 degrees right, and a wide oval), plus 2 extra variants of the wide ones, so 7 in all. Each is drawn as smooth blobs: skin in a face oval, no skin at the sides, collar or hair, light cheeks, brow and nose, dark eyes and mouth. They are reused at 5 image scales.
(2) Full-body outlines. Geometric figures built from a torso, head, neck, hips, two-segment arms and legs and feet. There are 4 poses: standing at 4 heights and widths, striding and throwing (each also mirrored), and sitting, so 9 outlines. Each is turned into a map of where edges of each of 4 directions should appear. The edge budget is split 28% head and shoulders, 36% torso, 36% legs, with penalties for edges just beside the outline and for edges at the wrong angle. Used at 3 scales.
(3) Head and shoulders patterns. A skin head over a neck with no skin beside or above it. Torso versus side contrasts in brightness, red against blue, and green. Brightness outline tests for the head, temples, trunk and upper arms, drawn at 2 widths and with both contrast signs. Used at 4 scales.
(4) Detailed face checklist. 5 face shapes, each with 10 measured contrasts (see stages), each with a hand-set acceptable range. Used at 4 scales.
(5) Fixed position preference grids and coarse whole-frame layout masks: centre, border, top band and bottom band.

stages.name: Colour classes
stages.computes: Averages 2x2 pixel blocks into a 48x48 image. Measures each block's brightness and colour opposites. From these it computes a soft score for skin (two versions: normal and pale). Skin is penalised for being too grey, too red, too blue, too yellow, too dark, or not red enough. It also scores brightness and several colour families: saturated blue, red or magenta (clothing), grass green, sky cyan, yellow, plus red against green, green against blue, pure blue and scarlet. Skin (60% normal, 40% pale) and brightness become the two maps used by the face and head searches.

key_numbers.meaning: red, green and blue weights for brightness
how steeply skin membership falls for too little red over green and for grey (colourless) colour
brightness (0 to 1) below which a block counts as too dark for skin
block size of the working image (48x48)

stages.name: Face template search
stages.computes: Slides the 7 face templates over the skin and brightness maps at 5 scales: blocks of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12 image pixels. Each place gets a score for skin in the oval and not around it, plus light cheeks, brow and nose with dark eyes and mouth. It keeps the best template at each place, then the best place in each of 4x4 regions of the frame. It subtracts a position penalty, smallest just above the centre and largest at the bottom corners, then keeps the best region and the best scale.

key_numbers.meaning: block sizes of the 5 scales, so face widths from about 5 to about 60 image pixels
tilt of the leaning face shapes
largest position penalty (bottom corners); the two central upper cells get 0
grid of frame regions that each keep their best face score

stages.name: Oriented edges
stages.computes: On the 48x48 image it measures edge strength in 4 directions (0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees), in both brightness and red against blue, counting both contrast signs. The colour edges count 65% as much as brightness edges. Each direction is weakened by the perpendicular direction and slightly by the diagonal neighbours. The result is then softly saturated so that very strong edges do not dominate.

key_numbers.meaning: edge directions
weight of red against blue edges relative to brightness edges
how much the perpendicular direction suppresses each direction
edge level above which further strength counts only 18%

stages.name: Full-body outline search
stages.computes: Matches the 9 body outlines against the edge directions at 3 scales: edge cells of 2, 4 and 8 image pixels. It keeps the best pose at each place, then the best place in each of 3x3 frame regions, minus a small position penalty, then the best region and the best scale.

key_numbers.meaning: figure heights in the template, about 25 to 145 image pixels across the 3 scales, so roughly a quarter of the frame up to the full frame
width stretch of the standing figures
largest position penalty (bottom corners) for body matches

stages.name: Head over shoulders and clothing
stages.computes: At 4 scales (blocks of 2, 4, 6 and 8 pixels) it scores a skin head over a neck, with no skin beside the head, above it in the hair, or right at the chin. It adds a torso check that the area below the head differs from both sides in brightness, red against blue, or green. Only the weaker of the left and right contrasts counts, capped at 0.44 and weighted 0.79. It takes the best of 4x4 regions with a centre preference, then the best scale.

key_numbers.meaning: cap on the two-sided clothing contrast
sideways offset of the side areas compared with the torso
largest position penalty (bottom corners)

stages.name: Head and shoulders outline
stages.computes: At 3 scales (2, 4 and 6 pixels) it runs 4 brightness tests. They compare the head with the area above it, the head with its temples, the trunk with its flanks, and the upper arms with the area above the shoulders. Each test result is pressed into a limited range, and the 4 are added with fixed weights. It keeps the best of 2 widths and both contrast signs, then the best of 3x3 regions with a position penalty, then the best scale.

key_numbers.meaning: range of brightness contrast within which each outline test counts
narrow and wide shoulder versions
largest position penalty (bottom corners)

stages.name: Detailed face checklist
stages.computes: At 4 scales (2, 4, 6 and 8 pixels) and over 5 face shapes it measures 10 contrasts, each mapped onto a 0 to 1 scale between a lower and upper limit. They are: each eye darker than the forehead and the cheek below it; the nose bridge lighter than the eyes; the cheeks and chin lighter than the lips; the forehead lighter than the hair line; the face lighter than its sides; the skin share inside the face oval; face skin against skin at the sides and below; cheek skin against skin above and below; the cheeks lighter than the eyes. The weighted total is kept for the best shape, then the best of 3x3 (or 2x2) regions with a position penalty, then the best scale.

key_numbers.meaning: range of skin share inside the face oval that is mapped to 0 to 1
range of eye darkness compared with the forehead and cheek
largest weights: skin share and skin contained inside the face
largest position penalty (bottom corners)

stages.name: Scene context
stages.computes: Averages the colour classes over 16x16 pixel tiles (a 6x6 grid). It compares skin, clothing colours and scarlet or blue in the centre against the border, grass low in the frame, sky high in the frame, and yellow at the border. Each comparison passes through a pair of thresholds into a capped vote: more central skin and clothing count for a person, more skin and yellow at the border count against. It also adds fine-detail contrast in the centre compared with the border, snow-like bright ground low in the frame, and another set of colour-layout votes.

key_numbers.meaning: tile size for the layout statistics
central skin share at which the skin vote stops growing
bright-ground level above which a tile counts as snow
fixed amount subtracted from the context vote

stages.name: Many faces
stages.computes: Averages the face scores across the 4x4 regions and the 5 scales, and keeps only the part above 0.43. It averages that over the frame and adds it to the context as a sign of several faces or a crowd.

key_numbers.meaning: face score a region must pass before it counts towards a group
amount subtracted before the group vote

stages.name: Final vote
stages.computes: Combines the face, head and clothing, full-body, head outline, context and detailed face scores with fixed weights. Body evidence grows more slowly once it passes 0.44. Face and head scores get extra credit above 0.91 and 1.0, and the detailed face score gets extra credit above 0.72. The total, minus a fixed reference of about 1.26, is the person score, and the no-person score is 0.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the detailed face score, and the extra weight above 0.72
weights of the face, head and clothing, body, and head outline scores
reference total that must be passed to say person

d.decision: It says person when the weighted total of the six evidence scores (with diminishing returns on body evidence and extra credit for strong face or head evidence) is more than about 1.26. Otherwise it says no person.
d.adapts_per_image: For every detector it searches over positions, template shapes and poses, and scales, and keeps the best match each time. It also keeps the best value within each frame region before applying the position penalty. There is no branching or iterating. Thresholded votes switch on or off depending on the measured scores, and edge strength is softly saturated. Nothing is normalised by quantities measured on that image.

d.summary: A hand-built person detector. It first marks skin-coloured pixels after a mild white-balance correction. It then runs three independent searches, each of which yields one best score for "a person is here": (1) a head-and-shoulders box layout slid over many positions and sizes, (2) a full-body outline made of left and right edge strips at seven body levels, and (3) connected blobs of skin scored on how face-like they look. The strongest search counts most and the others add a little, a whole-scene context score is added, and the total is compared with a fixed cutoff.
d.references: None learned or rendered. The only stored material is hand-specified box geometry. (a) A head-centred layout of 32 rectangles, each placed relative to a head box of width w and height h: face, hair, the region above the head, background left and right of the head, chest, both shoulders, background beside the shoulders, waist and its sides, legs and their sides, 11 small facial-feature boxes (eyes, nose, cheeks, brow, lip, chin, philtrum, forehead sides), one local-context box (1.65w by 1.46h) and 4 neck-to-shoulder slope boxes. This layout is laid over 19 head sizes. (b) 30 upright body-outline templates: 6 heights (20 to 128 px) by 3 widths (0.215, 0.315 and 0.44 of the height). The middle width also comes in leaning-left and leaning-right poses with wider legs. Each template has 7 body levels (head, neck, shoulder, ribs, hip, knee, ankle), and each level has 4 strips: outside left, inside left, inside right, outside right.

stages.name: Colour channels and skin map
stages.computes: Converts each pixel to brightness plus red-minus-green and green-minus-blue opponent colours. Estimates the scene's white point from bright, nearly neutral pixels and applies a small, capped correction. Each pixel then gets a soft skin likelihood from a flesh-hue and saturation window (the larger of a lightly and a more strongly white-balanced version). The image is flagged black-and-white when there is almost no colour.

key_numbers.meaning: brightness (0 to 1 scale) above which pixels start to count as white references for the colour correction
window on the red share of (red minus blue) that counts as flesh hue
mean absolute colour difference below which the photo is treated as black-and-white

stages.name: Head-and-shoulders search over positions and sizes
stages.computes: Slides a head box over a grid of positions for 19 sizes, with head widths from 3 to 83 px and heights 1.1 or 1.82 times the width. At each position it takes the average colour of each rectangle in the head-centred layout. Colour differences are scaled by the local brightness spread so that busy regions need more contrast.

key_numbers.meaning: range of head widths searched (10 widths)
grid step as a fraction of head width
horizontal offset of the background boxes beside the head
vertical offset of chest, waist and leg boxes below the top of the head

stages.name: Head-and-shoulders cues
stages.computes: Several cues are measured. Head contrast: the face differs from the background on both sides, the hair differs from what is above it, and the backgrounds on the two sides match. Skin in the face box but not in the surround. Hair darker than the face. A chest that differs from the face. Shoulders wider than the head and distinct from the background beside them. Body continuity further down, counted only if that part of the image is inside the frame.

key_numbers.meaning: how much a shoulder box must differ from the background beside it, relative to how much it differs from the chest
how far the frame must extend below the head before waist and leg evidence counts

stages.name: Facial-feature cues (larger heads only)
stages.computes: For heads at least 6.5 px wide it checks for two eye regions darker than the cheeks and forehead below and above them, a nose bridge brighter than the eyes, left-right symmetry, and a lip darker and redder than the chin and philtrum.

key_numbers.meaning: minimum head width at which eyes and mouth are examined
position of the eye boxes in the head box

stages.name: Head candidate scoring and spatial pooling
stages.computes: Weighted sums of the cues form three alternative scores: colour-led, shape-led and face-detail-led. The best of the three is kept, with small penalties for candidates low in the frame or near the side edges and for very small heads. The image is split into 6 regions (3 across by 2 down), and each region keeps its best candidate over all positions and sizes. For heads up to 20 px wide there is a bonus when other strong heads of the same size sit side by side (a crowd).

key_numbers.meaning: size of each of the 6 pooling regions
minimum horizontal spacing for a second head to count as a different person
maximum vertical offset between heads counted as a row
largest head width for which the crowd bonus applies

stages.name: Head vote
stages.computes: Takes the best region's score and adds a bonus when the second and third best regions are also fairly strong.

key_numbers.meaning: maximum bonus weights for the second and third best regions

stages.name: Full-body outline search
stages.computes: Slides each of the 30 upright figure outlines over a grid of positions. At each of the 7 body levels it checks that both the left and the right edges show an inside-to-outside colour change, that the two inside strips match each other (one garment), and that the two outside strips match each other (one background). It combines these with shirt consistency, skin at head height and shirt-to-trousers contrast, giving most weight to the head, shoulders, ribs and hips. Knees and ankles count less, and less still when cut off at the bottom of the frame. It keeps the single best placement.

key_numbers.meaning: figure heights searched
figure width as a fraction of its height
sideways lean of the leaning poses, as a fraction of width per unit of height
position grid step

stages.name: Skin-blob face search
stages.computes: Smooths the skin map, thresholds it and groups the skin pixels into connected blobs. Blobs of implausible size, fill or proportions are discarded. Each remaining blob is scored on proportions, oval fill, being widest in the middle, standing out from the skin level around it, a darker cap of hair above it, moderate brightness variation inside, and some skin below it (arms or neck). The best blob is kept, with a bonus if there is a second good one.

key_numbers.meaning: smoothed skin likelihood needed for a pixel to belong to a blob

key_numbers.value: 6 px area, 2 px wide, 3 px tall
key_numbers.meaning: minimum blob size
hard limits on how full the blob's bounding box is and on its aspect ratio

stages.name: Scene context score
stages.computes: Adds or subtracts evidence from the whole picture. It adds for grass, water with foam, snow, or baseball-style clay fields in the lower half; for small vivid red, magenta or royal-blue patches (clothing); for compact bright skin patches and a moderate overall amount of skin; and for edges concentrated in the centre rather than at the sides. It subtracts for mostly horizontal and vertical straight edges (buildings) and for skin-coloured pixels covering much of the image. Black-and-white photos get a fixed bonus.

key_numbers.meaning: lower part of the image examined for a grass playing surface
how strongly horizontal or vertical an edge must be to count as architectural
share of edge energy on such straight lines at which the building penalty starts
bonus added for black-and-white photos

d.decision: The three search scores (head-and-shoulders vote, body outline, skin blob) are sorted and blended with weights 0.73 for the strongest, 0.22 for the middle and 0.05 for the weakest. The scene context score is added. The photo is labelled "person" if the total exceeds 0.44, otherwise "no person".
d.adapts_per_image: Yes, heavily. The white-balance correction is estimated from each photo's own bright neutral pixels. Contrast tests are scaled by the brightness spread measured around each candidate. Both template searches range over positions and sizes and keep the best, both overall and per region. The crowd bonus looks for further heads near the best one. Skin blobs are found by connected grouping, filtered by measured shape, and the best ones kept. The three search results are sorted, so the strongest gets the largest weight. Black-and-white photos are detected and get extra bonuses. Facial-feature checks run only at larger head sizes.

d.summary: This is a hand-built person detector made of many hand-tuned cues. It turns colour into a skin-likelihood map, then searches thousands of candidate head positions and sizes. Each candidate is scored against an imagined human layout: an oval head with skin cheeks and darker hair, face details, a torso and legs below it, and hands that match the face's colour. A second outline-only check looks for a head, shoulders and legs stick figure among the top candidates. The best candidate's confidence is then added to whole-image evidence: groups of skin patches, scene type (sports field, snow, water, ruled grid-like interiors, dinner plates) and whether the centre of the picture stands out. The photo is called "person" when that total is positive.
d.references: None in the sense of stored images or prototypes. The "templates" are hand-placed geometric layouts written as fixed offsets relative to a head box: patches for cheeks, hair, forehead, eyes, brows, nose, mouth and chin, chest, belly, hips, trousers and legs, hands, and 12 points on an oval ring. There is also a stick-figure layout of edge directions (flat top of the head, vertical temples, sloping shoulders, vertical body sides, horizontal belt, two legs). Fixed colour ranges are hand-coded for skin, grass, dusty ground, courts, snow and water. Nothing is learned or looked up from example data.

stages.name: Colour re-description and skin likelihood
stages.computes: For each pixel, red-versus-green and green-versus-blue colour ratios are computed and partly corrected by subtracting a fraction of their image-wide averages (a mild white balance). A soft 0 to 1 skin score is set where these ratios fall in a warm, skin-like wedge and red is not too dark. Each pixel then carries skin score, green level, red minus green and blue minus green. Box averages of these are made cheap to look up anywhere.

key_numbers.meaning: fraction of the image's mean colour cast removed before testing skin colour
band of the red-versus-green ratio counted as skin, with soft edges 0.06 and 0.12 wide
upper limit of the green-versus-blue ratio for skin
minimum red brightness (0 to 1 scale) for a pixel to count as skin

stages.name: Head candidate generation
stages.computes: Candidate head boxes are laid on a grid at 9 widths and 2 shapes (square, and 1.67 times taller than wide), with a step of about a quarter of the box width. Where the grid is large, each spot gets quick scores: skin in the middle that stands out from its left, right and top surroundings, colour change on both sides and on top, a distinct shirt region below, and a dark-above-bright face pattern for larger boxes. Only the top-scoring spot in each block of about 6 by 6 grid spots is kept, separately for each quick score.

key_numbers.meaning: head widths searched, in pixels of the 96 by 96 image
head height divided by width
grid step as a fraction of head width and height
below this many grid spots, every spot is kept rather than only block winners

stages.name: Head and skin evidence per candidate
stages.computes: Each candidate gets several head cues: how much skin sits in the centre, cheeks and jaw; how much more skin it has than the surrounding area; colour change on both left and right sides at the cheeks (a plain one-sided edge gets little credit); a distinct and darker hair or cap region above; and an oval-boundary check, in which colour changes at 12 points around an ellipse, at two ring sizes, and more strongly at the top and sides. A penalty applies when the whole image is broadly skin-coloured.

key_numbers.meaning: points tested around the oval head outline
two oval sizes tried, relative to the head box
how far to each side the background patches are sampled
range of image-wide average skin over which the warm-scene penalty ramps up

stages.name: Body below the head
stages.computes: Below the head, at three body tilts (left, upright, right), the cues look for: a chest, belly and trousers that each differ from the regions beside them; shoulders that widen out from the neck; a torso bounded by edges on both sides from shoulder to hip, at two body widths; a colour change between shirt and trousers; and hand or forearm patches beside the body whose colour matches the face. Candidates whose body would lie off the bottom of the photo get a neutral value instead.

key_numbers.meaning: body tilts tried, as sideways shift in head widths per head height down
positions of chest, belly, hips, trousers and legs below the head centre, in head heights
sideways distance of the background patches beside the chest
two torso widths tried for the both-sides edge check

stages.name: Facial features
stages.computes: At three small head rolls, the method checks for eyes darker than the cheeks below them, brows, a nose bridge brighter than the eyes, a mouth darker than the area just above it and the chin, and left-right symmetry. The result only counts in proportion to how large, and so how resolvable, the head is.

key_numbers.meaning: head rolls tried (rotation of the feature layout, in radians, roughly)
vertical position of the eye patches; eyes sit 0.205 head widths either side of centre
head size range over which the face cue ramps from ignored to fully trusted

stages.name: Combine into three alternative explanations
stages.computes: Each candidate gets three scores: an exposed skin head, a resolved face, and a whole upright figure that needs no skin. Each is reduced by position priors that penalise heads low in the frame, near the left or right edge, cut by the border, or very small. Each is then checked by a verification term (oval outline, torso edges, skin spread evenly over the face patches, even colour). The candidate's confidence is the largest of the three after each is shifted and rescaled against its own threshold.

key_numbers.meaning: thresholds for the skin-head, face and figure scores
head centre row below which the low-in-frame penalty starts
head width below which the tiny-head penalty applies

stages.name: Outline-only stick-figure check
stages.computes: The 96 candidates with the best shape-only score (no colour) are checked against brightness edges at fine and coarse scales. The method looks for a horizontal edge on top of the head, vertical edges at the temples, diagonal edges at the shoulders, vertical edges along the body sides and waist, a horizontal belt edge and two leg edges, each compared with the edge density of the surrounding area. It tries 3 tilts and 2 body widths and keeps the best. This can raise the candidate's confidence, with a penalty if the body would be cut off by the bottom of the photo.

key_numbers.meaning: number of top candidates given the outline check
two edge-measurement scales
tilts tried for the stick figure
threshold for the combined outline score

stages.name: Best and second person
stages.computes: Takes the most confident candidate. Then finds the most confident candidate that does not overlap it (separated by more than about the sum of their sizes) and adds a small bonus when that second one is also confident.

key_numbers.meaning: separation, relative to the summed box sizes, needed to count as a different person
largest bonus for a second confident person

stages.name: Skin-blob grouping
stages.computes: On a half-resolution grid, the method thresholds the skin map, smooths it with a neighbour count and groups touching skin cells into blobs. For each blob it scores a filled, slightly tall shape, standing out from its surroundings, darker hair above, distinct clothing below, a sensible size and position, and another blob of similar hue below it at a plausible distance (a hand or arm). The best blob's score is a moderate bonus, or a small penalty if no blob qualifies.

key_numbers.meaning: skin-score levels for weak and strong skin cells
cell size of the grid used for grouping
preferred blob width divided by height
blob evidence threshold

stages.name: Scene type
stages.computes: Rewards smooth turf-green, snow-white or water-blue areas in the lower half (typical of sports scenes). Penalises long straight lines parallel to the image axes (buildings, rooms, vehicles). Rewards a warm spot in the upper part that is warmer than the bottom, and penalises photos with no warm colour in the upper three-quarters.

key_numbers.meaning: only rows below this are checked for field, snow or water
length of a straight run that counts as a long line
maximum upper-image skin level below which the photo is called bland

stages.name: Central focus, playing-field lines and plates
stages.computes: Rewards a centre that is sharper and more contrasting than the borders, skin within the salient central area, and saturated red or blue clothing-like colours in the centre. Rewards bright narrow straight markings on grass, dirt or courts. Penalises a bright neutral elliptical rim (a dinner plate) with food-coloured contents, tested at 27 positions and sizes.

key_numbers.meaning: scales of the centre-versus-surround colour contrast
orientations and length of the straight field-line check
plate positions and sizes tested and points sampled on each rim
rim brightness above which the plate edge counts as white

d.decision: Binary: "person" if (best candidate confidence) + (second-person bonus) + (scene score) + (skin-blob score, positive part times 0.84 and negative part times 0.23) + (centre-focus score) + (field-lines minus plates score) is greater than 0. Otherwise "no person".
d.adapts_per_image: Heavily adaptive. Colour is normalised by the image's own average cast. Head candidates are found by searching over 18 size and shape settings and keeping the best position in each block. Body tilt, body width, oval size and head roll are each searched, and the best is kept. Only the top 96 candidates get the outline check. The best candidate and the best non-overlapping second one are picked. Skin cells are grouped into blobs whose number and shape depend on the image, with early fallbacks when no blob exists. Several measures are scaled by the image's own brightness or edge density (face darkness relative to head brightness, edges relative to local edge density, the warm-scene penalty based on overall skin coverage), and the best plate ellipse is kept.

d.summary: A hand-designed person detector. It scans the photo at several scales with fixed, drawn templates for four views of a person: a close-up face pattern (dark eyes and mouth against lighter cheeks, brows and nose, plus a skin-coloured oval), a head-and-shoulders pattern (skin head, hair cap, contrast with the chest, and an outline of head, neck and shoulders), and two whole-figure patterns (head, torso and legs that each stand out from what is beside them, plus long edges along the body's sides). For each view it takes the best-matching location and the amount of strongly matching area, rewards places where several views agree, adds whole-scene clues (isolated skin patches, small bright clothing-coloured blobs, a green or blue playing field at the bottom, a penalty for long straight architectural lines), and says "person" when the weighted evidence clears a fixed margin.
d.references: No stored example images. Every template is drawn by hand from Gaussian blobs placed at fixed relative positions. (1) Face templates: 5 face shapes (3 upright with different width and height, 2 tilted by plus or minus 0.2 rad). Each has blobs for the eyes, cheeks, brows, nose bridge, nose, mouth, chin and hair, which make up 11 light/dark contrast patterns and 8 pairwise patterns per shape, plus a skin template per shape (skin face oval minus skin at the sides and above). (2) Head-and-shoulders templates: 3 sizes. Each has 5 skin patterns, 6 brightness patterns (hair over face, face versus sides, chest versus background, face versus chest, lower versus upper face, sides versus above), 2 garment-colour patterns, a sampled head, neck and shoulder outline drawn as a 12-point polyline for each side (split into head and shoulder parts, edge orientation following the outline), 4 "skin surrounded by non-skin" sectors and 3 "darker hair lobes around the face" sectors. (3) Standing-figure templates: 3 sizes. Head, torso and lower body are each contrasted with the regions to their left and right, plus 6 extra part contrasts and a skin-head pattern. (4) Clothed-figure templates: 3 sizes. Head, torso and legs cross-sections, arm and shoulder patterns, 7 more part contrasts, 6 long body-side and shoulder edge templates per size, and an optional skin head. (5) Scene templates: centre-surround spot templates for skin and for 3 saturated garment colours (warm red/orange, blue, magenta), 2 long straight line templates (vertical and horizontal), and 4 ground-colour probes (green, cyan/blue, blue, orange) weighted toward the bottom rows. There are also fixed location maps that favour the centre and penalise the borders.

stages.name: Colour and brightness pyramids
stages.computes: Turns the photo into a brightness image and builds copies of the colour and brightness images averaged down to 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 and 1/16 resolution.

key_numbers.meaning: standard red, green, blue mix used for brightness
side length in pixels of the pyramid levels

stages.name: Skin-colour map
stages.computes: At half resolution, scores each pixel as skin when its colour lies inside a region bounded by 7 colour constraints: red above green by a margin, red not too far above green, not too blue or green, and red bright enough. Each violated constraint lowers the score, which is clipped to the range 0 to 1. The map is then averaged down to coarser levels.

key_numbers.meaning: number of colour boundary constraints that define skin
minimum red level (0 to 1 scale) for skin
resolution of the skin map

stages.name: Oriented edge maps
stages.computes: Measures brightness edges in 4 directions (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees), counting both dark-to-light and light-to-dark. Each direction's edge strength is reduced by 0.65 times the strength in the perpendicular direction, so only clearly oriented edges score. The result is clipped to 0 to 1.

key_numbers.meaning: edge directions, 45 degrees apart
fraction of the perpendicular edge strength subtracted

stages.name: Face pattern search
stages.computes: At 4 scales and every position, compares brightness with the 5 face shapes. It checks that the eyes are darker than the cheeks and brows, the nose bridge is lighter than the eyes, the mouth is darker than the nose and chin, the hair is darker than the face, and the left and right halves match, with penalties for asymmetry. Each check is clipped and the checks are added up. Bonus terms reward both eyes being dark together, a dark mouth, and a skin-coloured face oval without skin at the sides or above. The best of the 5 shapes is kept at each position, then positions near the image border and toward the bottom are penalised.

key_numbers.value: about 5 to 8 pixels per face unit at each scale level, scales 1, 2, 4, 8
key_numbers.meaning: face sizes covered, roughly 4 to 45 image pixels wide
head tilt of the two tilted face shapes
border zone width and the largest border penalty

stages.name: Head-and-shoulders search
stages.computes: At scales 2, 4, 8 and 16 and 3 sizes, scores each position on four things: a skin head that differs from its sides, from above (hair) and from below (chest); brightness contrasts (dark hair cap, chest versus background, either polarity); a garment colour that differs from the background beside it; and oriented edges that follow a head, neck and shoulder outline, with parallel offset edges subtracted. Two more tests use a soft minimum, so they score only if all sectors pass: skin is separated from non-skin on all 4 sides, and darker hair surrounds the face on 3 sides. The best size is kept at each position, with border and location penalties.

key_numbers.meaning: template window size; the shoulders span about 2.6 head-widths on each side
sector score below which the all-sides tests penalise a missing side
extra weight given to the outline match

stages.name: Standing-figure search
stages.computes: At scales 2, 4 and 8 and 3 sizes, uses brightness and a red-versus-blue colour axis. It checks that the head, torso and lower body each contrast with the regions beside them on both sides, scoring the weaker of the two sides. It adds smaller terms for the head versus what is above it, the torso versus the legs, and the head's skin, and penalises a background that differs between left and right. The response is moved to the head's position, the best size is kept, and positions near the border and the top are penalised.

key_numbers.meaning: vertical positions of head, torso and lower-body centres in figure units
template window size
contrast threshold before a part counts

stages.name: Clothed-figure search
stages.computes: Like the standing-figure search but with a larger window. It adds arm and shoulder cross-sections, and long edges along the sides of the torso and legs and across the shoulders (each minus parallel offset edges), with an optional skin head. The best size is kept, with border penalties (strongest at the top).

key_numbers.meaning: template window size
head, torso and leg centre heights in figure units
edge-support threshold

stages.name: Cross-detector agreement
stages.computes: At each scale, brings the face, head-and-shoulders and figure maps onto a common grid. At each site it adds the three scores and subtracts part of the strongest one, so sites where two or more detectors fire together score higher than sites where only one fires.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of the face, head and figure evidence
share of the single strongest cue subtracted

stages.name: Per-detector summary
stages.computes: For each detector (face, head, figure, agreement, clothed figure), reduces all scales to a 6x6 grid and takes the strongest scale in each cell. It records three numbers: the single best score in the image, the average of the best scores in the four quadrants, and the average amount by which cells exceed a threshold (how much area matches strongly).

key_numbers.meaning: coarse grid over the whole image
strong-match thresholds for the face, head, figure, agreement and clothed detectors

stages.name: Scene clues
stages.computes: Measures four things over the whole image: (a) the average strength of small skin patches that stand out from their surroundings; (b) the strongest small blob of saturated red/orange, blue or magenta that stands out from its surroundings (bright clothing); (c) the average strength of long, thin, straight vertical and horizontal edges (buildings, furniture); (d) how much of the lower image is green or blue, a playing field, combined with a bright-clothing blob into a 'sports scene' clue.

key_numbers.meaning: centre-minus-surround threshold for an isolated skin spot (24x24 grid)
shape of the long-line template (spread 3.8 along, 0.48 across)

key_numbers.value: bottom rows weighted about 10 times the top
key_numbers.meaning: ground-colour probes emphasise the lower part of the image
threshold that field colour plus bright clothing must exceed for the sports clue

stages.name: Weighted vote
stages.computes: Gives each detector a margin: a weighted mix of its best score, quadrant score and strong-match area, minus a fixed offset. The scene margin adds the skin spots, bright blobs and sports clue and subtracts the long straight lines. A person score is the sum of every margin plus an extra bonus for each margin above zero.

key_numbers.meaning: offsets for the face, head, figure, agreement and clothed margins
weights against long vertical and horizontal lines
weight on isolated skin spots

d.decision: The 'no person' score is fixed at 0. The 'person' score is the combined vote minus 0.06. The photo is called 'person' when the combined evidence exceeds 0.06. The combined evidence adds each detector's margin (weights 0.25, 0.35, 0.05, 0.66, 1.0, 0.16 for face, head, figure, agreement, scene, clothed) and an extra bonus for each positive margin (weights 0.87, 0.96, 0.2, 0.98, 0, 0.84).
d.adapts_per_image: It searches over positions and scales and keeps the best match. At each position it keeps the best of several face shapes, tilts and body sizes. The summaries take the best score in the image and in each quadrant, and the strongest scale in each grid cell. The final step, which adds a bonus only for margins above zero, and the clipping inside the sub-scores act like soft branches. Nothing is normalised by statistics measured on the image: the whole-image skin average is computed but only feeds fixed constant maps, so it has no effect. Nothing is iterated or sorted.

d.summary: The method looks for a person in many hand-drawn ways. After a partial white-balance correction it marks skin-coloured pixels. It then scans the image at many sizes for a face pattern (skin oval with darker eyes, mouth and hair, bounded by non-skin), a head-and-shoulders outline, a standing-figure outline, and a uniformly coloured torso under a skin-coloured head, keeping the strongest match per detector. These best matches are blended with a few whole-scene cues (how many straight horizontal and vertical edges, where red, blue, green and white sit in the frame, how much of the frame is skin-coloured), and the sum decides person or no person.
d.references: No stored example images or learned prototypes. Every reference is a hand-built template made from Gaussian blobs and soft ellipses. (1) Face template, tilt-aware: a central skin oval, a non-skin ring around it, two eye spots darker than cheeks, brow and nose, a hair cap darker than the cheeks, a mouth darker than cheeks and chin, and a shirt region below. Drawn at 11 size/tilt settings, upright or tilted 20 degrees left or right. (2) Head-and-shoulders outline: about 5 mirrored contour segments (crown, neck, shoulder slope, upper arm), each a set of inside/outside point pairs across the contour, drawn at 5 sizes. (3) Standing-figure outline: 6 mirrored contour segments from head to legs, drawn at 4 sizes. (4) Clothed-torso template: torso centre, upper and lower torso, flanks, the areas beside the head, and a head spot above, drawn at 8 settings (6 upright sizes, 2 leaning). (5) Fixed scene weightings: a 4x4 map of where each colour class counts, 8 and 4 oriented edge patterns, and a centre-versus-side-columns texture map. (6) Fixed colour rules: 9 colour half-space tests that define skin, and 10 colour tests for red, blue, green and bright white.

stages.name: Downsample and global colour cast correction
stages.computes: The image is halved to 48x48 by 2x2 averaging and its overall mean colour is measured. Where the mean is redder than green, or greener than blue, beyond a dead zone, the excess (capped) is partly removed: red is lowered or raised, blue is raised or lowered, across the whole image.

key_numbers.meaning: dead zone (intensity units, 0..1) before a red-over-green or green-over-blue cast counts
cast size at which the correction stops growing (saturation)
fraction of the measured cast that is removed

stages.name: Skin colour membership and appearance pyramid
stages.computes: Each corrected pixel is tested against 9 colour constraints that combine red minus green, green minus blue and brightness. Summed violations give two soft skin scores, a loose one from 6 tests and a strict one from all 9, which are blended. Together with the luminance of the uncorrected colour this forms a two-part description (skin-ness, brightness), averaged down to 48, 24, 12 and 6 pixel grids.

key_numbers.meaning: brightness formula used everywhere
blend of the loose and strict skin scores
grid resolutions searched (96 px image divided by 2, 4, 8, 16)

stages.name: Position preference
stages.computes: Each detector's response map gets a penalty that grows toward the left and right edges (outer 20% on each side), the bottom of the frame, and the very top. Faces are penalised below 59% of the height or above 12%. Figures are penalised below 74% or above 18%.

key_numbers.meaning: face penalty starts below 59% or above 12% of image height
figure penalty starts below 74% or above 18% of image height
horizontal offset from centre (fraction of width) beyond which the side penalty applies
maximum face penalty at the bottom edge / at the side edges

stages.name: Face search
stages.computes: At every position and at 11 size/tilt settings, the face template is compared with the skin and brightness maps. The comparison rewards a skin-coloured centre and penalises skin in the surrounding ring and left/right imbalance of that ring. It also rewards eyes darker than cheeks (clipped, with a penalty if the two eyes differ), a darker hair cap above (clipped) and a darker mouth (clipped), plus a capped brightness contrast between shirt and flanks. For the largest scales a second, eye-weighted 'detail' score is also formed. The best position per setting is kept, and a coverage score (mean over a 3x3 grid of regional best matches) is recorded.

key_numbers.value: face widths about 4, 7, 11, 19, 27, 43, 70 px, tilted 35 px, eye-focused 31 and 64 px
key_numbers.meaning: template sizes in the 96 px frame (unit w times grid step); the skin oval is about 0.86 w wide and 1.1 w tall
in-plane tilt of two face variants
caps on how much eye, hair and mouth darkness contrast can add
face acceptance offset at the finest grid / at coarser grids

stages.name: Head-and-shoulders and standing-figure outline search
stages.computes: Brightness only: along each drawn contour segment, inside versus outside brightness is compared at matched points, and either polarity counts. The score rewards strong contrast that is consistent along the head part and along the body part, and penalises points that disagree with their group and imbalance between head and body. A skin-at-face-spot minus skin-beside-head term is added. The best position per size is kept, with coverage recorded for the standing figure.

key_numbers.meaning: head-and-shoulders sizes in the 96 px frame; shoulders span about 2.9 units
standing-figure sizes in the 96 px frame (about 3.5 units tall)
weight of the penalty for inconsistency along the head / body outline
saturation points for head and body outline strength

stages.name: Clothed torso under a head
stages.computes: Using brightness, red minus green, and blue minus yellow colour contrasts, it rewards a torso region that differs from the flanks and from the area above the shoulders. It penalises left/right flank differences, upper-versus-lower torso differences and left-versus-right torso differences (the torso should be uniform and symmetric), capping the reward. To this it adds a skin-coloured spot where the head should be, minus skin beside and on the torso, minus asymmetry, plus a clipped brightness step from face to hair. The best position is kept per setting.

key_numbers.value: unit about 4, 6, 10, 15, 23, 38 px; leaning variants 14 px
key_numbers.meaning: torso template sizes in the 96 px frame
sideways lean (shear) of the two tilted variants
cap on the torso-contrast reward
acceptance offset for the combined head-plus-clothing score

stages.name: Edge-orientation scene cues
stages.computes: Oriented brightness edges are measured at 48 and 24 grids. Overall dominance of horizontal and vertical over diagonal edge energy lowers the person score (man-made, architectural scenes), and more edge texture in the centre than in the side columns raises it. A second pass at the 24 grid measures straight edges above a threshold and subtracts horizontal and vertical line strength while adding diagonal.

key_numbers.meaning: weight against axis-aligned edge dominance
columns farther than 32% of width from centre count as periphery
edge contrast threshold (intensity) for the straight-line count
weight of straight horizontal/vertical (minus) versus diagonal (plus) lines

stages.name: Colour layout scene cues
stages.computes: At the 24 grid each pixel gets graded memberships for distinctly red, blue, green (each the smaller of its two dominance margins) and bright white. These are averaged over a 4x4 block layout. Red and blue in the middle two rows, and green and white in the bottom half, raise the person score.

key_numbers.meaning: colour dominance thresholds for red / blue / green (intensity difference)
brightness threshold for white (snow-like)
relative weights for blue-mid and green-bottom vs red-mid vs white-bottom

stages.name: Large skin-coloured area penalty
stages.computes: The fraction of the frame marked skin-coloured is measured. Anything above about 11% lowers the person score (large warm surfaces such as wood or sand).

key_numbers.meaning: skin-colour coverage fraction of the frame before the penalty applies
penalty per unit of excess coverage

stages.name: Evidence pooling
stages.computes: Within each detector family (face, bust, figure, face-detail, clothed) the per-size best matches are combined as mostly the maximum plus some of the mean. Each family gets an offset, and the strongest family counts strongly. Small sums reward several families being at least weakly positive, plus a clothed-torso bonus. Face and figure coverage add a bonus when the pattern recurs across regions.

key_numbers.meaning: face family: weight on best size vs mean over sizes (others 0.70 to 0.74 best)
weight of the single most convincing family
family level above which it counts toward agreement
extra direct weight on the clothed-torso family

d.decision: All the evidence is summed into one person margin: the strongest family, the agreement term, the clothed bonus, the recurrence bonuses, the edge-orientation, colour-layout and skin-area scene terms. "Person" is predicted when the margin is positive and "no person" otherwise. The two class scores are plus and minus half the margin.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes. The colour cast correction is set by that image's mean colour, with a dead zone and saturation. Each detector searches every position and keeps the best match, after the position penalty. Sizes and tilts are searched and the best and mean are kept per family. The most convincing family is chosen by maximum. Coverage uses regional best matches. There is no iteration, branching beyond these maxima, or sorting.

d.summary: A hand-built head-and-shoulders detector looks for people. It slides candidate head windows over the photo at 8 head sizes and 1 or 2 aspect ratios per size. At each position it scores four alternative person explanations made of many soft cues: an exposed skin-coloured face over clothing, a detailed close-up face, a covered or turned-away head on a standing figure, and a face matched against rendered face drawings. It also adds a photo-wide prior built from scene-type cues and skin layout. The photo is called 'person' if the best window anywhere scores above zero, with a small bonus when several separate image regions also score well.
d.references: 48 synthetic frontal face drawings, rendered in code at 48x48 and averaged down to 12x12 brightness patterns. Each is an oval head with shading, dark eye bands, cheeks, nose, a dark mouth line, a chin highlight and a dark hairline. They cover every combination of: head turn (left, frontal, right), tilt (two directions), side lighting (two directions), with or without glasses, and with or without a fringe. They are stored two ways: with only overall brightness removed, and with row and column averages also removed so stripes and gradients do not match. Fixed scene probes are also used: 6 elliptical plate outlines (rim ring and centre disc) at fixed positions, and fixed image bands for ground, water and snow.

stages.name: Skin-colour map
stages.computes: Each pixel gets a soft 'skin likelihood' from its warm red-to-yellow hue, a moderate saturation, enough red and red slightly above green. This is computed a second time after a mild grey-world white-balance correction based on the photo's average colour, and the larger value is kept (the corrected one counts slightly less).

key_numbers.meaning: (green minus blue)/(red minus blue): the accepted skin hue band
accepted range of the colour-strength ratio
weight given to the white-balance-corrected skin estimate
maximum per-channel colour-cast gain

stages.name: Photo-wide scene prior
stages.computes: Measures whole-photo context and turns it into a bias added to every window. Mown grass, sea with white foam, snow fields, warm bright tones and a busy centre against a smooth background raise the bias. Long straight edges (rooms, vehicles), food colours, a white plate rim around coloured contents, and large areas of skin-coloured material lower it. Very little skin colour overall also lowers it.

key_numbers.meaning: lower band of the photo checked for grass or turf (pixels out of 96)
length of the strips over which straight edges must keep their direction to count as man-made
strength of the plate/dish penalty, the largest scene term
overall skin-colour fraction at which the 'too much warm material' penalty ramps in

stages.name: Skin layout prior
stages.computes: At 4 sizes it looks for compact skin patches that stand out from their surroundings and are not part of long horizontal or vertical bands. The strongest such patch raises the bias. More skin in the upper part of the photo than the lower part raises it, and the reverse lowers it. Many patches at once (diffuse warm texture) lowers it.

key_numbers.meaning: patch sizes searched
upper and lower bands compared for skin amount
patch centres below this are ignored

stages.name: Oriented outline maps per head size
stages.computes: For each head size it smooths brightness and two colour-difference channels, then measures edge strength in four directions (horizontal, vertical, two diagonals). Each is normalised by how busy the surrounding area is, so edges count only when they stand out from clutter.

key_numbers.meaning: edge-measuring step
area used to judge the local amount of clutter

stages.name: Window search over positions and sizes
stages.computes: Candidate face centres are placed on a regular grid. At each centre a head window of a given height and width is checked, with height and width setting where all later probes land.

key_numbers.meaning: face sizes tried
two face aspect ratios per size (one at 80 px)
spacing of candidate centres, coarser for bigger heads

stages.name: Face-region cues
stages.computes: Inside the window it checks several things. Is there skin in the centre, more than on the ring just outside (cheeks, above, below)? Do the two cheeks match in colour? Are the eye bands darker than cheeks, forehead and nose bridge, and is the mouth darker than cheeks and chin? These darkness tests are scaled by the window's own contrast. It also looks for dark hair above or at the temples, and for a colour change from each cheek to the background beside the head, on both sides.

key_numbers.meaning: eye-band positions relative to the face centre
mouth and chin probe positions
position of the region above the face that should be darker
distance to the background patches beside the head

stages.name: Body cues below the head
stages.computes: It checks that clothing below the head differs in colour from the face. It checks for a shoulder line: patches below and beside the head differ from the space just above the shoulders, and both sides change in the same way. It checks that the torso contrasts with the scene further out, for skin-coloured hand or arm patches at typical arm offsets that match the face's colour, and for leg regions far below that differ from their sides. Body cues are only counted when the body would fit inside the photo.

key_numbers.meaning: centre of the shirt region
shoulder patches compared with patches at 0.47 h below, +/-0.92 w

key_numbers.value: arms at 1.3 to 2.6 h below, 0.7 to 1.56 w aside
key_numbers.meaning: places where a skin patch counts as a hand or arm
leg probe, needs about 3 to 4.6 head heights of room below

stages.name: Outline shape cues
stages.computes: It reads the outline maps at points along an expected crown, temples, jaw and sloping shoulders, with two shoulder heights allowed. Edges must appear on both sides, and edges just off the expected outline count against the match.

key_numbers.meaning: top-of-head outline position
side-of-head outline positions
alternative downward shift allowed for the shoulder line

stages.name: Face-drawing match
stages.computes: Only for heads at least 11 px tall. The window's brightness is sampled into a 12x12 patch, its contrast is normalised, and it is compared with all 48 face drawings in both forms. The best match is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: smallest head height at which drawing matching is used
sample grid over 1.22 h by 1.24 w

stages.name: Combine into four person hypotheses
stages.computes: Weighted sums of the cues give four scores: 'skin face over clothes', 'detailed face', 'covered head on a standing figure' (outline, shoulders, legs) and 'portrait' (drawing match). The best of the four is kept, then a position prior and the scene bias are added. The prior favours central and upper positions, penalises heads in the bottom third and penalises tiny heads. The score is lightly smoothed with neighbouring positions.

key_numbers.meaning: rows where a head centre is increasingly penalised (up to -0.21)
preferred head height in the frame
head heights below this get a small-head penalty

d.decision: Two values are taken over all positions and sizes (for each size, the window scores of its two aspect ratios are blended at 0.86 of the higher plus 0.14 of the lower). The first is the single best window score. The second comes from dividing the photo into a 4x4 grid of 24 px cells, taking the best score in each cell, and keeping the third-highest cell. That third-best cell adds up to 0.044 to the best score. If the total is above 0 the photo is called 'person', otherwise 'no person'. This is a hard threshold, not a comparison between two class scores.
d.adapts_per_image: Several things change from photo to photo. White balance is corrected using the photo's own average colour. Edge strength is normalised by local clutter, and facial darkness tests by the window's own contrast. Every position and size is searched and only the best is kept, and the best cells are ranked to take the third-highest. Arm colour is checked against the colour measured on that image's candidate face. The face-drawing test only runs at head sizes of at least 11 px. The best of 4 hypotheses is chosen per window. A photo-wide scene bias is computed from that photo's content.

clusters.approach: Bank of separate hand-drawn template detectors (face template on skin+brightness maps, head-and-shoulders, full-figure outline from oriented edges, clothed torso), each scanned over scales and pooled by region with position penalties, then fused with fixed weights and agreement or extra-credit terms plus scene-context cues against a fixed threshold

Head-centred candidate search: a head box slid over positions and sizes, each candidate scored with a hand-placed layout of head, hair, face-feature, shoulder, torso and leg probes (alternative hypotheses, best kept, position priors, multi-person bonus), plus whole-scene context priors (fields, snow, straight lines, skin amount)

pairs.shared: Hand-built skin map, separate searches (head/shoulders, full-body outline, face cues) each giving a best score, scene context, fixed-threshold sum
pairs.differs: A uses drawn face templates and oriented-edge body templates with many detector families; B uses a head-centred box layout, strip-based body outline and skin-blob faces, combined by sorted-rank blend

pairs.shared: Many hand-tuned cues for face, head over clothing, body outline, scene context (grass, snow), multi-person bonus, summed against a threshold
pairs.differs: C scores head candidates with one head-relative layout covering head, face, body and hands, picks max of three hypotheses, adds skin blobs and plates; A runs independent template detectors fused by weights

pairs.shared: Same pipeline: skin and brightness maps, oriented edges in 4 directions with perpendicular suppression, drawn face templates, head-and-shoulders, full-figure templates at several scales, regional pooling with border/bottom penalties, scene cues, fixed-weight vote against a fixed reference with extra credit for strong detectors
pairs.differs: A adds a detailed face checklist and crowd term; D adds clothed-figure detector and explicit cross-detector agreement map; tuning differs

pairs.shared: Drawn face templates on skin and brightness, head-and-shoulders outline, standing-figure outline, clothed torso under head, position penalties, scene colour-layout cues, weighted fusion
pairs.differs: E adds white balance, pools families by max plus mean with agreement term, uses inside/outside contour point pairs rather than edge-direction maps, and straight-line scene penalties; A has detailed face checklist and crowd term

pairs.differs: F is a single head-window search with body cues and four hypotheses, rendered face-drawing matching, and best-window decision; A fuses independent detector families by weights

pairs.shared: Separate head-and-shoulders, full-body, and face searches, each best score; scene cues (clothing colours, field, straight lines); fixed threshold
pairs.differs: D uses drawn templates, edge maps, pyramid scales, agreement maps and per-detector margins; B uses head-centred box layout, strip outline, skin blobs and a rank-weighted blend

pairs.shared: White-balanced skin map, head window slid over positions and sizes with head-relative probes for face, hair, background, shoulders, torso and legs, facial features, alternative hypothesis scores with best kept, position penalties, multi-region bonus, scene context
pairs.differs: B adds separate full-body outline and skin-blob searches blended by rank; F adds edge-outline cues and rendered face-drawing matching inside the single window search

pairs.differs: C is a single head-candidate search with per-candidate layout and hypothesis max; D runs independent template detectors with agreement maps and weighted margins
