steps.step: Per-pixel skin likelihood from a fixed colour window
steps.note: All compute a soft skin score from opponent colours with hand-set bounds. N1 adds a pale-skin variant; N3 blends loose and strict versions.

steps.step: Per-image white-balance or colour-cast correction before skin testing
steps.note: Only N3 removes part of the image's mean colour cast (0.42, with dead zone and saturation). It matches P2 and P3's grey-world correction. N1 and N2 use fixed colour rules only.

steps.step: Slide a head window over positions at a fixed set of sizes, keeping the best
steps.note: Every network scans positions at fixed scales and takes the max, as the programs do. The scale sets differ (N1 5 scales, N2 4, N3 11 settings, vs 19/18/8-15 in the programs). P2's block-winner pruning is not reproduced.

steps.step: Skin in face centre greater than in surrounding ring
steps.note: All networks have a skin oval minus non-skin surround term.

steps.step: Head contrast: face differs from background on both sides, hair or cap darker above
steps.note: Present in all. N2 uses a soft minimum over sectors and N1 the weaker side, which matches the programs' both-sides requirement. The programs' matching of left and right backgrounds (P1) appears only partly in the networks (N3 ring imbalance, N2 left/right background penalty for figures).

steps.step: Facial features: eyes darker than cheeks and brow, bright nose bridge, dark mouth vs chin, symmetry
steps.note: N1 has a 10-contrast checklist and N2 11 contrast patterns plus symmetry. N3 covers eyes, mouth and hair but has no explicit nose-bridge or symmetry term beyond an eye-difference penalty.

steps.step: Small in-plane head roll or tilt variants of the face layout
steps.note: A fixed set of tilts in all: P2 ±0.24 rad, P3 drawings with tilt. Networks: N1 12 degrees, N2 0.2 rad, N3 20 degrees.

steps.step: Face-detail cues gated or ramped by head size
steps.note: P1 uses features only for heads of at least 6.5 px, P2 ramps from 3 to 11 px, and P3 matches drawings only at 11 px or more. N3 forms its detail score only at its largest scales. N1 and N2 apply the face checks at every scale.

steps.step: Contrast normalised by local brightness spread, clutter or window contrast
steps.note: All three networks are described as not normalising by any image-measured quantity. Their perpendicular-direction suppression and saturation are fixed nonlinearities, not local normalisation.

steps.step: Correlation with rendered face drawings (normalised 12x12 patch match)
steps.note: The networks use fixed blob-drawn face templates that are summed linearly. P3 normalises the patch's contrast and takes the best of 48 renderings in two forms. These are related but not the same computation.

steps.step: Chest or shoulders below the head: clothing differs from face, shoulders differ from background beside them
steps.note: N1 has torso vs sides and upper arms vs above shoulders. N2 has chest vs background, face vs chest and garment colour. N3 has a clothed torso vs flanks and above the shoulders.

steps.step: Head, neck and shoulder outline from oriented or inside-vs-outside edges, with off-outline penalty
steps.note: N2's 12-point polyline with parallel-offset subtraction closely matches P3's off-outline penalty. N1 runs 4 brightness outline tests. N3 uses inside/outside point pairs.

steps.step: Full-body outline or stick figure: edges along both body sides at several levels, background and garment consistency
steps.note: N1 has 9 pose outlines on 4 edge orientations (close to P2's stick figure). N2 has standing and clothed figures with side contrasts and long side edges. N3 has 6 contour segments head to legs (close to P1's strips).

steps.step: Body lean or pose variants
steps.note: P1 leans ±0.42 and P2 tilts ±0.55 and ±0.48. N1 has striding, throwing and sitting poses rather than leans. N3 leans only its clothed torso (±0.43). N2 varies size only.

steps.step: Lower-body evidence counted only when the body fits inside the frame
steps.note: The programs switch body cues to neutral when the body would fall off the bottom of the frame. The networks only apply fixed bottom-of-frame position penalties.

steps.step: Hand or arm skin patches matching the face's own colour
steps.note: This needs a per-image comparison with the candidate face's colour. N2's arm cross-sections are brightness contrasts, not colour matches.

steps.step: Several alternative person hypotheses per candidate, keeping the max
steps.note: The programs take the max over hypotheses at each candidate. N1 and N2 each run separate detectors to their own image-level max and then add them with fixed weights. N3 takes the max over families at image level (weight 0.6). N2's same-site agreement map is the closest to per-candidate combination.

steps.step: Rank-weighted blend of detector scores (sorted, 0.73/0.22/0.05)
steps.note: N3 gives its strongest family extra weight. N1 and N2 use fixed per-detector weights with no sorting.

steps.step: Position prior: penalise heads low in the frame or near side edges
steps.note: Fixed position maps in all networks.

steps.step: Tiny-head penalty
steps.note: No network description mentions a penalty tied to the smallest scales.

steps.step: Second or third person and crowd bonus
steps.note: The programs search for separate strong candidates (non-overlap test, row of heads, third-best cell). The networks use fixed-grid stand-ins: N1 averages regional face scores above 0.43, N2 averages quadrants and strong-match area, and N3 records 3x3 regional coverage.

steps.step: Connected-component skin blobs scored for face-like shape
steps.note: No network does connected grouping. N2's centre-surround isolated skin spots are a fixed-filter stand-in.

steps.step: Compact isolated skin patch prior (centre-surround at a few sizes)
steps.note: N2 has skin spots that stand out from their surround, which matches P3's step 3. N1 compares only central and border skin share.

steps.step: Skin in the upper frame vs the lower frame
steps.note: N1 uses central vs border skin, not an upper vs lower split.

steps.step: Large skin-coloured area penalty
steps.note: N3 penalises skin coverage above 0.11 of the frame. N1 only counts border skin against. N2 computes the image skin average, but it has no effect.

steps.step: Grass, snow or water in the lower part of the frame
steps.note: All have fixed ground-colour probes weighted toward the bottom.

steps.step: Architectural straight horizontal and vertical lines penalty
steps.note: N2 has long-line templates and N3 axis-aligned edge dominance. N1's context step does not describe a straight-line penalty.

steps.step: Saturated red, blue or magenta clothing patches
steps.note: N3 places red and blue in the middle rows of a 4x4 layout rather than detecting blobs. This is close enough to count as the same cue.

steps.step: Centre more detailed or salient than the border
steps.note: N1 compares fine detail in the centre with the border. N3 compares centre texture with side columns. N2 has only location maps on its detectors.

steps.step: Dinner plate ellipse penalty
steps.note: No network has a plate probe.

steps.step: Playing-field line markings
Black-and-white photo detection and bonus
Fixed threshold on the summed evidence
steps.note: All give a hard binary decision against a constant.

network_only.step: Edge orientation maps with perpendicular-direction suppression (0.73) and soft saturation (above 0.17 counts 18%)
Edge orientation maps with perpendicular-direction suppression (0.65)
Sky-cyan colour high in the frame and yellow at the border as context votes
Piecewise extra credit in the final vote for face, head and detail scores above fixed levels (0.91, 1.0, 0.72), and diminishing returns on body above 0.44
Cross-detector agreement map: face, head and figure maps summed at the same site minus part of the strongest
Per-detector strong-match area: average excess over threshold across a 6x6 grid
Extra bonus for each detector margin above zero
Sports-scene clue: field colour combined with a bright clothing blob
Diagonal straight lines raise the person score
Agreement reward for several detector families being at least weakly positive
Mean over sizes blended with the max per detector family

cover.verdict: The three networks reproduce the programs' main detector structure. Each has a skin map, a position and scale search for a skin-centred face with non-skin surround, darker hair and dark eyes and mouth, a chest or shoulder contrast check, oriented-edge head and body outlines, fixed position priors, ground-colour, straight-line and clothing-colour scene cues, and a hard threshold. To that extent they solve the task with the same set of cues. They differ in how the cues are combined and adapted. Every program normalises contrasts by local brightness spread, clutter or window contrast, and no network does. Hypotheses are maxed per candidate in the programs but summed across detectors at image level in the networks. Size gating, frame-fit gating, the second-person search and connected skin blobs are replaced by fixed stand-ins. The networks also leave out face-colour-matched hands, the plate penalty, field lines, black-and-white detection, the tiny-head penalty and (in N1 and N2) white balance.

d.summary: A nearest-match method that compares the image against many synthetic digits. About 99 hand-drawn stroke skeletons are rendered with random distortions to make tens of thousands of example digits. Each test image is described by several cues: oriented stroke and edge energy on a coarse grid, a blurred ink layout, concavities found by looking along sightlines, enclosed holes found by filling from the border, stroke endings, and ink lying outside the rows that contain a loop. The class score blends (a) how close the best whole-image examples come and (b) how well the top part and bottom part each match examples drawn with the same width and slant.
d.references: The references are synthetic, with no real training images. They start from about 99 hand-written vector stroke drawings of the digits, given as line and curve paths in a unit box: roughly 8 to 13 per class, each with a frequency weight and a nominal width-to-height ratio. Each example picks a drawing at random according to those weights. The drawing is then randomly warped (width, slant, shear, bending, wobble), drawn with a soft elliptical pen of random thickness and varying pressure, scaled to fit a box of about 20 pixels, and centred by its centre of mass near (13.7, 13.7), with about 0.4 pixels of jitter. The cue descriptions of these examples are stored. (1) There are 4096 whole-digit examples per class, 40,960 in all, split into 4 random groups of 1024 per class. (2) There are 2304 part examples per class, 23,040 in all: 9 width and slant settings (width factor e^-0.24, 1 or e^0.24, crossed with slant -0.2, 0.12 or 0.46) times 256 examples each, rendered with smaller random variation. For these only the top-region and bottom-region cues are kept.

stages.name: Oriented stroke and edge energy
stages.computes: The full 28x28 image is probed with 12 smooth oriented detectors. Eight are signed edge detectors at 45 degree steps, which respond to an ink-to-background transition in one direction. Four are line detectors for thin bright strokes at 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees. Only positive responses are kept. They are averaged over 4x4 pixel cells placed every 3 pixels, giving a 9x9 grid per detector, and large values are compressed.

key_numbers.meaning: size of each detector's footprint, in pixels
Gaussian widths in pixels for the edge and line detectors: across the stroke, then along it
averaging cells in pixels, giving a 9x9 grid over the image
above a cell value of 0.26, any excess is reduced to 34% (a soft knee)

stages.name: Coarse ink layout
stages.computes: Ink is averaged over 4x4 pixel windows every 2 pixels, giving a 13x13 grid. A separate 2x2 average gives a 14x14 low-resolution copy of the digit, which the later cues use.

key_numbers.meaning: blur window and spacing in pixels for the 13x13 layout
block size in pixels for the 14x14 low-resolution image

stages.name: Sightline concavity tests
stages.computes: For each cell of the 14x14 image, ink is summed along straight rays to the border in 8 directions, and each ray is capped at 1 (blocked or open). The cell's own ink counts against it. Ten tests then mark background cells: cells between strokes on opposite sides (4 axes); cells enclosed on 3 of the 4 straight-line sides with the 4th side open, which is a bay facing up, down, left or right (4 tests); cells blocked on all 4 straight-line sides; and cells blocked on all 8 sides. The results are averaged over 2x2 cells to give a 7x7 grid per test.

key_numbers.meaning: how strongly ink along a straight or diagonal ray counts toward blocking it
penalty for the cell's own ink, so only background cells count as inside a concavity
how many blocked rays each test needs: opposite pair, 3 sides with one open, all 4 straight sides, all 8 directions

stages.name: Hole filling from the border
stages.computes: On the 14x14 image, a grey-level fill floods in from the image border and is stopped by ink walls (repeated 3x3 minimum spreading, 16 passes). At each cell it measures how far the background sits below the lowest wall between that cell and the border, which is the depth of an enclosed hole. This depth is summarised two ways: averaged over 2x2 cells (a 7x7 map), and as the maximum in three horizontal bands (top, middle, bottom).

key_numbers.meaning: number of fill passes, one cell of spread per pass on the 14x14 grid
bands at coarse rows 0-5, 4-9 and 8-13 (top, middle and bottom thirds) that report whether a loop is present

stages.name: Stroke ending detection
stages.computes: On the 14x14 image, 16 templates look for a stroke that ends. Each needs ink at the centre and continuing in one of 8 directions, with no ink to the sides, the back diagonals or behind. There are two reach lengths, and the larger response for each direction is kept. Each direction's strongest response is then taken over 5x5 cell windows spaced 3 cells apart, giving a 4x4 grid of where endings of each direction occur.

key_numbers.meaning: how far apart, in coarse cells (about 3.5 and 5.2 pixels), the checks behind and to the sides of a stroke end are placed
minimum response for an ending to count
windows in coarse cells for the 4x4 grid of ending locations

stages.name: Ink outside loop rows
stages.computes: For each row of the 14x14 image, it finds the deepest enclosed hole in that row and spreads this up and down by 2 rows. It subtracts 2.5 times that from the ink, which keeps only ink in rows away from any loop: stems, tails and bars. That ink is averaged over 4x4 cells every 2 cells, giving a 6x6 grid.

key_numbers.meaning: vertical reach of the loop zone, in coarse rows (about 4 pixels)
how strongly being near a loop removes ink
averaging cells in coarse units for the 6x6 grid

stages.name: Whole-digit comparison against examples
stages.computes: The stroke-energy, ink-layout and concavity descriptions are each standardised for this image and compared with each stored example by correlation. The hole map, hole bands, ending grid and loop-free ink are compared by negative squared difference. All seven comparisons are added with fixed weights to give one agreement score per example.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of the correlations for stroke energy, ink layout and concavity
weights of the squared-difference penalties for hole map, hole bands, stroke endings and loop-free ink
stored whole-digit examples per class

stages.name: Whole-digit class score
stages.computes: For each class, the examples are split into 4 groups and the best agreement in each group is kept. The class score is the average of the 4 group bests plus the single best.

key_numbers.meaning: random subsets per class whose best matches are averaged

stages.name: Top and bottom part matching
stages.computes: Two regions are cut from the stroke-energy and concavity grids. The top uses grid rows 0-5 of 9 (about pixel rows 0-20) and concavity rows 0-3 of 7 (about pixel rows 0-15). The bottom uses rows 3-8 (about pixel rows 9-27) and concavity rows 3-6 (about pixel rows 12-27). Each region is standardised and correlated with the stored part examples. For each class and each of the 9 width and slant settings, the best top match and the best bottom match are found separately (they may come from different examples) and added. The best setting is then kept.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of stroke-energy and concavity correlation within each part
width and slant settings that the top and bottom must share
part examples per class per setting

d.decision: Each class gets 0.61 times its whole-digit score (mean of 4 group-best matches plus the overall best match) plus 0.39 times its parts score (best top match plus best bottom match within the best shared width and slant setting). The class with the highest total wins.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes. It searches all stored examples and keeps the best match per group, per class, per part and per width and slant setting. The top and bottom parts can be matched to different examples, but they must share a setting. The stroke-energy, ink-layout, concavity and part descriptions are each standardised by their own mean and spread for that image before correlation. The hole fill propagates from the border according to the image's own ink walls, over a fixed 16 passes. The loop-free ink cue removes rows chosen by where this image's holes are. There is no branching and no position or scale search on the test image itself.

d.summary: Each digit is first straightened and partly size-normalised. It is then compared against a large library of synthetic digit drawings in two passes. A quick global comparison of coarse ink, stroke-direction and enclosed-hole layouts picks the 16 most similar drawings of each class. A slower comparison then lets nine image patches shift slightly and coherently to line up with each shortlisted drawing, and adds a small penalty for mismatched stroke ends and junctions. The class whose best two drawings fit most cheaply wins.
d.references: The library holds 163,840 synthetic digit images, 16,384 per class, rendered procedurally when the method is built. For each class, hand-written parametric stroke recipes (lines, rounded corners, cubic curves and elliptical arcs) describe several writing styles. 0 has 3 styles, 1 has 4, 2 has 9, 3 has 4, 4 has 5, 5 has 6, 6 has 5, 7 has 7, 8 has 7 and 9 has 10, with variants like a 1 with a flag and base, a crossed 7, an open-top 4, a looped 2 and a two-loop 8. Each recipe has randomised control points. Each rendering then gets a random smooth warp (affine terms, quadratic bending, small sinusoidal wobble), a random width, slant and shear, and a random pen thickness that varies along the stroke and is slightly elliptical. It is fitted into a box about 21 px across, centred in 28x28, and drawn as anti-aliased ink. Every rendering goes through the same normalisation as the input. For each one the method stores three things: a coarse descriptor (6x6 ink, 4 direction channels, aspect, slant and holes), a 14x14 six-channel detail map quantised to 32 levels, and 5x5 maps of stroke-end and junction density.

stages.name: Straighten and resize
stages.computes: Finds the ink centroid, the slant (how horizontal position drifts with height, from second moments) and the ink spread across and down after slant removal. It resamples the image around the centroid to remove the slant and pull the width and height spreads partway toward standard values, so narrow digits stay somewhat narrow. It keeps the log width-to-height ratio and the slant as extra cues.

key_numbers.meaning: maximum slant corrected, in horizontal pixels per vertical pixel
target horizontal and vertical ink spread (standard deviation, px)
exponents that make the size correction only partial (horizontal / vertical)
limits on the horizontal and vertical rescale factors

stages.name: Enclosed-background map
stages.computes: For each pixel it finds the lowest ink barrier that any path from that pixel to the image border must cross, minus the pixel's own ink. Background inside closed loops (the counters of 0, 6, 8, 9 and so on) scores high, and open background scores near zero. The value is estimated with repeated row and column sweeps in both directions rather than an exact search.

key_numbers.meaning: number of forward and backward sweep rounds that spread escape routes from the border

stages.name: Stroke direction maps
stages.computes: After a light 3x3 blur it measures the local intensity gradient. It splits the edge energy into four stroke-axis channels (horizontal, vertical and the two diagonals), treating opposite directions as the same. Each channel responds to edges aligned with its axis and gives zero for edges that are badly misaligned.

key_numbers.meaning: orientation axes, 45 degrees apart

stages.name: Coarse descriptor
stages.computes: It sums ink, each direction channel and the enclosed-background map in soft windows on a 6x6 grid, normalises each group to unit length and weights it. It adds soft-binned encodings of the aspect ratio and slant. The result is one fixed-length signature of overall layout, stroke directions, holes and proportions.

key_numbers.value: 6x6 at 4 px spacing, Gaussian width 2.4 px
key_numbers.meaning: coarse sampling grid of window centres (3.5 to 23.5 px)
relative weights of ink, direction, aspect, slant and hole groups
soft bins for log(width/height)
soft bins for slant

stages.name: Shortlist per class
stages.computes: It scores the input's coarse signature against every stored drawing's signature by normalised similarity, roughly a cosine. For each class it keeps the 16 most similar drawings and their similarity scores.

key_numbers.meaning: candidate drawings kept per class

stages.name: Fine detail maps
stages.computes: It builds half-resolution 14x14 maps of six channels: blurred ink, the four direction channels (boosted) and the enclosed-background map (damped). Values are quantised to 32 levels, the same way the stored drawings are.

key_numbers.meaning: detail map resolution (each cell is 2x2 input pixels)
emphasis on direction channels and on enclosed background relative to ink

stages.name: Deformable patch matching
stages.computes: It covers the 14x14 frame with a 3x3 arrangement of overlapping soft patches. Each patch may shift up to one half-res cell (about 2 input px) in any direction to best match the candidate drawing, scored by squared difference over all six channels. Shifts are penalised in proportion to their size and to how much ink the patch holds. A tree of neighbour links rooted at the centre patch charges for disagreement between adjacent shifts, and the method finds the cheapest overall arrangement exactly. The best total is divided by the combined ink of input and candidate.

key_numbers.meaning: patch centres and size on the 14x14 grid
maximum patch shift (about 2 input px)
cost per unit of shift away from centre
cost per unit of squared shift difference between linked neighbour patches

stages.name: Stroke ends and junctions
stages.computes: It thresholds the normalised image and thins the strokes to one-pixel skeletons (up to 12 rounds of peeling boundary pixels that do not break connectivity). It marks endpoints (one neighbour) and junctions (three or more branches) and spreads each over a 5x5 grid of soft windows. It compares these maps with the candidate's and charges a capped, weighted squared difference, so ends count twice as much as junctions.

key_numbers.meaning: ink level counted as stroke for thinning
grid for end and junction density
caps on a single cell's difference and on the total penalty
weights for endpoint and junction mismatch

stages.name: Combine per candidate
stages.computes: For each shortlisted drawing the total cost is the deformable-match cost, minus 0.43 times the coarse similarity, plus the end and junction penalty.

key_numbers.meaning: how much the coarse similarity lowers the cost

d.decision: For each class it sorts the 16 candidate costs, takes 0.77 times the lowest plus 0.23 times the second lowest, and predicts the class with the smallest combined value. A class therefore wins only if at least two of its drawings fit well.
d.adapts_per_image: Several steps depend on the particular image. The slant correction and partial rescale use the image's own centroid, slant and spread. The coarse signature groups are normalised to unit length per image. The shortlist is a search that keeps the top 16 drawings per class out of 16,384. For each candidate, the method searches for the best-cost arrangement of patch shifts, and the shift and neighbour penalties plus the final division scale with the ink present. Thinning runs until nothing changes or 12 rounds pass. The final step sorts each class's candidates and keeps the best two.

d.summary: The digit is compared against tens of thousands of synthetic handwritten digits that are drawn from hand-made stroke skeletons with random distortion and pen width. Similarity to each one combines three things: agreement of local stroke-direction maps, agreement of the blurred ink layout, and agreement of where enclosed holes (loops) are and how deep they are. A second comparison scores the upper and lower parts of the digit separately, letting each slide slightly. Each class's score comes from its best-matching drawings plus a bonus for how consistently its drawings match, and the two comparisons are added together.
d.references: Synthetic digit drawings rendered at build time from hand-written stroke skeletons. Each class has 4 to 10 skeleton styles (for example open and closed-top 4s, crossed and plain 7s, 1s with and without a flag or base), given as smooth spline or straight-line point lists in a 7 by 10 box, and each style has a frequency weight. For each class, 4096 drawings are made (40,960 in total). Each one picks a style, randomly changes its width (about 0.67 to 1.34x, from 0.55x for 8), slant, bow and wobble, sets pen radius to about 0.8 to 2.3 px with thickness varying along the stroke, scales it to fit about 19.4 to 20.4 px, and centres it by centre of mass with up to plus or minus 0.65 px of jitter. Some 0s, 6s and 8s (14%, 47% for 8) have the end of the stroke trimmed so the loop is left open. Three things are stored per drawing: its 8-direction edge map on a 9x9 grid, its blurred ink on a 13x13 grid, and its 6x6 hole-depth map. The first 1024 drawings per class also store upper-part and lower-part edge maps at 5 small offsets.

stages.name: Directional stroke edges
stages.computes: Measures how brightness changes along 8 directions at every pixel (every 45 degrees, so both sides of each stroke edge show separately), keeping only the positive responses.

key_numbers.meaning: edge directions, 45 degrees apart (4 orientations, each with 2 polarities)
size and smoothing of the local brightness-slope detector

stages.name: Coarse edge-direction map
stages.computes: Sums each direction's edge strength with Gaussian weights over overlapping patches, giving a 9x9 grid of 8-direction edge histograms that covers the image. The map is shifted to zero mean and scaled to unit spread, both for the whole grid and separately for its upper 6 rows and lower 6 rows.

key_numbers.meaning: pooling patch for each grid cell
spacing between grid cells, giving a 9x9 grid
upper and lower parts of the grid (each about two thirds of the height, overlapping in the middle)

stages.name: Blurred ink layout
stages.computes: Blurs the ink and samples it on a 13x13 grid, then shifts it to zero mean and scales it to unit spread.

key_numbers.meaning: blur applied to the ink
sampling spacing, giving a 13x13 grid

stages.name: Gap closing and downsampling
stages.computes: Thickens strokes by 1 px in every direction, then thins them back (a 3x3 closing), which seals small gaps. It averages the closed ink with the original ink and halves the resolution to 14x14.

key_numbers.meaning: neighbourhood used to close gaps
resolution of the map used to find loops (2x2 px per cell)

stages.name: Hole finding by flood fill
stages.computes: Floods background in from the image border and lets it spread through 4-connected cells, where ink acts as walls of varying height. Each cell's final water level is the lowest wall it must cross to reach the border, and subtracting the ink there gives how deeply that cell sits inside an enclosed loop. Background connected to the border scores 0.

key_numbers.meaning: number of spreading steps across the 14x14 grid (enough to cover it)

stages.name: Loop location map
stages.computes: Takes the deepest enclosure within each overlapping 4x4 cell window (stride 2), giving a 6x6 map of where loops are and how closed they are. It then measures each value against three depth levels (0, 1/3, 2/3).

key_numbers.meaning: sector size and spacing on the 14x14 grid (about 8 px wide, every 4 px), giving 6x6 sectors
depth levels used for a piecewise-linear depth comparison

stages.name: Whole-digit match against every drawing
stages.computes: For each of the 40,960 drawings, the match score adds three parts. Edge-map correlation is weighted 0.76 and blurred-ink correlation 0.24. The loop part is roughly the negative summed absolute difference between the image's and the drawing's 6x6 hole-depth maps, scaled by 0.011, plus a term that is the same for every drawing.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of edge-direction correlation
weight of blurred-ink correlation
weight per sector of the hole-depth disagreement

stages.name: Whole-digit class vote
stages.computes: Splits each class's 4096 drawings into 16 fixed groups of 256 and keeps the best match in each group. The class score is the best of those 16 values plus 0.4 times their average.

key_numbers.meaning: how each class's drawings are split up
weight of the average of the group bests

stages.name: Part-by-part match with small shifts
stages.computes: Uses the first 1024 drawings per class. The image's upper-part edge map is correlated with the drawing's upper part at 5 placements (unshifted, or one grid cell up, down, left or right), and the best placement is kept. Any shifted placement costs a small penalty. The lower part is scored the same way on its own. Score per drawing = 0.5 x best upper correlation + 0.5 x best lower correlation + the same hole-depth term as before.

key_numbers.meaning: largest shift each part may make on its own
penalty for using a shifted placement
weight of each part's correlation
drawings per class used for part matching

stages.name: Part-based class vote
stages.computes: Groups the part scores the same way (16 groups of 64): the class score is the best group value plus 0.4 times the average of the group bests, multiplied by 0.85.

key_numbers.meaning: how each class's part-matched drawings are split up
weight of the part-based vote relative to the whole-digit vote

d.decision: Each class's final score is its whole-digit vote plus 0.85 times its part-based vote. Each vote is the best group-best match plus 0.4 times the average of the group bests. The class with the highest final score is the answer.
d.adapts_per_image: The method changes with each image in several ways. Edge maps, part maps and ink maps are rescaled using that image's own mean and spread. For every drawing it keeps the best of 16 groups and the best within each group, which in effect searches for the closest drawing. In the part comparison, each part picks its best placement out of 5 small shifts. The flood fill runs a fixed 21 steps, but how far the water spreads, and so which regions count as holes, depends on where the image's strokes are.

d.summary: This is nearest-neighbour matching against a large library of synthetic digits. Each image is straightened and rescaled to a standard frame. It is then described by where strokes run in each of six edge directions over a coarse grid and a fine grid, by its ink layout, by its width-to-height ratio, and by where enclosed holes sit vertically. A cheap comparison picks the 32 most similar library examples of each digit, a costlier comparison with local shifts allowed scores those finalists, and each digit's score is a weighted mix of its three best finalists.
d.references: 143,360 synthetic digit images, 14,336 per class, generated procedurally before classification. Each one is drawn from a hand-written pen model of that digit: strokes are Bezier curves, lines and ovals with randomised control points, and many digits have several style variants (open or closed 0, 1 with or without a base and flag, looped or plain 2, 4 open or closed at the top, crossed 7, single-loop or two-loop 8, and so on). Each drawing is then randomly warped (width, lean, shear, bend, taper, waist, ripple), given a random stroke thickness, a tapered pen tip and an elliptical brush, scaled to about 20 px and rasterised with soft edges. Every synthetic image goes through the same straightening and description steps as the input, and only its descriptors are kept: a coarse 6x6x6 direction histogram, a fine 9x9x6 direction map, a 9x9 ink layout, the width-to-height ratio and a 6-band hole profile, all quantised to small integers.

stages.name: Slant estimate and straightening
stages.computes: Finds the ink's centre of mass and its slant (how far x drifts with y, from second moments). It then shears the image horizontally about the centre row to make the digit upright, using 88% of the measured slant.

key_numbers.meaning: Fraction of the measured slant that is removed (horizontal shift per pixel of height)
Largest slant allowed, in horizontal pixels per vertical pixel

stages.name: Bounding box and rescaling
stages.computes: In the straightened image (on a 44 px wide canvas, so nothing is cut off), finds the box around confident ink. Resamples so the box height becomes about 23 px and centres the box. Width is only partly normalised: the horizontal scale follows the box's width-to-height ratio raised to 0.66 and kept within a range, so narrow digits such as 1 are not stretched. Also records the log of the box's width-to-height ratio.

key_numbers.meaning: Brightness above which a pixel counts as ink when finding the box
Target digit height in the 28x28 output frame
Reference width: boxes narrower than this are not fully widened (exponent 0.66, scale factor kept within 0.65 to 1.62)

stages.name: Edge direction maps
stages.computes: Measures the brightness gradient at each pixel and splits it into six directed orientation channels 60 degrees apart, each the positive part of the gradient along that direction, squared and divided by edge strength. Each channel is softly averaged into a coarse 6x6 grid and a fine 9x9 grid of Gaussian cells. The values are square-rooted and each grid's descriptor is scaled to unit length.

key_numbers.meaning: Directed edge orientations (each sign of the gradient counted separately)
Coarse spatial grid for the quick comparison
Fine spatial grid for the detailed comparison
Gradient-strength offset that damps faint edges

stages.name: Ink layout
stages.computes: Averages raw ink into the same fine 9x9 Gaussian grid, square-roots it and scales it to unit length. The result is a blurred silhouette of where the ink lies.

key_numbers.meaning: Grid cells for the silhouette

stages.name: Hole profile
stages.computes: At three brightness cutoffs, finds background pixels that cannot be reached from the image border through background (enclosed holes). It counts those pixels per row, smooths the counts into six horizontal bands from top to bottom, and saturates each band. The three cutoffs are averaged, giving a height profile of where loops are.

key_numbers.meaning: Brightness levels below which a pixel counts as background for the hole search
Vertical zones (Gaussian spread 2.25 px) that report hole area by height
Most growth steps for the border-connected background search

stages.name: Quick shortlist per class
stages.computes: Scores every library example by how well its coarse direction histogram matches the input's. It subtracts a penalty for a different width-to-height ratio and a gentle penalty for a different hole profile in each band. The 32 best-scoring examples of each digit are kept.

key_numbers.meaning: Finalists kept per class
Cap on the log width-to-height difference used in the penalty

stages.name: Detailed rigid and elastic comparison
stages.computes: For each finalist, computes a rigid match (overlap of fine direction maps, plus overlap of ink silhouettes). It also computes an elastic mismatch: the fine grid is split into a 4x4 set of overlapping 3x3 cell patches with centre-weighted counting, each patch may shift the input by one cell in any of 8 directions or stay put for a small cost, and each patch keeps its lowest-cost shift. The patch costs are summed.

key_numbers.meaning: Largest local shift each patch may make on the 9x9 grid
Weight of the ink-silhouette difference relative to the direction difference in the elastic cost
Cost per cell of shift

stages.name: Combine evidence per finalist
stages.computes: Each finalist gets one score: 0.31 times the rigid direction match, plus 0.12 times the silhouette match, plus 0.23 times the quick score, minus 0.37 times the elastic mismatch, minus small penalties for differences in width-to-height ratio and hole profile.

key_numbers.meaning: Weight of the elastic mismatch, the largest single term
Weight of the mean hole-profile difference
Cap on the width-to-height log difference

d.decision: For each digit, the finalists' scores are sorted. The class score is 0.55 times the best plus 0.27 times the second best plus 0.18 times the third best. The digit with the highest class score wins.
d.adapts_per_image: Several steps depend on the particular image. Slant is measured on each image and removed. The bounding box, scale and partial width normalisation come from that image's own ink, with the ink threshold set relative to its brightest pixel, and the hole cutoffs are also relative to that peak. The hole search grows until it stops changing. A per-image search over the whole library keeps the 32 best examples of each class. Each local patch picks its own best one-cell shift. Finally, each class's top three finalists are found by sorting.

d.summary: The digit is first deslanted and rescaled to a standard height. It is then described by where edges of each of 8 directions occur, a coarse ink picture, a profile of enclosed holes, and its slant and width-to-height ratio. That description is compared with tens of thousands of stored renderings of hand-drawn digit outlines, and the closest stored examples are kept for each class. For the three most plausible classes, the best candidates are re-scored with a deformable patch match that lets small parts of the image shift slightly, and the class with the lowest combined mismatch wins.
d.references: There are 81 hand-authored stroke drawings of digits, 4 to 9 per class. Each is a list of control points on a 10 x 10 canvas, joined by smooth or straight curves, with an optional pen lift, and each has a style weight. Each class gets 5632 synthetic renderings (56,320 in all), split among that class's drawings in proportion to their weights. Every rendering randomly distorts its drawing: width scaling (narrower for 1), shear, tilt, bending, waist and bulge warps, a 3 x 3 grid of random control-point displacements, per-point jitter, variation in stroke thickness and elliptical pen shape, and tapered stroke ends. It is then inked at 28 x 28 and fitted into a box of about 19.8 px. Every rendering goes through the same normalisation and description as a query. The stored data per rendering is its edge and ink descriptor, its slant and aspect ratio, a 7-band hole profile, and a 16 x 16 map of edge polarity and ink.

stages.name: Slant and extent measurement
stages.computes: Measures how the ink's horizontal position shifts with height and turns that into a slant estimate. It then finds a soft bounding box from ink-mass quantiles in each direction (after deslanting, for the horizontal one), so faint stray marks do not set the size.

key_numbers.meaning: fraction of the measured slant that is undone (dimensionless shear)
largest slant measured before damping, in horizontal px per vertical px
cumulative ink-mass fractions that set the low and high edges of the box

stages.name: Deslant and resample to a standard frame
stages.computes: Resamples the digit into a 32 x 32 frame centred on its box with the slant removed. The height becomes fixed, while the width is only partly normalised (a geometric mean between keeping the original proportions and stretching to a target width). The slant and the width-to-height ratio are kept as two extra measurements.

key_numbers.meaning: height of the digit in the 32 x 32 frame
target width used in the partial width normalisation
floor on the horizontal scale relative to the vertical one, so thin strokes such as a 1 are not stretched into blocks

stages.name: Directional edge and coarse ink descriptor
stages.computes: Smooths the image lightly and measures brightness gradients. It keeps edges in 8 signed directions 45 degrees apart, each counting only within a narrow band around its direction. Each direction map is smoothed, averaged over an 8 x 8 grid of cells and square-rooted. A 16 x 16 coarse ink picture is added, and the edge part and ink part are each scaled to unit length, then weighted.

key_numbers.meaning: an edge must align with a direction to at least this fraction of its strength (about a +/-59 degree acceptance band)
edge maps summarised on an 8 x 8 grid over the 32 px frame
ink picture summarised on a 16 x 16 grid
relative weights of the edge part and the ink part

stages.name: Enclosed-hole profile
stages.computes: At three ink thresholds, marks the background connected to the image border and counts the background pixels it cannot reach (holes). It counts holes per row and sums them into 7 overlapping height bands, then compresses each band's area and averages over the three thresholds.

key_numbers.meaning: ink thresholds as fractions of the image's brightest pixel
centres of the 7 bands, with triangular weighting of half-width 5 px
half-saturation area: band value = area / (6 + area)

stages.name: Local polarity fields
stages.computes: Builds a 16 x 16 map with 5 channels per cell: positive and negative horizontal gradient, positive and negative vertical gradient, and down-weighted ink. Each channel is smoothed and averaged over 2 x 2 px cells. This map is used for the deformable match.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the ink channel relative to the gradient channels

stages.name: Per-class nearest-reference shortlist
stages.computes: For every class, scores each stored rendering by 1 minus the similarity of the descriptors, plus capped penalties for differences in aspect ratio and slant. It keeps the 64 closest, adds a penalty for the difference in hole profile, and keeps the best 12.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of the aspect-ratio and slant penalties, each capped at 3 units; aspect difference is scaled by 0.32 + 0.25 x aspect, slant difference by 0.65
candidates kept per class after the descriptor comparison
weight of the squared hole-profile difference
candidates kept per class after the hole check

stages.name: Pick three rival classes
stages.computes: Scores each class as a blend of its single best match and the mean of its 12 matches, and keeps the three classes with the lowest scores.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of the best match and the mean of the 12
number of rival classes passed to the fine match

stages.name: Deformable patch match
stages.computes: For each of the 12 candidates of each rival class, splits the 16 x 16 polarity map into a 4 x 4 grid of patches. Each patch may shift by up to one cell in each direction, with a cost per shift and a cost for shifts that differ from neighbouring patches. Shifts start at each patch's own best and are refined by alternating checkerboard passes. The total mismatch plus shift costs is divided by the query's own field energy.

key_numbers.value: +/-1 cell (2 px in the 32 px frame)
key_numbers.meaning: largest shift allowed per patch
cost per squared unit of a patch's shift
cost per squared unit of shift difference between neighbouring patches
number of checkerboard refinement half-sweeps

stages.name: Combine and score rivals
stages.computes: Adds the deformable-match energy, with a weight, to each candidate's shortlist distance. Each rival class is scored from its best combined candidate and the mean of its five best.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the deformable-match energy
weights of the best candidate and the mean of the 5 best
number of best candidates averaged

d.decision: Of the three rival classes, the one with the lowest final score wins. That score is 0.74 times the best combined distance (descriptor plus aspect, slant, hole and deformable-match terms) plus 0.26 times the mean of its five best.
d.adapts_per_image:
Several steps depend on the particular image:
- The slant, bounding box, scale and centre are measured on each image and used to deslant and normalise it.
- Hole thresholds are set relative to that image's brightest pixel, and the outside background is found by flood-filling until it stops changing.
- Stored renderings are searched and sorted per image to keep the nearest 64, then 12, per class.
- Only the image's three best classes get the fine match.
- The deformable match chooses each patch's shift by iterative refinement.
- The match energy is divided by the query's own field energy.

d.summary: The method matches the digit against a large bank of synthetically drawn digits. It describes each image by a contrast-normalised coarse ink map, coarse maps of oriented stroke edges, and an orientation-dominance map. For each class it keeps the best-matching drawings, scored separately on the upper part, the lower part and the whole image. On top of that, a small topological check finds the enclosed background regions (holes) by filling the paper inward from the border. It then adds small votes based on hole area, whether holes sit high or low, and whether there are two holes.
d.references: 40,960 rendered reference digits, 4096 per class, drawn procedurally rather than taken from data. Each one is built from pen strokes (cubic curves, straight lines and ovals) laid out in a template per digit. Each digit has several style variants: a 1 with or without a lead-in flick or base serif, a 7 with or without a crossbar, a 4 open or closed, an 8 drawn as two ovals or one looping stroke, a 9 with a separate or continuous loop, and so on. The strokes are randomly warped (aspect ratio, slant, rise, bowing, smooth twists, local bumps), and rendered with a stroke width of about 1.5 to 3.7 px (1s up to about 0.75 px thicker) and varying pressure. Each is scaled to roughly a 20 px box and centred by centre of mass at pixel 14 with up to 0.7 px of random offset. Each reference is stored as the same descriptor that is computed for the input image. The 4096 per class fall into 4 groups of 1024. There is also a small hand-set table of votes per class for the hole features.

stages.name: Coarse ink map
stages.computes: Blurs the image slightly and samples it every other pixel to give a 14x14 ink map. The map is then rescaled to zero mean and unit spread over that image.

key_numbers.meaning: width of the blur in pixels (5x5 window)
resolution of the ink map (every 2nd pixel)

stages.name: Oriented edge maps
stages.computes: Measures stroke edges at 4 orientations (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees), keeping each polarity (rising or falling ink) as a separate map: 8 maps. Each map is averaged over 4x4 pixel cells to give a 7x7 grid, and all 8 maps together are rescaled to zero mean and unit spread for that image.

key_numbers.meaning: directional edge detectors, about 0.9 px across the edge and 1.28 px along it
cell size of the 7x7 edge grid

stages.name: Dominant stroke orientation map
stages.computes: For each 7x7 cell and each orientation, adds the two edge polarities and subtracts 0.82 times the cell's average over all orientations, keeping only the positive excess. This marks which direction the strokes in that cell mainly run. The excess passes through a saturating curve and is then rescaled to zero mean and unit spread for that image.

key_numbers.meaning: fraction of the cell's mean orientation energy subtracted, so only the dominant directions survive
knees of the saturating curve on the orientation excess (gain falls from 3.2 to 1.85, 1.0, then 0.55)

stages.name: Combined descriptor
stages.computes: Joins the three maps into one 784-value description: 196 ink, 392 edge and 196 orientation values. The parts carry relative weights of 0.28, 0.49 and 0.23 of the total.

key_numbers.meaning: share of the match given to ink, edges and orientation

stages.name: Upper, lower and whole template matching
stages.computes: Compares the descriptor with every reference drawing by weighted squared distance. This is done three ways: on the upper part of the image, on the lower part, and on the whole image (the upper and lower parts together, for the same reference). The upper weights fade by grid row: full on the top two rows (image rows 0 to 7), 0.9 on rows 8 to 11, 0.5 on rows 12 to 15, 0.1 on rows 16 to 19, and nothing below. The lower weights are the complement.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of each 4 px band of rows, top to bottom, in the upper match (lower match uses 1 minus these)

stages.name: Best match per class
stages.computes: For each class and each of the three comparisons, takes the best-matching reference in each group of 1024 and averages the 4 group winners. The class score is 0.48 times the sum of the upper and lower scores plus 0.52 times the whole-image score. Upper and lower may pick different references.

key_numbers.meaning: references per class are split into 4 groups, the best of each is kept and the 4 are averaged
weights of the separate upper plus lower matches and of the whole-image match

stages.name: Ink barrier
stages.computes: Blurs the image and marks pixels whose blurred ink is above about 0.32 as walls, with a soft edge between about 0.29 and 0.32.

key_numbers.meaning: blurred ink level (0 to 1) above which a pixel counts as a wall
steepness of the soft cutoff, roughly 0.03 ink levels wide

stages.name: Flood fill from the border
stages.computes: Seeds the frame of border pixels and grows it one pixel per step in all 8 directions for 20 steps, blocked by the ink walls. Paper that is not a wall and was not reached is enclosed background: the holes.

key_numbers.meaning: number of one-pixel growth steps from the border

stages.name: Hole area and position votes
stages.computes: Measures the hole area at the top of the image (rows above about 12), at the bottom (below about 15.5), in a band around row 13.8, and in total. Clipped linear ramps on these give small votes. Total area of 1 to 11 px favours 0, 6, 8 and 9. A top-heavy hole favours 9 and counts against 6, a bottom-heavy hole favours 6 and counts against 9 and 4. A middle area of 8 to 32 px favours 0.

key_numbers.meaning: soft boundaries (spread 1.35 rows) of the top and bottom zones
centre and width of the middle band

key_numbers.value: 1 to 11 px, 2 to 15 px, 8 to 32 px
key_numbers.meaning: area ranges over which the total, top-versus-bottom and middle votes ramp up

stages.name: Hole count
stages.computes: Smooths the hole map over 2x2 pixels and counts the separate enclosed regions with a local counting rule over pixels, neighbouring pairs and 2x2 squares. A count ramping from 1.1 to 1.85 (that is, two holes) adds a vote for 8 (+0.081/0.75 at full) and votes against 0, 6 and 9.

key_numbers.meaning: hole count range over which the two-holes vote ramps from zero to full

d.decision: Each class score is the template-matching score (0.48 times the best upper match plus the best lower match, plus 0.52 times the best whole-image match, each averaged over the 4 groups of references) plus the small hole-area and position votes plus the two-holes vote. The class with the highest total wins.
d.adapts_per_image: The ink, edge and orientation maps are each rescaled by that image's own mean and spread, and the orientation map subtracts each cell's own average orientation energy. For each class it searches all 4096 references and keeps the best per group, separately for the upper, lower and whole match, so the winning references change from image to image. The flood fill follows the paper of that image, but always for a fixed 20 steps. There is no search over position or scale and no early stopping.

clusters.approach: Exhaustive nearest match against synthetic stroke-rendered digits, with no normalization of the input. Descriptors are oriented edge grids, blurred ink and hole maps from a border flood fill. Each class score is built from group-best matches (best in each random subset, then averaged or combined) on the whole image, plus a separate upper/lower part match where the top and bottom may pick different references.

Deslant and partial size normalization, then a coarse descriptor (ink, edge directions, holes, aspect and slant) shortlists the top K synthetic references per class. A deformable patch match re-scores the finalists: local patches shift by about one cell with shift penalties. Each class score is a weighted blend of its best few finalists.

pairs.shared: Synthetic stroke-rendered reference library; descriptors use oriented edges, ink layout and enclosed-hole depth; nearest-match class scoring.
pairs.differs: A does not normalize the input, compares exhaustively, adds concavity, ending and loop-free-ink cues, and matches top and bottom parts. B deslants and resizes, shortlists 16 per class, then reranks with tree-structured deformable patches plus endpoint and junction penalties.

pairs.shared: Nearly the same pipeline: synthetic skeletons, 40,960 refs, 9x9 oriented-edge grid, 13x13 blurred ink, flood-fill hole depth, correlation-based whole match, group-best class score, and a separate top/bottom part match on grid rows 0-5 and 3-8.
pairs.differs: A adds sightline concavity, stroke endings and loop-free-ink cues, and requires the parts to share a width and slant setting. C lets each part shift by one cell and combines the best group with the group mean.

pairs.shared: Synthetic library, edge-direction grids, ink layout, hole information, nearest-neighbour scoring.
pairs.differs: D deslants and rescales, shortlists 32 per class, reranks with an elastic patch-shift match and blends the top 3. It has no part matching and no group-best voting.

pairs.shared: Synthetic stroke drawings, edge-direction and ink descriptors, hole cues, nearest-reference scoring.
pairs.differs: E normalizes slant and size, shortlists per class, keeps 3 rival classes and reranks them with a deformable patch match. A matches exhaustively, adds top/bottom parts and uses many extra cues.

pairs.shared: Exhaustive match against about 40,960 synthetic refs with no input normalization; oriented edge maps plus ink; 4 groups of 1024 with group bests averaged; the score combines whole-image and separate upper/lower matches.
pairs.differs: A folds holes, concavities and endings into the similarity. F uses an orientation-dominance map, adds holes only as small hand-set class votes (plus a two-hole count), and scores by weighted squared distance.

pairs.shared: Synthetic library, direction maps, ink and flood-fill hole depth, nearest-reference scoring.
pairs.differs: B normalizes, shortlists, does a deformable patch match and checks endpoints and junctions. C compares exhaustively, uses group-best voting and a shifted upper/lower part match.

pairs.shared: Deslant and partial rescale; coarse descriptor of directions, ink, aspect and holes; per-class shortlist (16 or 32); finalists reranked by a local patch-shift elastic match; class score is a weighted blend of the best 2 or 3.
pairs.differs: B links patches in a tree with neighbour costs and adds an endpoint and junction penalty. D lets patches shift independently and adds a rigid fine-grid match term. Channel counts differ.

pairs.shared: Deslant and partial resize; descriptor of edge directions, ink, holes, aspect and slant; per-class shortlist; deformable patch match with shift and neighbour-disagreement costs; class score blends the best candidates.
pairs.differs: E shortlists in two stages (64, then 12) and reranks only 3 rival classes, refining shifts with checkerboard passes rather than an exact tree solve. E has no endpoint or junction term.

pairs.shared: Synthetic library; edge-orientation and ink descriptors; hole detection by border fill; nearest-reference scoring.
pairs.differs: F does not normalize, matches exhaustively on the whole, upper and lower regions with group-best averaging, and adds hand-set hole votes. B has a shortlist, deformable rerank and endpoint and junction penalties.

pairs.shared: Synthetic library, edge-direction grids, ink layout, hole cues, and local one-cell shifts in matching.
pairs.differs: D normalizes, shortlists, applies elastic patch shifts to the whole grid and blends the top 3. C compares exhaustively, uses group-best voting, and shifts only the upper and lower parts.

pairs.shared: Synthetic stroke drawings, 8-direction edges, ink, hole cues, small shifts during matching.
pairs.differs: E normalizes, shortlists, keeps rival classes and does a deformable patch rerank. C compares exhaustively and uses group-best voting plus upper/lower part matching.

pairs.shared: Exhaustive match against 40,960 unnormalized synthetic refs; 8 signed edge maps plus ink; whole-image plus separate upper/lower part matching; group-best class scoring.
pairs.differs: C puts flood-fill hole depth into the similarity, lets parts shift and uses correlation. F adds an orientation-dominance map, uses weighted squared distance with fading row weights, and applies holes as hand-set votes.

pairs.shared: Deslant and rescale to a standard height with partial width normalization; signed edge-direction plus ink descriptors; aspect and multi-threshold hole-band profile penalties; per-class shortlist; patch-shift elastic rerank; class score from a weighted top-k blend.
pairs.differs: E keeps 3 rival classes and uses neighbour-coupled shifts refined by checkerboard passes. D shifts patches independently and adds a rigid match term.

pairs.shared: Synthetic library, directed edge grids, ink layout, hole detection, nearest-neighbour scoring.
pairs.differs: D normalizes, shortlists and does an elastic rerank. F matches exhaustively on the whole, upper and lower regions with group-best averaging and adds hand-set hole votes.

pairs.shared: Synthetic library, 8 signed edge maps plus ink, hole detection by border fill, nearest-reference scoring.
pairs.differs: E normalizes, shortlists, keeps rival classes and does a deformable patch rerank. F matches exhaustively with upper/lower/whole group-best scores and hand-set hole votes.

steps.step: Synthetic reference library rendered from hand-authored stroke recipes (curves, lines, ovals) with style variants, random warps, pen thickness and a box of about 20 px
steps.note: All three networks use the same kind of procedural library (about 20 px box, elliptical or pressure-varying pen, crossed 7, flagged 1, open or closed 4 and so on). Networks keep 4096 per class, against 5632 to 16,384 in the programs, and centre by centre of mass instead of normalising each rendering.

steps.step: Estimate slant from second moments and deslant the input
steps.note: No network deslants the test image. N1 partly covers slant by keeping part references rendered at 3 fixed slants (see the aspect and slant step).

steps.step: Recentre and rescale the input to a standard frame with partial width normalisation (centroid or bounding box, height target, damped width scaling)
steps.note: All networks work on the raw 28x28 image and state there is no position or scale search. They rely on references being centred by centre of mass, like MNIST.

steps.step: Aspect ratio and slant kept as extra cues and compared with each reference (penalty or soft-binned feature)
steps.note: N1 replaces measured aspect and slant with a search over 9 fixed rendered width and slant settings (width e^-0.24, 1, e^0.24 by slant -0.2, 0.12, 0.46), and only in part matching. N2 and N3 have no aspect or slant cue.

steps.step: Oriented edge or stroke-direction energy pooled on a coarse spatial grid, normalised per image
steps.note: P3 uses 8 signed directions 45 degrees apart, P2 6 directed, P1 4 unsigned axes. N1 (8 signed plus 4 line detectors, 9x9), N2 (8 signed, 9x9) and N3 (8 signed, 7x7) compute the same kind of map. Networks standardise and correlate, where programs use unit length and cosine. These are equivalent up to centring.

steps.step: Coarse blurred ink layout descriptor, normalised per image
steps.note: Grids: P1 6x6, P2 9x9, P3 16x16. Networks: N1 13x13, N2 13x13, N3 14x14.

steps.step: Enclosed-background (hole) map: lowest ink barrier to the border, or a flood fill of the background from the border
steps.note: N1 and N2 use a grey-level minimum-barrier fill on 14x14, which is the same computation as P1's sweeps, at a different resolution. N3 uses a binary threshold flood fill at one threshold, where P2 and P3 average over three. Networks run a fixed number of passes (16, 21, 20) instead of running until convergence.

steps.step: Vertical profile of hole location (holes summed or pooled into horizontal bands) compared with references
steps.note: N1 has max hole depth in 3 horizontal bands plus a 7x7 hole map, compared with references. N2 has a 6x6 spatial hole-depth map instead of a band profile. N3 does not compare hole layout with references at all. It applies hand-set class votes on top, bottom and middle hole area.

steps.step: Score every reference by coarse descriptor similarity (cosine or correlation)
steps.note: Networks compute a weighted correlation (N1, N2) or a weighted squared distance (N3) against every stored reference.

steps.step: Keep a per-class shortlist of the top k references (16, 32, or 64 then 12) for a second, costlier stage
steps.note: No network has a sorted top-k shortlist or two-stage reranking. Fixed best-per-group maxima take its place (see the class decision step).

steps.step: Select a few rival classes for fine matching
steps.note: No class pruning in any network.

steps.step: Fine-resolution multi-channel map for detailed matching (14x14 six-channel quantised, 16x16 polarity plus ink, or 9x9 fine direction plus silhouette)
steps.note: Networks reuse their single coarse edge grid (9x9 or 7x7) for the part comparison. None has a separate finer detail map.

steps.step: Deformable patch matching: a grid of patches (3x3 or 4x4) each shifting by up to 1 cell to its best offset, with a shift cost
steps.note: N2 is closest. It has only 2 overlapping patches (upper and lower), each shifting by 1 cell (5 placements) with a fixed shift penalty. N1 and N3 have no shifts. They let the top and bottom parts match different references, which buys some tolerance to deformation.

steps.step: Neighbour-coherence penalty on patch shifts, solved exactly on a tree (P1) or by checkerboard refinement (P3)
steps.note: No network couples the parts' displacements.

steps.step: Normalise match cost by ink or field energy
steps.note: Networks use correlation with per-image standardisation instead. Nothing divides the deformable cost by ink.

steps.step: Skeleton thinning of thresholded strokes
steps.note: No thinning in any network.

steps.step: Stroke endpoint and junction density maps compared with the reference
steps.note: N1 finds stroke endings with 16 directional templates on 14x14 and pools them to a 4x4 grid per direction, without a skeleton and without junctions.

steps.step: Combine coarse similarity, fine or deformable cost and auxiliary penalties per candidate reference
steps.note: Programs add the stages per candidate. Networks score the whole digit and the parts against separate reference pools and add them only at class level (N1 0.61/0.39, N2 1/0.85, N3 0.52/0.48). N2 does add the hole term per drawing inside each vote.

steps.step: Class decision from a weighted mix of the class's best few candidates (top 2, top 3, or best plus mean of 5)
steps.note: Programs sort the candidates. Networks take maxima over fixed random reference groups (N1 4x1024 plus overall best, N2 16 groups as best plus 0.4 times mean, N3 4x1024 mean). This plays the same role, rewarding several good matches, but is computed differently.

network_only.step: Sightline concavity tests: ray-cast ink in 8 directions from each 14x14 cell and mark bays open up, down, left or right, between-stroke cells and fully enclosed cells (10 tests, 7x7 grids), correlated with references
Ink outside loop rows: subtract 2.5 times the nearby row hole depth from the ink to isolate stems, tails and bars (6x6 grid)
Thin bright-line detectors at 4 orientations alongside the signed edge detectors, with a soft-knee compression of cell values
Part reference pool conditioned on 9 width and slant settings, with the top and bottom matched independently but forced to share one setting
3x3 morphological closing to seal small stroke gaps before hole finding, averaged with the original ink
Piecewise-linear hole-depth comparison against depth levels 0, 1/3 and 2/3 on a 6x6 max-pooled loop map
References with deliberately trimmed loop ends (open 0, 6, 8) in the library
Dominant-orientation map: per cell, orientation energy minus 0.82 times the cell's mean orientation energy, through a saturating curve
Soft row-weighted upper and lower template matches (weights 1, 1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.1, 0, 0 by 4 px band)
Hand-set per-class votes from hole area, top versus bottom position and middle-band area
Hole count by a local Euler-style counting rule, with a two-hole vote for 8 and against 0, 6 and 9
Splitting each class's references into fixed groups and averaging or combining the per-group maxima

numbers.meaning: Size of the box each synthetic reference digit is fitted into when rendered
numbers.program_values: P1 about 21 px, P2 about 20 px, P3 about 19.8 px
numbers.network_values: N1 about 20 px, N2 19.4 to 20.4 px, N3 about 20 px

numbers.meaning: Number of signed edge directions, 45 degrees apart
numbers.program_values: P3 8 signed directions (P1 4 unsigned axes, P2 6 directed at 60 degrees)
numbers.network_values: N1 8 signed edges, N2 8, N3 8 (4 orientations x 2 polarities)

numbers.meaning: Largest local shift for a deformable part on the 9x9 direction grid
numbers.program_values: P2 1 cell on the 9x9 fine grid (9 positions)
numbers.network_values: N2 1 grid cell = 3 px on the 9x9 grid (5 placements)

numbers.meaning: 9x9 grid for the direction or edge histogram
numbers.program_values: P2 fine 9x9 Gaussian grid on the deslanted, rescaled frame
numbers.network_values: N1 9x9 (4x4 cells, step 3), N2 9x9 (3 px spacing) on the raw image

numbers.meaning: Ink level treated as stroke
numbers.program_values: P1 0.32 for skeleton thinning on the normalised image
numbers.network_values: N3 0.32 blurred-ink wall threshold for flood fill

numbers.meaning: 14x14 half-resolution map with 2x2 px cells
numbers.program_values: P1 14x14 six-channel detail map for patch matching
numbers.network_values: N1 and N2 14x14 low-res image for holes, endings and concavity; N3 14x14 ink map

numbers.meaning: Number of horizontal bands for the hole profile
numbers.network_values: N1 3 bands (top, middle, bottom)

numbers.meaning: Flood-fill or sweep iteration count
numbers.program_values: P1 2 sweep rounds, P2 up to 80 steps, P3 until convergence
numbers.network_values: N1 16, N2 21, N3 20 passes

cover.verdict: The networks share the programs' overall plan: a hand-authored procedural library, directional edge and ink-layout descriptors, a hole map from a border fill, and a best-few-references vote per class. At the level of each computation they differ. The networks never deslant or rescale the input. They have no aspect or slant cue (N1 only searches 9 fixed rendered settings). They replace the sorted top-k shortlist and rerank with maxima over fixed reference groups. They replace the coupled 3x3 or 4x4 deformable patch search with at most two independent upper and lower parts (shifted by one cell only in N2). Left out entirely are thinning, junctions, rival-class pruning, shift-coherence penalties and ink-normalised costs. The networks add their own cues instead: N1's concavity sightlines and loop-free ink, N2's gap closing, N3's dominant-orientation map and hand-set hole-count votes. So they solve the task in a closely related template-matching way, but not the same way.

d.summary: The main tool is a nearest-template comparison. The item's silhouette is described by where it has ink and by which empty pixels can be reached from each of the four image edges without crossing ink. That description is compared with about 15,000 procedurally drawn garment, shoe and bag outlines, and each class's best matches give its silhouette score. Hand-written soft rules add more evidence: shape measurements such as body width at set heights, gaps between legs, open space between sandal straps and the height of a shoe's upper; fabric detail such as a centre zip or placket, a V or round neckline, a hem rib and plaid; and an arched bag handle. A two-level decision follows: silhouette evidence settles which broad group wins (tops or footwear against the other classes), and all the evidence settles the class within the group.
d.references:
There are 15,360 drawn silhouettes, 1,536 per class. They are generated procedurally from parametric outline models with randomly drawn proportions:
- **Tops** (T-shirt, pullover, dress, coat, shirt): one body outline whose width changes with height (neck, shoulder, armpit, waist, hem) plus polygon sleeves. Sleeves can be short, tank, mid or long, and collars, rounded hems and neck dips vary.
- **Trousers**: two legs below a crotch height, with a waist, hips, leg spread and calf width.
- **Bags**: a body that can be rectangular or tapered, with an optional arched handle above it.
- **Sandals, sneakers and ankle boots**: drawn side-on from a sole and heel profile. Sneakers have a toe, tongue and heel counter. Boots have an ankle shaft. Sandals have one to three straps and an optional ankle strap, and some have a tall heel or a wedge.

Each drawing gets random scale (about 0.94 to 1.04), aspect ratio, small offsets and a slight shear. It is rendered at 56x56, reduced to 28x28, lightly blurred and then summarised exactly as the input is (see stage 3).

There is also a fixed bank of 160 bag-handle shapes: an arched crown, two side legs, an empty hole under the arch and a body below. They vary in width, top position, arch depth and horizontal offset.

stages.name: Soft foreground mask
stages.computes: The image is lightly blurred (centre-weighted 3x3) and each pixel's blurred brightness goes through a piecewise-linear ramp. The result is a 0 to 1 'is this the item' value: 0 below a faint level, steep at first, and fully 1 from a modest grey up.

key_numbers.meaning: blurred brightness (0 to 1 scale) where a pixel starts to count as item
brightness where the steep part of the ramp ends; by then the pixel counts as about 0.68 item
brightness from which a pixel counts fully as item

stages.name: Coarse occupancy grid
stages.computes: The mask is reduced to a 14x14 grid of 2x2 cells. Each cell's value is mostly its mean (0.84 weight) with a little of its maximum (0.16), so thin strokes still show. A small noise floor is then subtracted.

key_numbers.meaning: grid resolution, each cell 2x2 original pixels
occupancy below this counts as empty (removes specks)

stages.name: Emptiness and edge-reachability maps
stages.computes: Five maps are made for each grid cell. One is how empty the cell is. The other four say whether the cell can be reached from the left, right, top or bottom edge of the image without crossing ink, measured as 1 minus 1.5 times the ink accumulated along the row or column from that edge up to the cell, floored at 0. Together they describe the outline, the background regions open to each side and enclosed gaps such as between legs or under a handle.

key_numbers.meaning: how fast accumulated ink from an edge blocks reachability (about 0.67 of a fully inked cell blocks it)

stages.name: Template comparison
stages.computes: The five maps are compared with each of the 15,360 stored silhouettes by weighted squared difference. Emptiness carries the most weight, then the from-top, from-bottom, from-left and from-right maps. Each class's templates sit in 4 fixed groups of 384. The best (closest) match in each group is found, and the class's silhouette score is 0.55 times the best of the 4 group bests plus 0.45 times their average.

key_numbers.meaning: relative weight of the emptiness, from-left, from-right, from-top and from-bottom maps in the distance
templates per class and the grouping used for best plus consensus
mix of overall best match and average of group bests

stages.name: Shape measurements at full resolution
stages.computes: The mask is thresholded at a firmer level (above 0.15). At 28x28 it gives: horizontal enclosure (pixels that have ink both to their left and their right on the row), vertical enclosure, empty pixels enclosed horizontally (gaps inside the item on a row), empty pixels enclosed vertically, ink and open-from-top. These are averaged over fixed bands and windows. The results are body width at rim, shoulder, chest, waist, hip and hem heights; leg-split and slit gaps in the lower centre; open space between straps (toe and arch zones); front and rear column height; top-profile depth at instep, throat, back and toe positions; neck and shoulder top depth; spans at arm and upper-chest height; and gaps beside the hem below the cuffs.

key_numbers.meaning: mask level above which a pixel is firm ink for these measurements
how fast accumulated ink from an edge blocks open-from-edge status
shoulder, chest, waist, hip and hem bands, as fractions of image height from the top
leg-split window, in image-width fractions from the centre and height fractions

stages.name: Leg-gap and waistband probes
stages.computes: On a near-black map (pixels darker than about 0.02), 27 narrow, slightly slanted vertical lines through the lower centre are tested for darkness along their length. Each must have ink along a parallel line at one of 5 spacings on both sides. The best line scores as a gap from crotch to cuff between two legs. Separately, 27 bands across the top (various widths, offsets and tilts) are tested for being fully covered by fabric (waistband).

key_numbers.meaning: brightness below which a pixel counts as black
where the gap lines run (width fraction from the centre, height fraction)
spacings between the gap line and the flanking leg lines, as fractions of image width
top band tested for full waistband coverage

stages.name: Construction rules
stages.computes: The measurements go through soft ramps (0 below a low value, 1 above a high value) and are combined with soft AND (minimum) and OR (maximum). The result is cues such as two legs with a gap reaching the bottom, a flat belted top, a tapered leg shape, a skirt flare, an hourglass waist, an armless long bodice, a neck rising above the shoulders, cuffs above the hem, sleeves extended beyond the shoulders, a T-shaped step at chest versus arm height, open strap space, a low heel counter, an ankle notch, a rear shaft taller than the front and a rising shaft. Each class gets a fixed weighted sum of these cues.

key_numbers.meaning: ramp on the leg-split gap fraction used for the trouser fly-gap cue
ramp on upper-chest span minus arm-level span (the T-shirt step from short sleeves)
ramp on enclosed vertical gap area (open space between sandal straps)
ramp on rear height minus 0.8 times front height (boot shaft)

stages.name: Fabric and tailoring detail

key_numbers.meaning: standardised brightness range kept
centre strip compared with side strips for zip or placket (width fractions from the centre)
stripe periods tested for plaid
ramp on plaid strength; at full strength it adds 1.65 to shirt

stages.name: Bag-handle detector
stages.computes: The soft mask is compared with 160 handle shapes: an arched crown with two legs and a body below scores as a reward, and ink in the hole under the arch scores against. The best response above an offset adds strongly to bag.

key_numbers.meaning: offset a handle response must exceed to count
multiplier from handle strength to bag score

stages.name: Evidence fusion and group-level decision
stages.computes: Full score is silhouette plus construction, fabric and handle evidence. For the tops group (T-shirt, pullover, coat, shirt) and the footwear group (sandal, sneaker, boot), each class's score is shifted so the group's best equals the best of a coarse score. The coarse score is silhouette only for footwear, and silhouette plus 0.38 times construction for tops. Fabric and handle evidence therefore only rank classes within a group, while trouser, dress and bag keep their full scores.

key_numbers.meaning: share of construction evidence in the coarse score for tops

d.decision: The highest final score wins. Within tops and within footwear, classes are ranked by their full combined evidence. Each group's best score is replaced by the group's best coarse silhouette score, and that is what competes with trouser, dress and bag (which keep their full scores) and with the other group. In effect it is a two-level choice: first the kind of object, decided mostly by silhouette, then the specific class.
d.adapts_per_image:
- **Template search:** for each class, the method searches all 1,536 stored silhouettes and keeps the best match in each group of 384, so the template that counts differs from image to image.
- **Best-of probes:** the leg-gap lines, flanking-leg spacings, waistband bands, placket, V and round neckline templates, flank stripes, stripe gratings and bag handles each keep only their strongest response.
- **Normalisation:** brightness is standardised by the image's own mean and spread before fabric analysis.
- **Group re-anchoring:** the tops and footwear groups are shifted by their best scores, which depend on the image.
- **Soft logic:** the rules use soft minima and maxima rather than branching.
- **Not adaptive:** there is no iteration and no search over scale or position beyond the fixed probe variants. Templates are compared in the image's fixed frame.

d.summary: The item is cropped to its own bounding box and stretched to fill a fixed square. Its silhouette, summarised as a coarse occupancy grid, four edge-to-outline depth profiles and its width-to-height ratio, is compared with tens of thousands of synthetic silhouettes procedurally drawn for each class, giving a nearest-neighbour shape distance per class. On top of that, many hand-set geometric tests (row widths, neckline, leg gap, holes, toe-to-shaft rise, bag handle) and interior texture tests (centre-front seams, zips, buttons, prints, logos, collars) add or subtract evidence class by class. The highest combined score wins.
d.references: 32,000 synthetic silhouettes, 3,200 per class. Each one comes from a hand-written parametric outline model with randomised proportions.
