Six crops are tried and the best one is kept per letter. For each letter, the 6 nearest references are picked by sorting.

d.summary: The image is turned into three coarse 11 x 11 maps: where edges of each of four orientations are, where thin bright or dark line-like bars of each orientation are, and a lighting-corrected brightness (silhouette) map. These maps are compared against those of 18,432 synthetic hand drawings: 768 randomised poses for each of the 24 letters, made with a hand-shape model of palm, wrist and finger tubes. Each class is scored by its best-matching drawings, allowing small shifts, and a second comparison run on locally contrast-equalised regions is added to that score.
d.references: 24 x 768 = 18,432 rendered hand templates, 768 per letter. Each is a shaded drawing of a hand made of simple parts: an elliptical palm, a widening forearm or wrist band (sometimes with a dark sleeve), and fingers and thumb drawn as tapered tubes along hand-set joint paths. The poses are hand-written per letter: which fingers are extended, folded or curled, their angles and spread, the thumb's position, sideways hands for G/H/T, downward-pointing hands for P/Q, and the O/C/F curl. Twenty pose and appearance parameters are drawn from a quasi-random low-discrepancy sequence: finger length and thickness, bend, spread, thumb reach, sideways yaw (shear), in-plane rotation of about +/-15.5 degrees plus a per-letter tilt, horizontal squash, zoom, off-centre shift, light direction, background grey level, contrast and sleeve presence. Each drawing is made at 34 x 34, shrunk to 28 x 28, and turned into the same edge, bar and brightness maps as the input. Edge maps blend the shaded image (0.74) and the silhouette outline (0.26). There is a second template set with the same poses: the edge and bar maps contrast-normalised within each of 9 regions and weighted towards places where the drawing has structure.

stages.name: Exposure normalisation
stages.computes: The whole image is shifted and scaled to zero mean brightness and unit brightness spread, which removes overall brightness and contrast differences.

stages.name: Oriented edge strength
stages.computes: Edge strength, ignoring its polarity, is measured at every position for four orientations (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees) using small smoothed derivative detectors. Each orientation is then suppressed by 0.61 times the response at the perpendicular orientation, keeping only the positive remainder, so clean single-direction edges stand out over texture.

key_numbers.meaning: detector footprint in pixels, giving a 24 x 24 response map
detector width across and along the edge, in pixels
fraction of the perpendicular-orientation response subtracted

stages.name: Edge saturation and coarse histogram
stages.computes: Edge strength above a knee is compressed to 12% slope, so very strong edges do not dominate. Strengths are then averaged over 4 x 4 pixel windows every 2 pixels, giving an 11 x 11 grid per orientation. The four maps together are standardised to zero mean and unit spread for that image.

key_numbers.meaning: edge-strength knee in standardised-brightness units
coarse cell size and spacing (11 x 11 cells)

stages.name: Oriented bar (ridge) strength
stages.computes: Same as the edge stages, but the detectors respond to thin bright or dark bars (finger-like strokes and creases) at the four orientations. Perpendicular suppression is 0.61, a knee at 0.68 cuts the slope to 10%, they are pooled to 11 x 11 and standardised for that image.

key_numbers.meaning: bar half-width across and length scale along, in pixels
bar-strength knee

stages.name: Lighting-corrected silhouette map
stages.computes: For each of the 11 x 11 cells, the (negated) mean brightness of a 4 x 4 pixel block is taken. A left-to-right background lighting trend is removed, estimated from the brightness difference between the top-right and top-left corners. The map is then standardised for that image. In effect it is a coarse light/dark layout of hand against background.

key_numbers.meaning: top-left and top-right corner patches used to estimate the background lighting gradient
strength of the gradient correction across the grid width
silhouette cell size and spacing

stages.name: Global template comparison
stages.computes: The nine stacked maps (4 edge, 4 bar, 1 silhouette) are compared with every template's maps by a weighted similarity: edges 0.48, bars 0.28, silhouette 0.48, all templates unit-length. Templates are tried at 3 x 3 offsets of one cell, and the best offset is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: positional slack searched in each direction
relative weight of edge, bar and silhouette evidence

stages.name: Per-class pose consensus
stages.computes: For each letter, the 768 pose templates are split into 4 groups of 192, each spread over pose space. The best match in each group is taken and the four bests are averaged, which rewards a letter several of whose independent pose samples fit.

key_numbers.meaning: poses per group, maximum taken within each
groups averaged per letter

stages.name: Regional contrast equalisation
stages.computes: The edge and bar grids are cut into 3 x 3 regions of about 4 x 4 cells (about 8 pixels square). Each region is shifted to zero mean and divided by its own spread, with a floor that stops near-empty regions being blown up. This puts faint and strong parts of the hand on equal footing.

key_numbers.meaning: region size, starting at cells 0, 4 and 8
spread floor in the regional normalisation

stages.name: Local-detail template comparison
stages.computes: The equalised edge (0.64) and bar (0.36) maps are compared with the second, regionally normalised template set. As before, the best of 3 x 3 one-cell offsets is kept, along with the max per group of 192 poses, and the 4 groups are averaged per letter.

key_numbers.meaning: edge vs bar weight in the detail templates
template emphasis on places where the drawing has structure

d.decision: Each letter's score is its global consensus score plus 0.6 times its local-detail consensus score. The letter with the highest total wins.
d.adapts_per_image: Several steps depend on the image. Brightness is standardised using that image's own mean and spread. The edge, bar and silhouette maps are each standardised by statistics measured on that image. The background left-right lighting trend is estimated from that image's top corners. Each of 9 regions is contrast-normalised by its own spread. Each template is searched over 3 x 3 positional offsets (+/-2 px) and the best kept, and within each group of 192 poses only the best-matching pose counts. There is no iteration or branching beyond these maximum selections.

d.summary: The method compares each photo with a large library of synthetic 3D hand renderings and picks the class of the best match. It first estimates where the hand is by modelling the background from the top corners and upper sides and by tracing in from the top, left and right borders until an edge is crossed. It then compares a coarse silhouette and edge-direction layout over 27 shifted and rescaled framings against every rendering, keeps the 6 best renderings per letter, and rescores those on a finer grid. The rescoring uses region-by-region matching with small local shifts, a whole-image comparison and agreement on enclosed holes.
d.references: About 24,576 synthetic hand renderings: 1,024 per letter for all 24 letters. Each is a hand built from tapered tubes (three segments per finger, three for the thumb) and ellipsoids for the palm, with a forearm entering from below. Per-letter rules set the finger bend angles (extended, curled, clawed, hooked, curved, ring), the finger spread, the thumb placement (e.g. along the side, under the fingers, circling the index or middle fingertip, spread out, pinching, upright between the fingers) and the ranges of yaw, pitch and roll (e.g. sideways for G and H, pointing down for Q and P). Lengths, thicknesses, angles, palm width and height, framing and offset are randomised. Each one is shaded at 48x48 with a random directional light, ambient level, contact shadows and cast shadows, then softened and resampled to 28x28 together with its exact hand silhouette. For each rendering two descriptions are stored: a coarse 8x8 one (silhouette layout plus four edge-direction layouts) and a fine 14x14 one with 7 layers (silhouette, local brightness detail, four edge-direction strengths, enclosed holes).

stages.name: Background surface estimate
stages.computes: Takes the median brightness and its spread in the two top corners and in two patches on the upper left and right sides. From these it fits a tilted background plane: a level, a left-to-right slope taken from the corner difference (trusted less when the corners are textured), and a top-to-bottom slope taken from the side patches versus the corners.

key_numbers.meaning: size of the top-left and top-right corner patches used as background samples
upper side patches used to estimate the vertical background slope
cap on the estimated brightness slope across the frame (brightness units, 0 to 1 scale)

stages.name: Border-inward background tracing
stages.computes: For each column traced down from the top, and each row traced in from the left and the right, it extrapolates a straight-line brightness trend from the first few pixels. It then measures how far each pixel departs from that trend, plus the strongest edge crossed so far and the largest departure seen so far. A pixel's background distance is the smallest over the three directions, and this caps the distance from the background plane, so anything reachable from a border without crossing an edge counts as background.

key_numbers.meaning: border run used to set each trace's baseline brightness and trend
maximum allowed brightness trend along a trace
weight of the strongest edge crossed so far, which reduces trust in the background beyond an edge

stages.name: Hand occupancy map
stages.computes: It combines the normalised departure from the background with the normalised local edge texture, both scaled by the image's own average departure, and takes the larger of the two as a soft hand-presence map. The map is then softened and damped wherever there is no fine local detail, so that smooth lighting ramps are not mistaken for hand.

key_numbers.meaning: brightness departure that counts as fully hand-like, set from the image's mean residual
minimum fraction kept in areas with no fine detail (smooth regions are damped to 55%)

stages.name: Multiple framings
stages.computes: Builds 27 resampled versions of both the photo and the occupancy map: three zoom levels, each with a 3x3 grid of shifts. Pixels that fall outside the frame are clamped to the edge.

key_numbers.meaning: sampling-step factors: 0.82 zooms in on the centre, 1.21 zooms out
horizontal and vertical shift steps (-d, 0, +d) at each zoom

stages.name: Coarse shape and edge description
stages.computes: For each framing it averages the occupancy map into an 8x8 grid of 4 px cells. It also builds four 8x8 maps of edges whose direction lies near horizontal, vertical or one of the two diagonals, with edge strength normalised by the image's mean gradient and compressed so it saturates. Each part has its mean removed, the lower rows are down-weighted (forearm and clothing vary), and each is scaled to unit length.

key_numbers.meaning: coarse layout grid
direction-agreement cutoff: an edge counts toward an orientation only if it lies within about 45 degrees of it
weights on the bottom three rows (corners lowest), so the wrist and sleeve area counts less
relative weight of silhouette layout versus edge-direction layout

stages.name: Library search and shortlist
stages.computes: It compares each framing's coarse description with every stored rendering by normalised correlation and keeps each rendering's best score over the 27 framings, together with the framing that gave it. For each letter it then keeps the 6 highest-scoring renderings.

key_numbers.meaning: renderings kept per letter for detailed verification
renderings per letter searched

stages.name: Fine description
stages.computes: For each shortlisted rendering's chosen framing it builds a 14x14 grid of 2 px cells with layers for: occupancy, local brightness relative to a heavily smoothed version (normalised by mean gradient), edge strength in each of the four directions, and enclosed holes. Holes are background regions that cannot be reached by flooding in from the frame border, such as the circle of O or F.

key_numbers.meaning: fine comparison grid
how far the flood from the border spreads (pixels) when finding enclosed holes
fraction of total edge strength an orientation must exceed to count

stages.name: Region-wise matching with local shifts
stages.computes: It splits the fine grid into 9 overlapping 6x6-cell regions (3x3 layout, about 12 px each) covering palm and finger areas. It correlates each region of the photo with the rendering after normalising each region separately, lets each region shift by one cell (2 px) in any of the four directions with a small penalty, and keeps the best fit. Regions are then averaged, weighted by how much structure they contain and by position.

key_numbers.meaning: overlapping regions, each about 12x12 px
maximum independent shift per region
score penalty per cell of shift
weight of the bottom row of regions (wrist area) versus about 1.05 to 1.25 for the others

stages.name: Whole-grid comparison and hole agreement
stages.computes: It computes a single normalised correlation over the whole fine grid across the six non-hole layers, with occupancy weighted most heavily. Separately, it scores the overlap between the photo's enclosed holes and the rendering's, minus a small penalty when the rendering has a hole.

key_numbers.meaning: layer weights: occupancy, brightness detail, each edge direction
penalty for a rendering that has an enclosed hole, so hole letters must earn it

d.decision: Each shortlisted rendering gets a combined score: 0.3 x coarse match + 0.4 x region-wise match + 0.3 x whole-grid match + 0.085 x hole agreement. Each letter's score is 0.8 x its best rendering's score plus 0.2 x the average over its 6 renderings, and the letter with the highest score wins.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes, in several ways. The background plane and the border traces are fitted to each image's own corners and borders. Hand-likeness and edge strengths are normalised by that image's average contrast and gradient. The match searches 27 framings (3 zooms by 9 shifts) and keeps the best per rendering. The shortlist (top 6 per letter) depends on the image. Each fine region searches 5 small shifts and keeps the best. Region confidences depend on how much structure the image and rendering show there.

d.summary: The method compares the photo with a large library of synthetic hand drawings, made in advance for every letter, and gives each letter the score of its best-matching drawings. Before matching it turns the photo into several descriptions: oriented edges, a background-versus-hand map (from how much each spot differs from a background brightness estimated at the border, plus how enclosed each spot is by strong edges), thin-finger and finger-gap maps, outline profiles seen from the left, right and top, and fine local detail in the palm and finger zones. Each drawing is tried at 9 small offsets and the best offset is kept. A letter's score combines its single best drawing with how well its drawings match on average across 16 groups.
d.references: 27,648 stored references in each of several description families: 24 letters x 128 poses x 9 positional offsets (shifts of -2.7, 0 or +2.7 pixels in x and y). Each pose is a procedurally built, shaded hand rendered at double resolution on a 40x40 canvas with a flat background of brightness 0.81, then cropped to 28x28. The hand is a palm ellipse, a wrist tube entering from below or the side, and fingers and thumb drawn as tapered tubes through hand-placed joint points, posed per letter (curled, extended, folded thumb, sideways for G/H/T, pointing down for P/Q, C/O curves). Random variation per pose covers finger length (0.89 to 1.13), thickness (0.9 to 1.12), splay (0.72 to 1.45), curl bend, lean, horizontal squash (0.79 to 1.26), tilt (about 0.15 rad spread plus a letter offset), zoom (0.82 to 1.23) and lighting direction. Variants such as mirrored R crossings, an outward or inward Q wrist, and shifted fingers depend on the pose index. For each rendered pose and offset the method stores: an 8-direction edge picture (image edges, edges inside the hand, silhouette outline), a coarse hand-versus-background picture, a thin-parts picture, a gap picture, three outline profiles (from left, right, top), and band-passed detail pictures for a palm window and a finger window.

stages.name: Brightness standardisation
stages.computes: Subtracts the photo's mean brightness and divides by its spread, so the matching ignores overall brightness and contrast. The border is then extended by repeating the edge pixels.

key_numbers.meaning: pixels of border extension on each side (28 to 32) so edge detection covers the frame rim

stages.name: Oriented edge measurement
stages.computes: Measures smoothed brightness change in 4 orientations (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees), keeping each polarity separately (8 edge types). Each is averaged over 2x2 pixel cells, giving a 14x14 grid. Strong edges are compressed, then each edge type is restandardised over the image.

key_numbers.meaning: smoothing width of the edge detector, in pixels
edge strength (standardised units, per cell) above which the excess is reduced
fraction of the excess removed above that level, so strong edges count only 19% past it

stages.name: Background-difference map
stages.computes: On a 14x14 version of the photo, predicts background brightness at each cell by blending the left and right border columns at that row, weighted by horizontal position, with the top-left and top-right corner patches. The map scores how much each cell departs from that prediction, darker departures counting more than lighter ones and large departures saturating. It is high where the cell looks like background and is restandardised.

key_numbers.meaning: vertical reach (in 2-pixel cells) of the border-column background estimate
relative weight of being lighter than the predicted background, against 1.0 for darker
departure (standardised units) beyond which further difference counts much less

stages.name: Enclosure by edges
stages.computes: For each cell and each of 5 escape directions (left, right, up, up-left, up-right; not down, where the wrist enters), finds the strongest local brightness step crossed on the straight path to the frame border. Steps come from a lightly smoothed photo. The easiest escape route is kept: cells that can reach the border without crossing a strong edge read as background, enclosed cells as hand. The result is restandardised and added to the background-difference map. The left, right and top maps are also kept separately as outline profiles.

key_numbers.meaning: smoothing width in pixels before measuring steps
escape directions tried (all except downward)
longest jump in cells when tracking the strongest edge along a ray (1, 2, 4, 8 combined, covering the 14-cell frame)

stages.name: Hand and background spreading
stages.computes: Spreads the combined hand-likeness and background-likeness maps by one cell, each cell taking the strongest value among its 8 neighbours minus a distance penalty. The result is a hand-grown map and a background-grown map, each restandardised.

key_numbers.meaning: penalty per cell of distance (1.2 for diagonals) when spreading to neighbours

stages.name: Local detail map
stages.computes: Subtracts a blurred version from the 14x14 photo to keep only fine local structure such as knuckles and finger separations, then restandardises it.

key_numbers.meaning: blur width in 2-pixel cells removed as the coarse component

stages.name: Whole-hand comparison with every drawing
stages.computes: For every letter, pose and offset, correlates the photo's descriptions with the drawing's matching ones: edges, hand-versus-background picture, thin finger parts against the hand-grown map, gaps beside fingers against the background-grown map, and the three outline profiles. The scores are added with fixed relative weights. Lower rows (wrist area) and far sides count less. The best of the 9 offsets is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of the hand-versus-background match relative to the edge match (1.0)
weight of the thin-part and the gap matches each
weight of each of the three outline-profile matches
row index (of 14 cells) below which the shape, gap and profile references fade, by up to 62 to 68%

stages.name: Palm and finger detail comparison
stages.computes: Correlates the local detail map with each drawing's band-passed detail inside a palm window (mid-frame) and a finger window (top of frame). For sideways or downward letters (G, H, P, Q, T) the windows lie along the pointing axis instead. Each window keeps its own best of the 9 offsets, and both are added to the whole-hand score for that pose.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of each detail match
offset positions tried (3x3 grid at -2.7, 0, +2.7 pixels)

stages.name: Per-letter pooling over poses
stages.computes: For each letter, takes the best total over its 128 poses. The 128 poses also form 16 consecutive groups of 8; the method takes each group's best and averages those 16 values. The letter score is best pose plus that average.

key_numbers.meaning: drawn poses per letter
poses per group for the averaged support term (16 groups)

d.decision: The letter with the highest score wins. A letter's score is its single best-matching drawing plus the average, over 16 groups of 8 drawings, of each group's best match. Each drawing's match is the sum of its whole-hand agreement at its best offset and its palm and finger detail agreement, each at its own best offset.
d.adapts_per_image: The photo is standardised by its own brightness mean and spread, and each intermediate map is restandardised the same way. The background brightness is estimated from that photo's own border columns and top corners. For each cell the method searches the escape directions and keeps the easiest path to the border, and it tracks the strongest edge along each ray. Every drawing is tried at 9 offsets and the best is kept, with separate best offsets for the whole hand, palm detail and finger detail. Finally it keeps the best of 128 poses per letter and the best within each group of 8.

d.summary: The method compares each photo against a large stored library of synthetic hand images. Every letter's library entry is drawn from a hand-built 3D hand model posed for that letter. Each photo is turned into a contrast-normalised description: where edges are and which way they point, light and dark relief, thin finger-like ridges, and how far the background can be reached from the border without crossing an edge. For each letter, the 20 most similar library images are then re-checked. The check asks whether the photo has edge or relief features at those images' stored landmark spots (upper and lower halves of the frame may each shift by a pixel or two) and whether their stored empty-background spots are free of structure. The letter whose best few re-checked matches score highest wins.
d.references: About 79,900 synthetic rendered hand images in all: 24 letters x 52 batches x 64 = 3,328 per letter. Each comes from a procedural 3D hand model. The palm is 4 ellipsoids and the forearm 3 ellipsoids along a wrist direction. The four fingers and the thumb are each 3 tapered capsule segments. Per-letter joint bend angles, finger spread, thumb placement mode (side, folded, under 2 or 3 fingers, out, pinching, touching a fingertip and so on) and overall yaw, pitch and roll of the hand are set by hand for each letter. Random jitter is added to angles, finger length, palm breadth, thickness, wrist direction, arm length, framing, centre and size. Some letters get special-case wrist directions, and Q has an alternative downward pose 60% of the time. Each hand is drawn with depth ordering at 56 x 56 and shaded by a random directional light with ambient falloff and simple cast shadows. Skin is slightly darker near finger joints. The hand is set on a flat background of random brightness (mostly light, sometimes dark) with a gentle random gradient, then shrunk to 28 x 28. Three things are stored for every rendered image. (1) The same global description computed for test photos. (2) 64 landmark spots: the 32 strongest edge or relief points in the top half of the frame and the 32 strongest in the bottom half, each tagged with which edge direction or relief type was strongest there. (3) 24 empty-background spots that lie off the hand but close to it.

stages.name: Edge direction and strength
stages.computes: Brightness change is measured at each pixel on a lightly smoothed copy of the image. Strength is divided by the image's own root-mean-square edge strength, capped and compressed. Pixels near the left and right borders and toward the bottom (where the wrist enters) count for less.

key_numbers.meaning: cap on edge strength, in multiples of the image's RMS edge strength
power used to compress edge strength
how much the side columns and the bottom rows are down-weighted

stages.name: Edge-direction maps on grids
stages.computes: Edges are split into 4 unsigned directions (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees), and each pixel counts only for directions within about 55 degrees of its edge. Each direction map is summarised with soft-edged spatial cells on a fine 10x10 grid and a coarse 6x6 grid. A 9x9 grid version also keeps edge polarity, i.e. which side is brighter.

key_numbers.meaning: alignment cutoff (cosine): the edge must be within about 55 degrees of the direction
grid cells per side for the fine, coarse and polarity-kept summaries of a 28-pixel image

stages.name: Thin ridge (finger) detector
stages.computes: Along 4 directions, measures both the step and the ridge or valley response between pixels 1 apart, scaled by the image's edge level. The response is averaged along the perpendicular, the likely long axis of a finger, and summarised on a 7x7 grid.

key_numbers.meaning: weights on step-like versus ridge-like response
grid cells per side for the ridge summary

stages.name: Light and dark relief
stages.computes: Subtracts a heavily smoothed background estimate (about 9 rounds of smoothing) from a lightly smoothed image. Brighter-than-surroundings and darker-than-surroundings parts are kept separately, scaled by edge level, and summarised on 9x9 grids. Total edge strength is also kept on an 8x8 grid.

key_numbers.meaning: extra smoothing rounds used for the background brightness estimate
cap on relief, in units of the image's edge level

stages.name: Background reachable from the border
stages.computes: Spreads in from the top, left and right edges (not the bottom) and records, for each pixel, the strongest edge that must be crossed to reach it. Low values mean open background, high values mean enclosed by the hand outline. The result is blended with edge strength and summarised on an 8x8 grid.

key_numbers.meaning: edge strength (times image RMS) at which an edge fully blocks the spread
spreading steps, so the reach is about 16 pixels inward

stages.name: Assemble and compare description
stages.computes: Each block is centred (85% of its mean removed), normalised to unit length, weighted and concatenated. The photo's similarity to every stored image of each letter is computed as an inner product, and the 20 most similar stored images per letter are kept.

key_numbers.meaning: weights of fine-direction, coarse-direction, polarity, edge-strength, border-reach, relief and ridge blocks
candidate stored images kept per letter

stages.name: Local feature maps for landmark checking
stages.computes: Six per-pixel maps are built: 4 edge-direction maps (stricter alignment) and bright and dark relief against a wide background estimate. Each is scaled by image edge level and capped. Each pixel's value is mixed with the maximum over its 4 neighbours and squashed to 0 to 1. A combined busyness map (strongest edge plus relief) is also squashed.

key_numbers.meaning: direction alignment cutoff for the landmark maps
half-saturation level of the squashed landmark maps
half-saturation level of the busyness map used for background checks

stages.name: Landmark and empty-space verification
stages.computes: For each candidate, the photo's feature strength is averaged at the candidate's 32 upper and 32 lower landmarks, each in its stored feature type. This is tried at 9 small offsets, and the upper and lower halves may each use either the offset or the unshifted position. A penalty is subtracted for busyness at the candidate's 24 empty-background spots, with each spot's contribution capped so partial occlusion is tolerated. The best offset is kept.

key_numbers.meaning: no shift, 2 pixels up, down, left or right, and 1 pixel diagonally
preference for the unshifted half, and cost of any shift
weight of the background-busyness penalty
cap on each background spot's penalty

stages.name: Per-letter score
stages.computes: Each candidate's merit is its description similarity plus 0.7 times its verification score. The letter's score mixes the best and the average of its top 4 candidate merits.

key_numbers.meaning: weight of landmark verification relative to description similarity
top candidates averaged per letter
mix of best and mean among the top 4

d.decision: The letter with the highest score wins. Its score is 0.45 times its best candidate merit plus 0.55 times the mean of its 4 best merits. A merit is description similarity plus 0.7 times the landmark and empty-space check.
d.adapts_per_image: Yes. Edge and relief strengths are divided by the image's own RMS edge strength. The border-reach background estimate is propagated step by step and follows the image's own outlines. For each letter the method searches all stored images and keeps the 20 most similar. For each candidate it searches 9 small offsets, choosing independently whether the upper and lower halves shift, and keeps the best. It then keeps the top 4 candidates per letter.

clusters.approach: Direct dense template correlation: standardised image to coarse oriented-edge and related evidence grids, correlated with every synthetic rendered hand at a 3x3 small-shift search, scores pooled per letter by group-wise best-pose maxima (sum or average), with no hand segmentation or reframing step

Hand-localising nearest-neighbour retrieval: estimate hand versus background by reachability from top/left/right borders without crossing edges, describe the image (silhouette or border-reach plus edge directions), retrieve the top-k most similar synthetic renders per letter (with reframing or shortlist re-verification), and score the letter by a best plus mean-of-top-k mix

pairs.differs: B segments the hand by border reachability, builds six crops, adds silhouette and Fourier outline signature, scores 0.6 best + 0.4 top-6 mean; A has no segmentation, uses 3x3 shift with independent upper/lower halves and sums batch maxima

pairs.differs: D estimates background plane and border-traced occupancy, searches 27 framings, shortlists top 6 per letter and reranks with regional shifts, whole-grid and hole agreement; A is a single-stage dense correlation with half-split shifts and batch-max sum

pairs.differs: B segments the hand via border reachability, crops six framings, uses outline Fourier signature and top-6 best/mean kNN; C uses lighting-corrected brightness instead of segmentation, 3x3 shifts, group-max consensus and a regional-normalised second pass

pairs.differs: F has no crop/bounding box, uses a top-20 shortlist with landmark and empty-background verification; B scores six crops directly with an outline signature

pairs.differs: F adds border reachability, retrieves top 20 per letter and verifies landmarks and empty spots with best/mean of top 4; C uses 3x3 shift dense correlation and group-max consensus plus regional pass

pairs.shared: Background prediction from border/corner samples plus edge-enclosure from borders, silhouette and edge-direction layouts, fine local detail, small shifts, rendered hand library
pairs.differs: D searches 27 framings, shortlists 6 per letter and reranks with region-wise shifts and hole agreement; E is single-stage dense correlation at 9 offsets with thin/gap/profile terms and group-max pooling

pairs.differs: D reframes at 27 framings and reranks with region-wise correlation, whole-grid and enclosed holes; F reranks by stored landmark spots and empty-background busyness with upper/lower half shifts

steps.step: Synthetic 3D-modelled hand renderings per letter (tubes/ellipsoids, hand-set per-letter poses, randomised pose, lighting and background) used as the reference library
steps.note: All six use a procedural tube-and-ellipse hand with per-letter poses (sideways G/H/T, downward P/Q, curved C/O). Library sizes differ: P1 about 69k, P2 24.6k, P3 79.9k, N1 15.4k, N2 18.4k, N3 3,072 poses x 9 stored shifts.

steps.step: Oriented edge maps in 4 orientations (0/45/90/135), pooled on a spatial grid
steps.note: N1 and N3 keep polarity (8 signed types), as P3's 9x9 polarity block does. N2 is polarity-blind with perpendicular suppression, which is closer to P1 and P2.

steps.step: Per-image edge-strength normalisation plus capping or compression of strong edges
steps.note: The programs divide by the image's own max, RMS or mean gradient. The networks standardise brightness globally, then apply a fixed knee or saturation. N2 and N3 also restandardise the edge maps per image. The result is similar but not the same normaliser.

steps.step: Border-reachability or enclosure: how much edge must be crossed to reach the top, left or right border (never the bottom)
steps.note: N3 takes the strongest step along straight rays in 5 directions, excluding down. That matches P2's straight border traces and P1's straight-scan component, but not the curved flood fill in P1 (18 sweeps) or P3 (16 steps).

steps.step: Background brightness predicted from border pixels (row-wise left/right interpolation or a corner-fitted plane), and the departure from it
steps.note: N3 blends the left and right border columns per row with the top corners and scores departure, which is close to P1's row-wise background guess. N2 only removes a left-right gradient estimated from the top corners before using raw darkness.

steps.step: Combined soft hand-likelihood (silhouette) map, pooled to a coarse grid as a descriptor block
steps.note: N3 adds the background-difference and enclosure maps, as P1 and P2 do. N2's silhouette is lighting-corrected negated brightness, not a hand estimate. N1 has no silhouette channel at all.

steps.step: Hand bounding box from the hand map, and a crop fitted to the hand
steps.note: No network localises the hand. All of them match the fixed 28x28 frame.

steps.step: Search over framings: shifts and zoom levels, keeping the best
steps.note: P1 uses 6 crops including zooms, P2 uses 27 framings (3 zooms x 3x3 shifts), P3 uses 9 offsets. The networks search only a 3x3 shift grid (about 2 to 2.7 px), with no zoom. Scale variation is pushed into the rendered references.

steps.step: Fine relief or crease map: smoothed image minus heavily smoothed background, split into lighter and darker
steps.note: N1 measures lighter and darker than a 9x9 smoothed neighbourhood, which matches P3's bright and dark relief. N3 uses a band-pass detail map, like P1's creases and P2's brightness detail.

steps.step: Thin ridge or bar (finger-like line) detector in 4 orientations
steps.note: N2 has oriented bar detectors. N1 has only non-oriented centre-surround spots. N3 has a 'thin parts' picture whose computation on the photo is not described.

steps.step: Outline or profile signature of the silhouette
steps.note: P1 uses shift-invariant Fourier harmonics of row and column width and offset profiles. N3 correlates left, right and top enclosure maps directly, which depends on position and uses no Fourier step.

steps.step: Enclosed-hole detection (background regions not reachable from the border) and hole agreement
steps.note: No network has a hole channel.

steps.step: Down-weighting of the lower (wrist) rows and the side columns
steps.note: N1 uses a top-to-bottom ramp with a reduced bottom row. N3 fades rows below row 8 and the far sides. N2 has no positional weighting, only structure-based weighting.

steps.step: Mean-removed, unit-length descriptor correlated with every reference of every letter
steps.note: This is the shared core: a normalised inner product against the whole library.

steps.step: Local-max tolerance spread (each value mixed with its neighbourhood maximum)
steps.note: P3 mixes each pixel with the max of its 4 neighbours in the landmark maps. N1 takes the 3x3 max. N3 spreads only the hand and background maps, with a distance penalty.

steps.step: Region-wise matching with independent local shifts per region
steps.note: N1's upper and lower halves each take their own best shift, the same as P3's independent upper and lower halves. P2 uses 9 regions. N2 normalises 9 regions separately (as P2 does) but shifts them together. N3 gives palm and finger windows their own offsets.

steps.step: Top-K shortlist per letter followed by a second, finer re-verification of the shortlisted references
steps.note: N2 and N3 add a second comparison, but over all references rather than a shortlist, and not as a finer re-check.

steps.step: Landmark-spot check and empty-background-spot busyness penalty
steps.note: Not present in any network.

steps.step: Per-letter pooling that mixes the best match with the support of several near-best matches
steps.note: The programs use best plus the mean of the top K (6, 6, 4). The networks use maxima within fixed batches or groups of references: N1 sums 8 batch maxima, N2 averages 4 group maxima, N3 takes best plus the mean of 16 group maxima. This is a fixed stand-in for top-K sorting.

steps.step: Letter with the highest score wins
steps.note: Argmax in all six.

network_only.step: Global brightness mean and spread standardisation of the raw image before feature extraction
Mirror padding of 5 px before the local detectors
Centre-surround small bright and dark spot detectors (not oriented)
Reference-side blending of opposite-polarity edges near the hand outline (10 to 30%), so a hand lighter or darker than the background still matches
Per-letter score is the sum of maxima over 8 fixed batches of 80 renderings
Global brightness standardisation of the raw image
Perpendicular-orientation suppression (0.61) of the edge and bar responses
Second, regionally contrast-normalised reference set compared separately and added at 0.6 weight
Quasi-random low-discrepancy sampling of pose parameters, and averaging of maxima over 4 groups of 192
Global brightness standardisation of the raw image
Hand-grown and background-grown maps (8-neighbour max with a distance penalty), matched to thin-part and finger-gap reference pictures
Asymmetric background departure (darker counts 1.0, lighter 0.56)
References stored pre-shifted at 9 offsets instead of shifting at test time

numbers.network_values: N1: +/-1 cell (about 2 px) per upper and lower half; N2: +/-1 cell (2 px) global

numbers.meaning: Fine comparison grid of 14x14 cells, each 2x2 px
numbers.network_values: N1: 14x14 cells of 2x2 px; N3: 14x14 grid of 2x2 cells

numbers.meaning: Positional shift step for the 3x3 framing or offset search
numbers.network_values: N3: +/-2.7 px offsets

numbers.meaning: Background and skin brightness ranges of the rendered references
numbers.network_values: N1: background 0.47 to 0.86, skin 0.37 to 0.61

numbers.meaning: Top-corner patch size used to estimate the left-right background lighting gradient
numbers.network_values: N2: 8x6 px corner patches

numbers.meaning: Zoom factors 0.82 and about 1.21 to 1.23
numbers.network_values: N3: rendering zoom range 0.82 to 1.23

numbers.meaning: Offset count of 9
numbers.program_values: P3: 9 offsets (2 px plus-shape and 1 px diagonals) for landmark checks
numbers.network_values: N3: 9 offsets in a 3x3 grid at +/-2.7 px for whole-hand matching

numbers.meaning: Weight about 0.32 to 0.36 on a detail or thin-line block
numbers.program_values: P1: crease weight 0.32 and thin-line weight 0.355 (against edges 0.76)
numbers.network_values: N3: detail weight 0.32 (against edges 1.0); N2: bar weight 0.36 (against edges 0.64)

numbers.meaning: Value 0.85
numbers.program_values: P3: 85% of block mean removed; P1: 0.85 zoom
numbers.network_values: N1: upper-hand row weight 0.85; N3: spreading penalty 0.85

numbers.meaning: Value 0.82
numbers.program_values: P1: top edge-row weight 0.82; P2: zoom 0.82
numbers.network_values: N1: 0.82 of excess removed; N2: 0.82 x support

numbers.program_values: P1: silhouette weight 0.61; P2: 0.64 brightness-detail weight and orientation fraction; P2: 0.18 hole penalty; P3: 0.18 half-saturation

cover.verdict: The networks share the programs' strategy at the level of a family, but they do not compute the same pipeline. All six correlate oriented-edge, relief and silhouette-like grids against a library of procedurally rendered 3D tube hands, with a small shift search and per-letter pooling of near-best matches. N1 closely follows P3's independent upper and lower half shifting and its bright and dark relief, and N3 recreates the P1/P2 border background model and edge-enclosure hand map with straight rays. What the networks leave out: hand localisation and hand-fitted cropping (P1), any zoom search, the curved flood fill, enclosed holes (P2), shift-invariant outline harmonics (P1), and the top-K shortlist with finer re-verification, including P3's landmark and empty-space checks. They swap top-K sorting for fixed batch or group maxima, and the few hand-chosen numbers they share with the programs are generic (2 px cells, about 2.7 px shifts) rather than signature constants.
